Resolve services inside RunAsync: using Autodesk.Revit.Attributes; using DBTools.Core.Tools.Commands; using DBTools.Core.Tools.Commands.Context; using DBTools.MyTool.Features.Inspection; namespace DBTools.MyTool.App.Composition; [Transaction(TransactionMode.Manual)] public sealed class MyToolCommand : ToolCommand { protected override Task RunAsync(ICommandContext context) { ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(context); return context.Resolve<InspectionWorkflow>().ExecuteAsync(context.Document); } } This example assumes the feature defines InspectionWorkflow.ExecuteAsync(Document). The context exposes UIApplication, UIDocument, Document, Logger, OwnerHandleProvider, ShowBanner, and inherited Resolve<T>(). A documentless command overrides RequiresActiveDocument=false. Accessing its Document or UIDocument throws. Every ToolCommand implements IExternalCommandAvailability. Set availabilityType to the concrete command. The default predicate requires an open document unless RequiresActiveDocument is false. Override IsCommandAvailableCore for other predicates and use CommandAvailability methods such as HasActiveView, HasSelection, or HasStructuralFramingSelection. Use the scoped ITransactionRunner for model changes. Its callbacks are synchronous, even though the entrypoint returns a Task. A modeless command uses the queued run profile and an owned session. See Modularity for call-gate, transaction, logging, and session contracts. 6. Add views, settings, and hooks A tool view embeds a stable element such as Grid. It has no x:Class, code-behind, tool CLR namespace, or event attributes. Presentation supplies the window shell. Core's ToolWindowFactory installs runtime services and registers its session. See Tool-window sessions. Use ObservableObject, [ObservableProperty], and [RelayCommand] from CommunityToolkit.Mvvm for bindable state and commands. Match the ViewModel's folder and namespace. Keep design-time ViewModels independent of Revit and production services. Sandbox Integration describes resource names, manifest declarations, visibility, and preview construction. For persisted options, define a DTO and a source-generated JSON context. Register one SettingsSection<T> and read it through ISettingsProvider. A settings pack adds the editor context and view. Settings Packs contains the complete registration and persistence sequence. For view-change work, register an IViewActivationTask service. For owned event subscriptions, implement IHookLifecycle and register the concrete service and hook mapping. Hooks describes admission, failure handling, rollback, and synchronous shutdown. Feature Warnings describes configuration failures that disable commands. 7. Add tests and validate Tests live under the owning Tests/ directory and mirror production ownership: Tests/ ├── Features/Inspection/InspectionWorkflowTests.cs ├── Integration/Revit/Features/Inspection/InspectionWorkflowHostedTests.cs ├── Support/ ├── DBTools.MyTool.Pure.Tests.csproj └── DBTools.MyTool.Local.Tests.csproj Pure projects compile plain NUnit tests against the tool project. Local projects use explicit positive compile membership for [RevitLocal] fixtures and their support. A DA project claims coverage only through real APS WorkItem tests. Optional *.Portable.Pure.Tests projects exercise portable production targets on Linux. Keep the execution projects separate. Use focused commands during development: ./test.sh list --tool GM --scope pure --fixture DuplicateDetectionEngineTests ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure --fixture DuplicateDetectionEngineTests ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects DBTools.GM.Local.Tests -y 2026 Replace GM with the new tool's directory key after its test projects exist. See Testing Tools for execution hosts and routing. Run the new tool's Pure fixtures through test.sh. Use Revit-hosted tests for ribbon composition and commands that need the Revit API. Use Windows Pure fixtures for WPF bindings, themes, and window cleanup. See Testing Tools for selection and execution commands.

developer-guide/developing/sandbox-integ.title: Sandbox Integration | DB Tools
developer-guide/developing/sandbox-integ.summary: Sandbox Integration Sandbox previews tool windows and validates a staged distribution without starting Revit. Native validation runs on Windows and constructs real WPF windows. Run one fresh Sandbox process for each candidate year. Use this page to register a preview, build Sandbox, and run it on Windows. See Sandbox Validator for candidate loading, assembly boundaries, and the validation sequence. Portable build validation checks metadata, raw XAML, and Dev Mode policy on Linux. Native WPF validation and live Dev Mode injection require Windows. Register a window Declare a raw view in the tool's manifest.yml: sandboxWindows: - id: DBTools.MyTool.Main displayName: "My Tool" group: "Common" xamlResource: "DBTools.ToolViews.MyTool.MyToolWindow.xaml" windowKind: Modal width: 1200 height: 700 minWidth: 900 minHeight: 500 startupLocation: CenterScreen designTimeViewModelType: "DBTools.MyTool.App.DesignTime.MyToolWindowDesignTimeViewModel" designTimeViewModelAssembly: "DBTools.MyTool" designTimeViewModelVisibility: Public Embed the matching resource in the owning tool project: <EmbeddedResource Include="App\Views\MyToolWindow.xaml" LogicalName="DBTools.ToolViews.MyTool.MyToolWindow.xaml" /> Field Requirement and meaning id Required stable window identity. displayName Required catalog/window title. group Required catalog group. assembly Optional raw-view assembly override. Otherwise the tool's manifest owner. xamlResource Required exact embedded logical resource name. windowKind Modal by default, or Modeless. designTimeViewModelType Required fully qualified design-time type. designTimeViewModelAssembly Required simple assembly name. designTimeViewModelVisibility Required Public or Internal, matching the type. width, height, minWidth, minHeight Optional finite dimensions. Width/height must be positive. Minimum sizes may be zero. showInTaskbar Optional Boolean. Defaults to false. startupLocation Optional WPF startup location. Defaults to CenterOwner. titleBindingPath, titleStringFormat Optional title binding and format. The parser rejects unknown fields and blank required values. Use exact enum spellings. Multiple entries can share a design-time type while using different stable IDs and raw resources. The manifest owns this metadata. Sandbox does not infer a Window type from a filename. Raw views and runtime ownership Use a stable root such as Grid. Raw views have no Window root, x:Class, code-behind, event attributes, tool CLR namespaces, payload pack URIs, payload BAML, or implicit templates for tool types. Bind visible text, headers, items, and tooltips explicitly. Use explicit templates, selectors, and display paths for bound content. Use tool-window sessions to open the same raw view in the product. Settings pack views supplied by pack factories are a separate embedded editor surface. Design-time ViewModels A Public type needs a public parameterless constructor. An Internal type must be non-public and have a public or non-public parameterless constructor. The manifest must select the matching visibility. The type must be constructible. Keep construction independent of Revit documents, external events, network services, and production settings. namespace DBTools.MyTool.App.DesignTime; public sealed class MyToolWindowDesignTimeViewModel { public string Title => "My Tool"; public IReadOnlyList<string> Rows { get; } = new[] { "Example", "Preview" }; } Populate the ViewModel with sample state and commands. A display-only action can use NoOpCommand from DBTools.Core.UI.Commanding.DesignTime.NoOp. Use Global Mapper (GM) and Super Girt Tool (SGT) manifests under src/Tools/ as examples of raw-view and design-time ViewModel registration. Build and run Build a product candidate and Sandbox: ./build.sh AssembleDistributionCandidate -y 2026 ./build.sh BuildSandbox -y 2026 Candidate assembly can compile edited source. Acceptance targets require a clean committed tree. Read the build output for its build ID and use that invocation's candidate directory: .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/distribution-candidate/Release/2026/ .artifacts/sandbox/Release/2026/net10.0-windows/ Run Sandbox on Windows with the matching Revit year installed. Both modes resolve that installation, require its runtime files, and check metadata/runtime compatibility. Run these commands from the repository root: dotnet run --project src/DBTools.Sandbox/DBTools.Sandbox.csproj -p:RevitYear=2026 -- --dist-dir .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/distribution-candidate/Release/2026 Replace <build-id> with the ID printed by the candidate build. To validate without the interactive catalog, add headless mode and the matching installed Revit reference directory: dotnet run --project src/DBTools.Sandbox/DBTools.Sandbox.csproj -p:RevitYear=2026 -- --headless --dist-dir .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/distribution-candidate/Release/2026 --revit-reference-dir 'C:\Program Files\Autodesk\Revit 2026' These are native Windows commands. Daemon-routed acceptance uses its hidden desktop. See Testing Tools for routing. Options Sandbox [--dist-dir PATH] [--headless --revit-reference-dir PATH] Option Default and behavior --dist-dir PATH .artifacts/dist/Release. Accept a year directory or a root containing supported year directories. --headless Disabled. Run native validation without the interactive catalog. --revit-reference-dir PATH Required with --headless. Invalid without it. Both path options also accept --name=value. Blank values and unknown arguments fail. A distribution root selects the newest supported year containing DBTools.dll. It does not reject a root merely because both years are present. Use an explicit year directory to select 2026 when 2027 also exists. A missing candidate fails before WPF startup. Headless mode suppresses interactive UI but still creates native WPF windows, checks layout and bindings, exercises supported interactions, and closes owned windows. It requires Windows Desktop. It is not a Linux metadata-only mode. Package native validation inputs Run PackageSandboxValidationInput to package the current candidate and Sandbox for Windows distribution acceptance: ./build.sh PackageSandboxValidationInput This target requires a clean committed source tree and every supported year. Sandbox output and archive paths include the year: .artifacts/sandbox/<configuration>/<year>/<tfm>/ sandbox/<year>/<sanitized-tfm>/ Use the archive with the distribution acceptance command. For validation checks, failure handling, and the distinction between portable, native, and live Dev Mode validation, see Sandbox Validator. Troubleshooting Failure Action Missing view resource Match xamlResource to the owning project's LogicalName. ViewModel construction failure Check assembly/type names, declared visibility, and parameterless constructor access. Binding errors Read binding-listener output and supply explicit display bindings. Candidate file/identity mismatch Rebuild the selected candidate and inspect its recursive file set. Wrong candidate year Pass an explicit year directory rather than the distribution root. Reference mismatch Supply matching installed-year Revit references in headless mode. Cleanup failure Inspect the window/session cleanup failure before terminating the process. See Sandbox Validator, Assembly Loading, and Creating New Tools.

developer-guide/developing/settings-pack.title: Settings Packs | DB Tools
developer-guide/developing/settings-pack.summary: Settings Packs A settings pack supplies a tool's editor in the DB Tools Settings window. It binds a typed settings section, an editor context, a WPF view, and optional warnings. Packs appear as cards grouped by their registered ribbon panel. ISettingsProvider reads current settings and commits section batches. SettingsWindowViewModel owns Save and Reset through SettingsPersistenceWorkflow. Pack contexts edit state and validate it. They do not save independently. Files and typed sections The default user file is %APPDATA%/DBTools/settings.<year>.json. AppPaths.SettingsFile requires an initialized Revit year. The process can relocate its base directory through the DBTools.AppPaths.BaseDir AppContext value. SettingsSectionReader reads appsettings.json from its base directory, then overlays the user file. An absolute user path is used directly. A relative one resolves against the base directory. The reader validates files at construction and reads both layers again on every Get. It retains no file watchers or open handles. A section is one JSON property, such as Tools.FoundationTags. Its name must be nonblank and cannot contain :. It is not a nested configuration path. Section and property lookup is case-insensitive. { "Tools.MyTool": { "AutoUpdateEnabled": true, "FamilyPattern": "^Example$" } } Register generated System.Text.Json metadata with the section as JsonTypeInfo<T>. The same metadata reads options and serializes writes: using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using DBTools.Core.Settings.Domain; namespace DBTools.MyTool.Settings; public sealed class MyToolSettings : IAutoUpdateSettings { public bool AutoUpdateEnabled { get; set; } = true; public string FamilyPattern { get; set; } = "^Example$"; } Place its JSON context in a separate matching file: using System.Text.Json.Serialization; namespace DBTools.MyTool.Settings; [JsonSerializable(typeof(MyToolSettings))] internal partial class MyToolSettingsJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext { } IAutoUpdateSettings requires only AutoUpdateEnabled. HasWarning belongs to editor/session state and must not be added as a persisted warning flag. Keep DTO graphs independent of Revit and UI state. The allowed leaf types are bool, string, and double. Nullable values, collections, dictionaries, and nested DTOs must resolve to those leaf types. Add-in enums and custom TypeConverter/JsonConverter implementations are not supported settings types. Use settable properties with initialized defaults so missing keys retain those defaults. Pure and Revit-hosted test executables disable reflection-based JSON serialization. Read semantics and failures The reader recursively overlays objects and merges arrays by index. A shorter override array retains the default array's remaining elements. A later scalar or null does not replace an earlier object or array. A different container kind replaces the earlier container. Normalization preserves scalar conversions for strings, Booleans, and doubles. String nulls become empty strings. Boolean and double values parse from scalar text. Doubles use invariant culture. Invalid values fail the section read. Missing sections return a new settings instance. Only a missing file or parent directory means absent configuration. Invalid JSON, a non-object root, access faults, and a directory at a file path remain errors. Comments and trailing commas are accepted. Commits preserve unrelated sections but do not retain comments. Manifest declaration Declare the persistence key and pack metadata in manifest.yml: id: DBTools.MyTool assembly: DBTools.MyTool moduleType: DBTools.MyTool.App.Composition.MyToolToolModule order: 0 panel: Common tool: settings: configSection: Tools.MyTool settingsPacks: - key: common.my_tool title: "My Tool" warnings: - id: core.my_tool.configuration title: "My Tool Configuration Invalid" message: "Correct the family pattern and save settings." disableTools: - DBTools.MyTool configSection names the JSON property. Pack key and warning id are unique catalog identities. They do not have to equal that property. Existing keys use forms such as structural.foundation_tags and core.structural.combined_tags. Each warning requires id, title, and message. disableTools is optional. See Feature Warnings for activation and command blocking. The module's panel supplies the pack's group through GetRequiredPanel(): Value Settings group Settings DB Tools Settings Common DB Tools Common Structural DB Tools Structural Testing DB Tools Testing Services DB Tools Services Registration Register the typed section in ToolModule.RegisterSettings: public override void RegisterSettings(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { services.AddSingleton(new SettingsSection<MyToolSettings>( manifest.GetRequiredConfigSection(), MyToolSettingsJsonContext.Default.MyToolSettings)); } Register the editor in RegisterSettingsPacks. The following excerpt assumes SettingsPackContext implements ISettingsPackContext<MyToolSettings>, accepts a warning ID, and exposes HasWarning. MyToolSettingsView is the tool-owned pack view: public override void RegisterSettingsPacks(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { var section = new SettingsSection<MyToolSettings>( manifest.GetRequiredConfigSection(), MyToolSettingsJsonContext.Default.MyToolSettings); var pack = manifest.GetSingleSettingsPack(); var warning = pack.GetSingleWarning(manifest.Id); services.AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition<MyToolSettings, SettingsPackContext>( new SettingsPackRegistration<MyToolSettings, SettingsPackContext> { SettingsSection = section, PackKey = pack.Key, PackTitle = pack.Title, RibbonPanel = manifest.GetRequiredPanel(), ApplyBehavior = SettingsPackApplyBehavior.NextToolRun, ContextFactory = (_, input) => new SettingsPackContext(input.RequireWarningId()), ViewFactory = context => new MyToolSettingsView { DataContext = context }, Warning = new SettingsPackWarningRegistration<SettingsPackContext> { Id = warning.Id, Title = warning.Title, Message = warning.Message, ToolInternalNamesToDisable = warning.DisableTools, FlagGetter = context => context.HasWarning, FlagSetter = (context, active) => context.HasWarning = active } }); } These APIs live under DBTools.Core.Settings.Composition, .Persistence, .SettingsPack, and .Warnings. Manifest extension methods live under DBTools.Core.Tools.Manifest. Use the tool's real namespaces for its context, view, and DTO. SettingsSection, pack key/title/panel, and context/view factories are required registration members. When present, a warning requires its ID, title, message, and flag getter/setter. AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition also checks strings and delegates at runtime. ApplyBehavior defaults to Immediate. Set it explicitly when values apply at the next tool run or require a restart. Apply timing Value Meaning Immediate Saved values apply immediately, such as ribbon visibility flags. NextToolRun Commands or view-activation tasks read saved values on their next run. RequiresRestart The pack documents a specific restart requirement. Do not show a blanket restart warning for all settings. Read settings at the operation boundary so saved changes reach the next operation. Runtime and context ownership ISettingsPackDefinition supplies catalog metadata and creates one ISettingsPackRuntime for an editor row. That runtime binds the exact context, typed section, lazy view factory, staged writes, and warning delegates. Callers cannot pair an unrelated context with a warning definition. SettingsPackCollection carries SettingsPackHostContext from the window factory into runtime creation. Use SettingsPackHostContext.Empty without a host or FromApplication(application) with one. A context extracts the typed application through TryGetApplication<TApplication>(). Initialize bindable state in constructors. Perform model changes through explicit editor actions. Elevation Tags uses host data for preview snapshots and accepts no active document as an empty preview. Combined Foundation Tags uses explicit Refresh, Clear Warning, and Install/Repair actions for prerequisite work. It reports that an action is unavailable when it needs an active document. Context interfaces The editor implements these base contracts: public interface ISettingsPackContext { Task<SettingsValidationResult> ValidateAsync(CancellationToken ct = default); } public interface ISettingsPackContext<TOptions> : ISettingsPackContext { void Load(TOptions options); TOptions BuildOptionsSnapshot(); } Optional contracts add specific behavior: Interface Responsibility ISettingsStateContext Raise StateChanged for editable-state changes. IPendingChangesContext Expose HasPendingChanges. IOwnerAwareContext Receive an owner handle provider for dialogs. ISettingsPackSaveState<TOptions> Accept MarkSaved(committedOptions) as the persisted baseline. ISettingsWarningContext Identify the warning that validation evaluates. ISettingsPackSaveValidation Expose BlockSaveOnInvalid to refuse invalid drafts. IWarningFixProvider Supply a matching warning's Fix action and label. SettingsValidationResult.Success is a property. Use SettingsValidationResult.FromErrors(...) for invalid values. Exceptions mean validation failed to run. They are not an invalid-result substitute. Honor cancellation and return messages that identify the invalid value and its correction. Auto-update editor base SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<TOptions> in DBTools.Core.Settings.SettingsPack.AutoUpdate implements the common toggle editor. It owns title/description/tooltip text, AutoUpdateEnabled, HasWarning, ToggleEnabled, ClearWarningCommand, WarningId, pending-change tracking, StateChanged, and the validation envelope. It blocks saving invalid options. The protected base constructor supplies warning identity and editor text: protected SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext( string warningId, string title, string description, string toggleToolTip); Derived contexts implement: protected abstract void LoadCore(TOptions options); protected abstract void CollectValidationErrors(List<string> errors); protected abstract bool SettingsEqual(TOptions left, TOptions right); public abstract TOptions BuildOptionsSnapshot(); Load applies the toggle, clears the context warning, calls LoadCore, and notifies state changes. LoadCore sets a baseline through SetBaseline. MarkSaved uses the exact committed options, not the latest editable snapshot. Edits made while a commit is pending therefore remain dirty. Elevation Tags and Joist Girder Weights use this base. Combined Foundation Tags implements the interfaces directly because its prerequisite state and repair actions need a different context. Regex pattern lists RegexPatternListContext owns bindable RegexPatternEntry rows, add/remove commands, a configured maximum, empty-list default seeding, snapshots that omit blank rows, and state-change events. Load takes at most the configured maximum. Removal retains at least one row. Tool contexts retain their binding property names and validation rules. Elevation Tags and Combined Foundation Tags use the shared list mechanics with at most three rows per pattern list. Do not copy those mechanics into a new context. Joist Girder Weights uses individual FamilyNamePattern, DeadLoadPattern, LiveLoadPattern, and TotalLoadPattern strings rather than pattern lists. Tool settings examples Combined Foundation Tags persists TagFamilyPatterns, PierFamilyPatterns, and FootingFamilyPatterns. Empty lists select these tool defaults: TagFamilyPatterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ PierFamilyPatterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ FootingFamilyPatterns ^(?:Footing|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Elevation Tags uses TagNamePatterns with default ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$, plus TypeOffsets keyed by spot-elevation type name. Joist Girder Weights supplies these defaults for blank individual patterns: FamilyNamePattern ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ DeadLoadPattern (?:^DL$|Dead\s*Load) LiveLoadPattern (?:^LL$|Live\s*Load) TotalLoadPattern (?:Point\s*Load|Total\s*Load) Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) uses LibraryOptions, which contains a Files list of LibraryFile values. Its pack owns file selection, validation, and pending changes. Read each tool's DTO and generated JSON context when extending it. Runtime reads and programmatic writes ISettingsProvider exposes typed reads and heterogeneous batch writes: TSettings Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings> section) where TSettings : class, new(); Task CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default); Inject the provider and typed section. Read once per operation, then pass that snapshot to the work: var current = settingsProvider.Get(section); if (!current.AutoUpdateEnabled) return; For view-activated updates, ViewActivationTask<TSettings> reads once during admission and captures the snapshot in the admission. It checks session warnings separately. See Hooks. A programmatic write uses the same typed metadata: var current = settingsProvider.Get(section); current.AutoUpdateEnabled = true; await settingsProvider.CommitAsync(new[] { section.CreateWrite(current) }, ct); Batch related section changes in one CommitAsync. A direct commit persists options. The Settings workflow additionally applies flags, baselines, and warning publication. Save and reset sequence SettingsWindowFactory opens the raw DBTools.Presentation.Settings.Views.SettingsWindow.xaml resource through ToolWindowFactory. The registered modal session owns the window, error boundary, owner, handlers, and cleanup. Packs remain separate tool-owned views. SettingsPackViewModel owns one bound runtime, lazy view creation, pending changes, reset state, owner propagation, warning projection, and disposal. SettingsPanelBlock groups rows. SettingsWindowViewModel delegates persistence to SettingsPersistenceWorkflow under Settings/ViewModels. Save proceeds in this order: Evaluate the unsaved drafts. A blocking invalid result stops the save. This pass can update editor warning flags but does not change command blocking. Capture current pack writes and the flags snapshot. Commit the complete batch with one file swap. Mark each pack saved against its exact committed options. Apply committed flags. Validate saved settings in fresh warning-aware runtimes. Project and publish warning decisions to the ribbon and Settings UI. The Validate button diagnoses draft values. It does not publish the draft as saved warning state. Opening Settings validates loaded options. Startup checks warning-aware packs without constructing their views. See Feature Warnings. A validation or writer failure before publication leaves the settings file and saved baselines unchanged. A failure after the swap becomes SettingsPostCommitException, which identifies the operation and phase. Persisted values remain the saved baseline and the window stays open. Concurrent edits remain pending against that baseline. Reset All commits default flags and every pack's default snapshot. It attempts to apply all committed defaults before warning validation and aggregates application failures. A pack reset commits only that pack. Both actions ask for confirmation and use the normal warning/feedback path. Cancel preserves current state and feedback. Choosing Reset Settings in the load-problem alert already confirms the reset, so it does not prompt twice. Atomic persistence SettingsSectionWriter performs these steps: Reject an empty batch, null entries, and case-insensitive duplicate section names. Serialize calls on the writer instance and acquire the sibling settings.<year>.json.lock file exclusively. Re-read the current document under that lock. Replace only the supplied sections. Serialize with each section's generated metadata into one document. Write a .<guid>.tmp file in the same directory and publish it with File.Move(source, destination, overwrite: true). Attempt staged-file cleanup on success, failure, and cancellation. A competing process can hold the lock for up to 10 seconds before the writer fails with IOException. Cancellation while waiting leaves the file unchanged. The OS releases the lock on handle close or process exit. The empty lock file persists and does not indicate a live lock. TextFileIO.s_publicationGate serializes file publication process-wide across writer instances. The writer's own semaphore serializes its commits, while the sibling lock file coordinates separate processes. TextFileIO allows at most six publication attempts for transient sharing, locking, and access-denied failures. It refuses known read-only destinations immediately and surfaces publication access denial as IOException with the original cause. Cleanup does not replace the primary failure. No backup file is retained. Same-year Revit processes share this file. Re-reading under the cross-process lock preserves other sections published by the previous writer. A case-variant section name replaces that section in place. An absent file starts an empty object. An existing empty, whitespace-only, malformed, or non-object file is corrupt and is not silently reset. Editor views Create a tool-owned view for the editor. Bind the auto-update toggle to AutoUpdateEnabled and ToggleEnabled. Bind regex row editors to their explicit properties and commands. Pack views created by ViewFactory are embedded editors. See Modularity for top-level tool-window resources. See Testing Tools for execution commands and Feature Warnings for warning publication and Fix actions.

developer-guide/developing/testing-tools.title: Testing Tools | DB Tools
developer-guide/developing/testing-tools.summary: Testing Tools Use test.sh to select, build, and execute repository tests. Use build.sh on Linux/WSL or build.ps1 on Windows to compile product and test graphs. Static discovery and request validation do not execute tests. Run commands from the repository root. Pure tests run without Revit. Revit-hosted tests use the local scope. Design Automation tests use the da scope and execute real APS WorkItems. Execution hosts Tool keys in the examples include Global Mapper (GM) and Super Girt Tool (SGT). Choose the scope for the behavior you need to test: Scope Host pure NUnit/VSTest without Revit. Most tool, App, and Core projects require Windows, including WPF fixtures. *.Portable.Pure.Tests projects run on Linux. local Revit-hosted tests on a daemon worker, marked [RevitLocal]. da Design Automation tests using real APS WorkItems, marked [RevitDA]. BUILD includes Linux-native contract tests and Windows Sandbox Pure tests. DIST selects Windows distribution acceptance and requires the daemon. Daemon runs use a hidden desktop. Windows Pure tests can also run locally on Windows with the required runtimes installed. See Test Pipeline for project membership, routing, staged inputs, and daemon adapter design. Build and validation commands ./build.sh [Target] [parameters] pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 [Target] [parameters] Both wrappers map options to build/Build.proj and acquire the SDK pinned in global.json. Native Windows uses PowerShell. build.sh refuses that host. Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027 use net10.0-windows. Year selection chooses references and output placement. Build targets Target Behavior BuildAll Default wrapper target. Build, validate, and promote the Release distribution. Compile no test projects. BuildApp Build product outputs for the selected years. ValidatePrePush Build App outputs and validate manifest type references. BuildTests Compile all test graphs. Execute no tests. BuildSelectedPureTests Compile the selected Pure projects. BuildSelectedLocalTests Compile the selected hosted projects without launching Revit. BuildSelectedDesignAutomationTests Compile selected DA projects. AssembleDistributionCandidate Assemble product files and candidate metadata. StagePortableAcceptanceInput Stage the candidate and references for portable acceptance. ValidateDistributionCandidate Run candidate metadata and static Dev Mode policy validation. PromoteToDist Publish the current accepted candidate to the distribution tree. ValidateManifestTypes Check manifest types against compiled output. VerifyArtifacts Check the built product files. BuildSandbox Compile the standalone Windows Sandbox for the selected years. BuildValidationRunner Build the portable .NET 10 Dev Mode policy worker. PackageSandboxValidationInput Package candidate and Sandbox for native Windows validation. BuildBundle, BuildInstaller Package a promoted distribution, or consume --candidate-dist. Restore, Clean, Info Restore required graphs, clean build state, or print configuration. Acceptance targets require a clean committed source tree and both supported years. Leave the year filter unset for BuildAll, portable acceptance, and Sandbox validation packaging. Focused product/test builds and candidate assembly support normal edited-source development. BuildAll validates metadata and static Dev Mode policy on Linux. It does not run native Sandbox, WPF interactions, Revit, or live Dev Mode injection. Build parameters Parameter Default and meaning --Configuration CONFIG Release or Debug. Default Release. -d or --debug selects Debug. --Years YEARS, -y, --year All supported years for builds. Accept one year or a space/comma-separated list. --SkipClean BOOL true. --clean selects false. --Verbose [BOOL], -v false. Bare flag selects true. -q/--quiet selects false. --DryRun [BOOL] false. Bare flag selects true. --TestProjects A,B Required for selected test targets. Use exact project filename stems without .csproj. --CandidateDistributionPath DIR, --candidate-dist DIR Package an already-promoted distribution without rebuilding or promoting it. --InnoSetupExe PATH Override installer compiler discovery. --Revit2026Dir DIR, --Revit2027Dir DIR Override installed Revit reference directories. Full option names ignore case and dashes. Boolean values must be true or false. Selected test graph targets reject --clean and --DryRun. Read the complete reference with ./build.sh --help or pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 --help. ./build.sh BuildApp -y 2026 ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects DBTools.GM.Local.Tests -y 2026 ./build.sh BuildSelectedPureTests --TestProjects DBTools.GM.Pure.Tests ./build.sh BuildTests Build logs and child binlogs live under .artifacts/build/<build-id>/. console.log contains detailed output even when the terminal is quiet. .artifacts/build/console.log copies the latest invocation's log. A completed marker records the invocation's end. Selected test graphs also write .artifacts/build/test-matrix.binlog. Source checks Check source placement and generated maps separately from compilation: python3 .agents/work/canon_source_maps.py --check python3 .agents/work/canon_source_fidelity.py --gate --mechanical-root testing --mechanical-root build .githooks/pre-push Regenerate maps with python3 .agents/work/canon_source_maps.py after source moves. See Build Pipeline for distribution acceptance, Dev Mode preflight, and build-server configuration. test.sh command reference ./test.sh <verb> [options] Verb Action build Delegate remaining arguments to build.sh. test Build selected current artifacts, freeze them, then execute. list Statically list tests or projects without execution. validate-request Resolve and validate selectors/projects without test execution or submission. submit Build and submit Local hosted tests. Reject Pure and DA. rerun --request ID Replay failures from a previous daemon request's submitted bytes. The default scope is pure. Without tool selection, discover owners for the requested scopes. Local execution, including compile-only, requires an explicit year or DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS. Pure-only requests are year-free and reject --year/--years. DA uses 2026. Selectors and build options Option Meaning --tool TOOL[,TOOL] Tool directory keys, case-insensitive, or BUILD, APP, CORE, DA-SENTINEL, DIST. --scope SCOPE[,SCOPE] pure, local, da, or all. --project PATH[,PATH] test, validate-request, or list only. Repeatable repository-relative project paths with forward slashes. Intersect other selectors. --fixture NAME Repeatable exact fixture/class selector. Narrow compilation to owning projects. -f FILTER, --filter FILTER VSTest filter locally. Supported exact/prefix FQN translation for daemon jobs. --fqn FQN Repeatable exact test identity. -y YEAR, --year YEAR Repeatable hosted year. --years 2026,2027 Hosted years as CSV. --changed-since REV test only: select affected owners. Unknown inputs select all. --compile-only, --build-only test only: compile and record inputs without executing tests. --no-build Strictly consume matching prepared artifacts. Available with test, submit, and validate-request. --projects list only: sorted scope<TAB>project.csproj rows, including empty projects. --summary Summarize static method counts by project. Cannot combine with --projects. --request ID Previous daemon request for rerun. Choose exactly one selector form: fixtures, filter, or FQNs. Fixture names select exact classes rather than similarly named longer classes. A fixture narrows the requested scopes to those that own it. An ambiguous short fixture name fails with exit 2. Use its namespace-qualified name or an explicit tool. Without --tool, the wrapper infers ownership from --filter, --fqn, or --fixture. Ambiguous filter/FQN matches across tools fail with exit 2. Resolved fixtures can select several owners. Without a usable inferred owner, the request retains the owners selected by its other options. Source discovery handles qualified attributes, combined/separate attribute lists, and implicit NUnit fixtures. Static method counts do not expand parameterized cases and are not runtime pass counts. list narrows fixture ownership to projects, then lists those projects' indexed methods. It does not apply the runtime fixture/filter expression to each printed method. Unknown project paths, paths outside the selected tool/scope, invalid selector combinations, and empty required selections fail with exit 2. There is no arbitrary dotnet argument passthrough after --. The APP Pure selection is DBTools.App.Pure.Tests. APP Local also includes DBTools.App.HostedTurns.Local.Tests. CORE selects both Windows and portable Pure projects, or both Core Local and HostedTurns Local projects. SGT Pure selects its Windows and portable projects. Tool project selection follows the actual Tests/ projects rather than a hard-coded fixture list. Daemon options Option Meaning --relay URL Override DBTOOLS_DAEMON_RELAY_URL. --machine MACHINE Explicit diagnostic machine pin. Ordinary hosted requests use automatic selection. --headers-env NAME Name of an environment variable containing relay headers JSON. --header 'Name: Value' Repeatable explicit header. Keep credentials out of command history. --label LABEL Job label. --queue-timeout HH:MM:SS Bound queue/claim wait, including the hosted Revit lease. --execution-timeout HH:MM:SS Bound execution after lease acquisition. --isolation MODE Hosted isolation mode. Invalid for Pure-only requests. --keep-open Request that hosted Revit remain open. Invalid for Pure-only requests. --result-json PATH Write daemon terminal evidence. Local-only Pure runs remove this path and use TRX counts. --include PATH Repeatable extra file/directory to stage. The wrapper forwards queue and execution timeouts independently. It supplies no single --timeout option or local default for either value. Hosting behavior belongs to the daemon. The wrapper accepts --keep-open. Execution remains subject to the worker's lifecycle policy. Compile-only rejects daemon execution options, includes, and result reports. --no-build cannot combine with compile-only. DA-only execution rejects daemon options, and --result-json is invalid with DA. A DA-only year selection accepts only 2026. A combined request must include 2026. Environment controls include: Variable Default/use DBT_PURE_CONCURRENCY 2 concurrent daemon Pure submissions. DBT_MSBUILD_MAX_CPU_COUNT 2 graph build workers. DBT_BUILD_SERVERS 1 for wrapper-owned scoped servers. 0 disables them. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_RELAY_URL Configured relay endpoint. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_MACHINE_ID Hosted machine pin when supplied. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS Local years when argv supplies none. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_CLI CLI executable override. Default dbtools-daemon-cli. The wrapper does not persist authentication tokens. Relay authentication belongs to daemon configuration. Distribution acceptance DIST is a closed acceptance command, not an ordinary tool suite. It requires test --tool DIST --scope pure, automatic machine selection, and the exact filter FullyQualifiedName=DBTools.Distribution.Windows.Tests.WindowsAcceptanceTests.ValidatesTheStagedCandidate. Supply --result-json and exactly one --include file named validate-dist-<64 lowercase hex digits>.zip. The archive contains the complete candidate, references, and Sandbox payload. Other tools, fixture selectors, explicit machine pins, and arbitrary include files are rejected. Build the archive with PackageSandboxValidationInput. The acceptance test validates it before launching a fresh Sandbox for every supported year. Its compile-only selection builds the test graph without requiring an archive or executing acceptance. Discovery and examples These commands inspect selections without submitting tests: ./test.sh --help ./test.sh list --tool GM --scope pure --fixture DuplicateDetectionEngineTests ./test.sh list --tool APP,CORE --scope local --projects ./test.sh list --tool GM,SGT --scope pure --summary ./test.sh validate-request --tool GM --scope pure --fixture DuplicateDetectionEngineTests Local validate-request checks CLI availability, a selected year, selector translation, and model metadata. It does not require or validate a relay URL, connect to the relay, or submit a job: ./test.sh validate-request --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 \ --queue-timeout 00:05:00 --execution-timeout 00:30:00 Run tests with: ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure --fixture DuplicateDetectionEngineTests ./test.sh test --tool GM,RecordSet --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local --years 2026,2027 Do not use --scope all as a routine catch-all: it includes the credentialed APS scope and requests each selected owner's corresponding projects. Use explicit scopes and the smallest relevant fixture while iterating. BUILD selects two Linux-native contract projects and Sandbox's Windows Pure project. To run only the Linux-native projects: ./test.sh test --tool BUILD --scope pure \ --project testing/DBTools.Build.Tests/DBTools.Build.Tests.csproj,testing/DBTools.Distribution.Tests/DBTools.Distribution.Tests.csproj On Windows, Linux-native BUILD projects and *.Portable.Pure.Tests are skipped before compilation with a notice. Explicitly selecting only native projects fails. A changed-owner request with no runnable Windows projects and no explicit project selection skips with a notice. DIST remains daemon-routed on every OS. Reuse compiled tests Compile the selection, then execute its prepared artifacts: ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 --compile-only ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 --no-build --no-build requires the same selected projects, source content, and output bytes. Run normal test again when the record is missing or stale. rerun replays failures from a previous daemon request's submitted bytes: ./test.sh rerun --request REQUEST_ID Prepared records are stored under .artifacts/tests/build-record-<lane>-<year>-<selection>.json. Use rerun to reproduce a submitted failure. Use normal test to test edited source. See Test Pipeline for prepared records, frozen inputs, and CI artifact transfer. Daemon adapter entry projects Developer adapter entries under testing/Daemon/Pure/ and testing/Daemon/Hosted/ also expose VSTest discovery and execution. The vendored adapter version is pinned in testing/Daemon/Directory.Build.props. Entry.targets checks both vendored and restored package SHA-256 values before dotnet test. IDE runners and vstest.console do not execute that pin check. Hosted entries generate per-year Sources, Models, and Includes. Hosted source assemblies are NUnit libraries loaded in Revit. Pure sources retain the test SDK for separate VSTest testhosts. Generated runsettings derive RequiresInteractiveDesktop from selected Pure assemblies. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REQUIRES_INTERACTIVE_DESKTOP can override that setting, subject to the daemon's hidden-desktop requirement. Select a Hosted entry and a year, or a Pure entry and filter, through dotnet test: # Discover hosted tests without submission. dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/VTC.Hosted.Entry.csproj --list-tests # Execute one hosted fixture against Revit 2026. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS=2026 dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/VTC.Hosted.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CategoryTabClassifierTests" # Execute a Windows Pure fixture through the adapter. dotnet test testing/Daemon/Pure/GM.Pure.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DuplicateDetectionEngineTests" Use one execution route for a run. Test Pipeline describes how the entries are built. Test project setup Create test projects beneath the production owner's Tests/ directory. Follow Test Pipeline for project properties, source membership, portable targets, and runtime dependencies. Map each testing/**/*.cs path to "test" in .desloppify/config.json zone_overrides. Update the entries when adding, deleting, or renaming a file. Check those entries with: python3 .agents/checks/integrity.py --structure-only TestSupport and fixture inputs testing/TestSupport contains source-linked shared helpers, not replacement product behavior: Directory Purpose Execution/ [RevitLocal] and [RevitDA] attributes in DBTools.Tests.Shared.Execution. Paths/ Repository lookup, staged model paths, and installed family-template resolution. Logging/ NUnit output bridge and explicit App-path initialization. Fakes/ Recording notifiers/loggers/overlays and inline boundary helpers. Revit/ Ambient Revit host and document leases. Wpf/ Bounded dispatcher pumps, fault scopes, binding capture, and modal protection. Settings/ Isolated settings data and generated metadata. GM/ Shared GM construction, assertions, external doubles, and Local harness support. For example, RecordingErrorNotifier exposes banner counts, title/message, and AllBanners. RecordingProgressOverlay exposes Show/Hide counts and step updates. Assert product outcomes in addition to boundary observations. Shared doubles live in testing/TestSupport/Fakes under DBTools.Tests.Shared.Fakes. InlineSafeExecutor exposes RunCount and OptionsHistory. InlineTransactionRunner exposes RunCount and TransactionNames. Use the production executor, transaction service, or call gate when its behavior is the subject of the test. Source-link Pure helpers into Pure projects and Revit helpers into Local projects. Shared neutral helpers can serve both. Keep NUnit setup scopes and fixture namespaces aligned with their owner. Model paths TestPathResolver reads DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_MODELS_DIR on every call. The daemon supplies the staged root. Relative paths retain their year, tool, shared-directory, and filename segments. Rooted paths and ./.. traversal segments fail. There is no fallback to a user model cache. var model = TestPathResolver.ResolveTestModelPath("2026", "GM", "gm_test_model.rvt"); A model under <year>/Regression/ is a staged working copy whose external links are not included. DocumentLease disables link loading before opening that copy and refuses regression paths outside the staged root. RevitFamilyTemplateResolver searches only requested template names beneath CommonApplicationData/Autodesk/RVT <running-year>/Family Templates. It orders English-Imperial candidates first, then paths deterministically. BasicFileInfo.Extract(...).Format must equal the running Revit year. No matching installed template yields Inconclusive with observed formats/errors. Repository-controlled models and assets are different: missing staged files must fail the test. Hosted context and cleanup Use RevitHost.RunAsync(...) for the daemon-provided UIApplication. It initializes year, ambient call-gate state, the App host, and runtime assembly context. WPF name-only product loads resolve with the active App assembly. RevitAmbientScope owns publication/restoration of the ambient UIApplication. A native callback's API scope applies only to its synchronous prefix. Later continuations use a fresh product probe or gate. DBT_TEST_RUN_ID identifies automation so startup errors remain headless. Fixtures release only runtime/task hosts, owners, static state, documents, and overlays they own. The daemon terminal owns final release of its active Autodesk document. Use document leases rather than closing unrelated documents. When work and cleanup fail, preserve both. Attempt every owned document close, UIDocument disposal, logging shutdown, transaction-group finalization, and window/session disposal. A production launch smoke must use the production session owner and await its exact startup and failure-bearing completion. Await session completion to observe Closed handlers, ViewModel cleanup, and scope disposal. Add or move a fixture Identify the production operation and the result to assert. Select Pure tests for behavior without Revit, Revit-hosted tests for real API/document/session behavior, or Design Automation tests for APS execution. Mirror the production path beneath Tests/, or Tests/Integration/Revit/ for Revit-hosted fixtures. Include the fixture and support in the matching project. Use real product workflows, matchers, planners, and persistence. Supply doubles for external inputs such as Revit, network, filesystem, and time. List the selection, run the focused fixture, and run the affected Pure suites. Compile Revit-hosted fixtures separately when a Revit worker is unavailable. When moving a fixture to Pure, replace incidental Revit data carriers with native values or snapshots at an existing product boundary. Keep actual WPF behavior in Windows Pure tests and document/API behavior in Revit-hosted tests. Local, Both, and DA NUnit categories are invalid routing metadata. Use [RevitLocal] and [RevitDA] for those execution hosts. Other categories can describe properties independent of the host. A Design Automation test requires a product entry that works without UIApplication, UIDocument, selection, or an interactive session. Global Mapper examples GM Pure fixtures use native mapping state, persistence, similarity, usage projections, and planning. Construct required ProjectState records explicitly with 64-bit element IDs. Use FamilyMappingOptionProjector for nested family options without constructing the complete application window. Keep preview data native until the WPF boundary. Fixture Boundary StatePersistenceTests, UIStateCacheTests, UIStateLifecycleTests UI-state and saved-mapping persistence. MappingIntentStoreTests, ProjectStateStoreTests Mapping intent and project-state replacement. SharedParameterTreeProjectorTests Native shared-parameter tree projection. SavedMappingRestoreWorkflowTests Saved-mapping restoration. FamilyMappingSelectionNavigationWorkflowTests Family-details navigation. FamilyMappingOptionProjectorTests Nested family options. OperationRowProjectorTests Commit-review operation and error rows. SessionOperationGateTests Session operation admission and overlay lifetime. Use Revit-hosted tests for document adapters, shared parameters, deep scans, window composition with Revit dependencies, and active-view/document behavior. Super Girt Tool examples SGT Pure tests exercise domain values, feature decisions, undo/redo, and file-backed UI state. UIStateStoreTests uses Windows Pure. ExtentResolverTests and MemberResolutionSpanIndexTests exercise the portable domain. PreviewPlacementParityTests uses Revit-hosted execution for placement parity. Real geometry/document adapters and Revit selection also require Revit. Example: native duplicate detection DuplicateDetectionEngineTests.DetectAsync_HigherScore_WithParameterOverlap uses real duplicate matchers and asserts their returned pairs. The fixture's setup supplies _svc and the external element-name query _names. SetFamilyParameterDiscovery constructs the native discovery state: [Test] public async Task DetectAsync_HigherScore_WithParameterOverlap() { var projectState = new ProjectState { Families = new Dictionary<long, ProjectStateFamilyRecord> { [100] = new ProjectStateFamilyRecord { ElementId = 100, Name = "Door Type" }, [101] = new ProjectStateFamilyRecord { ElementId = 101, Name = "Door Type 1" } } }; SetFamilyParameterDiscovery(projectState.Families[100], "Width", "Height", "Frame Depth"); SetFamilyParameterDiscovery(projectState.Families[101], "Width", "Height", "Frame Depth"); _names.AddName(100, "Door Type"); _names.AddName(101, "Door Type 1"); var result = await _svc.DetectAsync(projectState); var pairs = result.Groups .Where(group => group.Kind == DuplicateKind.Families) .SelectMany(group => group.Pairs) .Where(pair => (pair.FromId == 100 && pair.ToId == 101) || (pair.FromId == 101 && pair.ToId == 100)) .ToList(); Assert.That(pairs, Is.Not.Empty); Assert.That(pairs.All(pair => pair.Score >= 90), Is.True); } View Template Comparer (VTC) supplies CategoryTabClassifierTests, which opens the staged SGT model and classifies real Revit categories. That fixture uses [RevitLocal] to exercise the category adapter. Hosted UI restrictions Revit-hosted tests cannot display blocking modals. The daemon rejects modal dialogs, disabled native owners, and Revit unhandled-exception windows. This restriction also applies to short-lived dialogs. Show hosted sessions modelessly with Show and bounded DispatcherDrain or DispatcherFaultScope helpers. Keep API, assembly-context, theme, and real Revit owner checks hosted. Test ShowDialog results, modal-loop exit, native owner disable/restore, and modal-child refusal in Windows Pure tests with real WPF windows and stand-in owners. Audit indirect alert and file-picker calls too. ToolWindowDialog rejects Revit processes/routing categories before using the session. Its bounded watchdog supports Windows Pure tests, including a beforeShow callback. Hosted assembly setup also installs a modal tripwire on Revit's UI dispatcher: it records WPF ShowDialog entry and posts a Send-priority close of that exact dialog. The test fails even after Pass, Ignore, or Inconclusive. The daemon can detect a modal before the tripwire runs. CommonDialog may raise the event without a WPF Window. The tripwire records it without closing an unrelated window. Native message boxes, TaskDialog, disabled owners, and separate STA dispatchers remain outside that backstop. The daemon's window probe is authoritative. Exceptional closure tests use Core's per-window error boundary. Assert that only the exact attached window receives a classified handled-error signal, foreign failures remain unhandled, and unsubscribe/detach remove the observer. Hosted sessions consume that signal through a bounded modeless pump, finalize, and surface the original error before cleanup/lifetime assertions. Modal-frame behavior remains Windows Pure coverage. Test settings and warnings Use isolated files with the real settings reader and writer. Cover defaults, layering, case-insensitive keys, generated serialization, invalid values, atomic batches, competing writes, cancellation, and corrupt files. Exercise pending changes and post-commit failures through the real context and persistence workflow. Use Windows Pure tests for WPF bindings and owner handles. Use Revit-hosted tests for prerequisite actions that modify a document. With real warning, catalog, and context services, check these outcomes: Invalid saved configuration activates a warning during startup. An unsaved invalid draft leaves shared command blocking unchanged. Save and Reset publish decisions for committed values. Clear and Fix act on the matching context and report failures. Command preflight checks every applicable active warning. Ribbon enabled state follows the latest individual warning update. A runtime execution exception suppresses the task for its document session. A startup validation exception is logged without activating a feature warning. APS Design Automation Sentinel LightweightSentinel_ExecutesRealDesignAutomationWorkItem is the real APS test. Its net8.0 client loads no Revit or Windows API. It uploads a zipped Sentinel appbundle and seed model, executes a Revit 2026 WorkItem, and asserts the Revit version and returned output. The daemon does not run it. A real Sentinel run requires APS app credentials in the environment: ./test.sh test --tool DA-SENTINEL --scope da Variable Meaning APS_CLIENT_ID Required app client ID. APS_CLIENT_SECRET Required app secret. APS_BUCKET Optional OSS bucket. Default dbtools-tests. Missing credentials fail rather than skip. The CLI estimates 5–12 minutes per WorkItem, and the test's wait is bounded at 12 minutes. Each run consumes APS processing time. Account allowances and billing must be checked separately. They are not repository configuration. Each run creates appbundle/activity versions, binds unique run<32 hex digits> aliases, and uses an output object with that identity. The activity references this run's uploaded bundle version. Cleanup runs on success or failure, keeps the newest two versions, and prunes at most 25 versions of each resource per run. Activities are pruned first. Appbundle aliases/versions referenced by remaining activities are retained. Missing resources need no pruning. Both resources receive cleanup attempts. If activity references cannot be read, keep all appbundle aliases and delete only unaliased versions. Already-deleted versions and aliases count as removed. Cleanup and primary failures remain visible together. APS error bodies, SDK messages, and WorkItem reports pass through redaction before logs, exceptions, and TRX output. The client removes known credentials, issued/bearer tokens, authorization/cookie headers, credential fields, and signed URL secrets, and truncates long text. The project also has network-free tests using a fake HTTP handler for version binding, pagination, token renewal, redaction, pruning, cleanup, run identity, bundle layout, and credential errors. Their selection is: ./test.sh test --tool DA-SENTINEL --scope da -f 'TestCategory!=RevitDA' The wrapper builds the frozen 2026 graph and runs its client locally. DA rejects daemon submit/rerun routing and result-JSON options. Evidence includes result.trx, uploaded bundle work files, and downloaded output under .artifacts/test-results/<run>/DBTools.DesignAutomation.Sentinel.DA.Tests/. Results and troubleshooting Read executed, passed, failed, and skipped counts in the runtime results. Use the request ID to locate a daemon run. Local Pure runs use TRX counters and preserve a failing TRX under .artifacts/test-results/<run>/<project>/result.trx. Daemon runs print the underlying job output and collect terminal reports. --result-json is daemon evidence, not a local Pure result file. Failure Action Missing model/params Check the project-declared model closure and daemon-staged paths. Do not search alternate models. Stale/missing build record Run normal test for the selected current source. --no-build intentionally refuses stale bytes. Relay/host initialization Check CLI/relay configuration. Compilation alone is not a test result. Windows Desktop runtime unavailable locally The wrapper selects the daemon. Check its CLI and relay configuration. Hidden-desktop refusal Inspect the daemon report and request ID for visible_desktop_violation or private_desktop_unavailable. Batch-only failure Isolate shared state in setup/teardown and inspect cleanup errors. BUILD artifact prerequisite Build the required product/test years explicitly. Artifact tests do not create prerequisites. Candidate-consuming BUILD fixtures additionally require AssembleDistributionCandidate. Their filters do not infer it. Acceptance checks require clean source. DistributionContractTests inspect real output references and reject bundled Revit host DLLs. Revit supplies those DLLs at runtime. Inspect %APPDATA%/DBTools/Logs/ first for reported application failures. Hosted job output returns application logs. Use the selected Revit year's journal for a crash only when those logs are inconclusive. See Test Pipeline and Build System.

developer-guide/index.html.title: Developer Guide | DB Tools
developer-guide/index.html.summary: Developer Guide This guide describes how DB Tools is built, structured and tested, and how to develop its tools. Start with the Architecture Overview, which describes the components, startup and tool loading. Section Contents Architecture Components, startup, build and test pipelines, assembly loading, themes Projects The Core, App, Sandbox and Presentation projects Tools (Technical) Implementation of each tool Developing Creating tools, settings packs, hooks, warnings, Sandbox integration, testing Troubleshooting Common errors and the logs Wiki Server How a push to kirsch33/dbtools-wiki updates the published site Requirements the .NET SDK pinned in global.json; build.sh and build.ps1 install it when it is missing; Python 3.10 or later on Linux and WSL; Desktop Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) or Revit 2027 to run the add-in. Building does not need Revit. Building ./build.sh # BuildAll: build, validate and publish both years ./build.sh BuildApp -y 2026 # product assemblies for one year ./build.sh AssembleDistributionCandidate -y 2026 pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 BuildAll # native Windows BuildAll, ValidateDistributionCandidate, PromoteToDist, BuildBundle and BuildInstaller always build every supported year; a -y that omits one fails. See Build Pipeline. Testing ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure # one tool, without Revit ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 # in Revit, through the daemon ./test.sh test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SomeTestName" ./test.sh test --scope all Revit-hosted tests (the local scope) run on the dbtools-daemon fleet. See Test Pipeline for the design and Testing Tools for the options. Writing documentation The wiki is built with DocFX from wiki/. Run bash .github/scripts/build-docs.sh conceptual to build the pages into wiki/_site; the Documentation workflow publishes the site through the wiki server. Write developer and user pages in the style of Unix reference documentation (Debian and GNU manuals, man pages): State what a component is, what it does, how it works, how to use it and its limits. Put the main point first. Use plain declarative sentences in the present tense and the active voice; use the imperative in procedures. Use the names the code uses, one term per concept. Use lists for steps and parallel items, tables for tabular data, and code blocks for commands, paths and literal values. Document commands as a synopsis, options and examples. Describe the current behavior only. Leave out change history, status and verification notes, dates, issue numbers, and the vocabulary of the process that produced a change. Keep a history note only for a migration step or compatibility break the reader needs. Leave out filler, hedging and repeated summaries. State each real limitation once, where it applies. Verify every technical claim against the current code, scripts and configuration before you write or keep it. The same rules apply to source comments, CLI help and messages. A comment explains a reason, an invariant or a non-obvious API behavior, not what the code already says. CLI help uses man-page form: a synopsis, then one line per option with its default. An error message names what failed, the relevant value or path and, where useful, what to do.

developer-guide/projects/app.html.title: DBTools.App | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/app.html.summary: DBTools.App DBTools.App builds DBTools.dll, the Revit add-in entry and the App runtime. It targets net10.0-windows (DBT_RevitTargetFramework) for desktop Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. Project Item Value Project src/DBTools.App/DBTools.App.csproj Assembly DBTools.dll Target net10.0-windows Product references DBTools.Core, DBTools.Presentation Merged package ricaun.Revit.UI, folded into DBTools.dll by the declared assembly merge Manifests Embedded in App for every tool Revit API references are compile-only and are never staged as product runtime files. The App project must not add a loose-copy target for the merged ricaun.Revit.UI files. Product output stages App at the year root and the tool assemblies below Tools/. Responsibilities App owns: the public parameterless Revit entry (AddinEntry) and the daemon idle acknowledgement; the non-inlined startup and shutdown boundary, and the startup fallback diagnostics; lifecycle, hooks (AppHooksToolModule), ribbon composition, the settings host and shutdown; the embedded tool manifests. The fourteen tool projects under src/Tools/ own their tool assemblies, including the Super Girt Tool (SGT), Settings and DialogSuppression. Each tool owner embeds its icons, raw views and manifest-declared design-time view models. Presentation owns the stable themes and compiled WPF controls. Source tree src/DBTools.App/ ├── Addin/ # Revit entry and installed-copy idle acknowledgement ├── Composition/ # DI and manifest-facing registration ├── Host/ # failure, test-run and window-owner boundaries ├── Lifecycle/ # publication, cleanup and lifecycle state ├── Logging/ # App logging-window integration ├── Ribbon/ # planning, Revit effects, state and startup styling ├── Runtime/ # App runtime and local Revit task ownership ├── Settings/ # App settings host and integration ├── Shutdown/ # synchronous shutdown workflow └── Startup/ # preparation, deferred work, effects and runtime boundary src/DBTools.App/MAP.md is generated from the source tree and manifest fields. Do not edit it by hand; after an owner directory or test path changes, run python3 .agents/work/canon_source_maps.py. Startup AddinEntry has a public parameterless constructor for Revit. The first action of OnStartup checks DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_ROLE and the load context of the entry assembly. Idle copy: only a file-backed entry in AssemblyLoadContext.Default acknowledges the installed idle copy. It records the key DBToolsDaemon.IdleAddin:<simple-name> (for App, DBToolsDaemon.IdleAddin:DBTools) with the entry location as its value, and returns success without touching the ribbon, events or other startup work. Normal startup: every other context (ProductLoadContext, DevModeLoadContext, a null context and any other context) enters ToolWindowCallbackScope and the non-inlined AppStartupBoundary. Startup initializes the App runtime, validates themes, composes the ribbon, starts the Revit call gate and publishes deferred startup work. Failure cleanup runs synchronously at the Revit API boundary and combines the primary and cleanup failures. A startup, shutdown or ribbon-runtime failure that cannot reach the normal log is written by a BCL-only writer to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log, so a missing Core or UI dependency does not hide the diagnostic. Shutdown OnShutdown uses the same boundary and returns only after the lifecycle cleanup result is complete. An idle installed entry has no runtime and returns success directly. The App runtime host lifecycle (ShutdownHost) step, the dispatcher-registry retirement and the cleanup summary are written to the fallback log after logging is disposed. The Revit task host step logs failures through the live logger. Composition AppRuntimeFactory builds the service root once. AppServiceProviderFactory registers logging, settings, UI ownership, Revit call gates, safe execution, command preflight, hooks, alerts and ribbon composition. AppToolModuleRegistrar asks Core's ToolModuleCatalog to discover the embedded manifest resources once. It instantiates the module owners, collects their settings, services and hooks in temporary registration state, validates module responsibilities and merges the state into the App container. Core's ToolAssemblyResolver loads the module, command, availability and icon owner of each manifest by explicit path from the product year's Tools/ directory, in the active owning load context. It checks the declared PE identity, rejects a loaded image with the same name from another path or identity, and probes no other directory. The command preflight creates the concrete command availability type before execution. ToolCommand.Execute and IsCommandAvailable enter the Presentation callback scope of the owning assembly. ExecutionContext flow is suppressed across callbacks, so host dispatchers and timers cannot keep a reference to an owning load context. Ribbon Ribbon planning builds each PushButtonData directly from a ToolRegistration: the file-backed Location of the command assembly, the command full name and the optional availability class full name. Grouped controls keep manifest order and use the same definitions. Settings, SGT and DialogSuppression use the same registration path as every other tool. On a reload (Dev Mode), RibbonComposer finds the retained panels without changing them and validates every requested panel and button before it removes, creates or restores anything. A refused reload leaves the ribbon unchanged and throws InvalidOperationException with a message that ends Restart Revit to load this ribbon definition. Retained ribbon change Result Same assembly path and command class Button reused. Changed availability class on a retained button Applied. Cleared availability class Refused; restart Revit. Removed, reordered or retyped items or buttons Refused; restart Revit. Changed stack placement, membership or row boundaries, or an item added to a retained stack Refused; restart Revit. Changed assembly path or command class Refused; restart Revit. New panel items or grouped-button children after the retained items Appended. Tests Pure tests cover the idle gate (role and load-context decisions), ribbon planning, settings and startup state. They compile only the source needed for platform-neutral behavior, must not run Revit startup and must not load Revit-typed members. Local (Revit-hosted) tests reference the real App project and cover entry behavior, real ribbon composition, command availability, lifecycle cleanup and Revit window ownership. A Revit-hosted test initializes the selected Revit year and uses the shared call gate. Revit-hosted tests take runtime ownership from the staged product tree. Tool project references stay compile references and do not add separate product images to the test dependency closure. Hosted inputs include the complete year root with Tools/ preserved; test assemblies, NUnit files and companions are separate inputs. The daemon's ProductLoadContext forwards product references to the same product instances that App uses. Release checks validate App's entry identity, embedded manifest ownership, command and availability owners, the stable Presentation resources, source-map freshness and the placement in the year tree. See Assembly Loading Contract, Project References and Test Pipeline.

developer-guide/projects/core.html.title: DBTools.Core | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/core.html.summary: DBTools.Core DBTools.Core is the shared infrastructure library of DB Tools. It contains the Revit execution layer (call gates and run scopes), transaction management, safe execution, logging, settings, the tool module system and shared UI components. Property Value Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Targets Desktop net10.0-windows (Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027); portable net10.0 WPF Desktop target only (UseWPF=true) Nullable Enabled Responsibilities Revit execution: thread-safe Revit API access through call gates and run scopes. Transactions: transaction and sub-transaction handling with rollback on failure. Safe execution: central error handling with user notification and logging. Logging: Serilog-based structured logging with a UI sink. Settings: typed settings sections with persistence and validation. Tool modules: discovery, registration and lifecycle of tools. Shared UI: window support, alert dialogs, progress overlays and behaviors. Build Desktop builds compile the complete Core for one Revit year. Pure tests and the Sandbox use that same image. Revit references are compile-only. Portable builds ($(DBT_PortableTargetFramework)) compile only the explicit source list in DBTools.Core.csproj, without WPF, Revit, merging or content identity. Designer builds (DBT_IsDesignerBuild=true) exclude Revit sources so the XAML designer can load without the Revit SDK. _wpftmp builds (temporary projects during BAML compilation) exclude Revit-dependent sources and re-include the runtime files that XAML resolution needs. A default desktop build writes its assembly to the artifact locations that the shared build props select. Revit-hosted test projects reference the evaluated Core TargetPath, not the product staging tree. Dependencies Reference Purpose DBTools.Manifest (project, desktop only) Portable manifest parser; merged privately with YamlDotNet DBTools.Presentation (project, desktop only) Stable WPF resources and controls Serilog.Extensions.Logging Structured logging; Core supplies the ThreadId enricher Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection Dependency injection CommunityToolkit.Mvvm MVVM base classes CSharpFunctionalExtensions Result types LibTessDotNet Polygon tessellation InternalsVisibleTo These assemblies see Core internals: runtime: DBTools, DBTools.GM, DBTools.SGT, DBTools.ERFT, DBTools.Settings, DBTools.DialogSuppression, DBTools.FoundationTags; Core tests: DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests, DBTools.Core.Local.Tests, DBTools.Core.HostedTurns.Local.Tests, DBTools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests; App tests: DBTools.App.Pure.Tests, DBTools.App.Local.Tests; tool tests: DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.Local.Tests, DBTools.DialogSuppression.Local.Tests, DBTools.ElevationTags.Local.Tests, DBTools.ERFT.Local.Tests, DBTools.FoundationTags.Local.Tests, DBTools.FramingJoins.Local.Tests, DBTools.GM.Local.Tests, DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.Local.Tests, DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes.Local.Tests, DBTools.RecordSet.Pure.Tests, DBTools.RecordSet.Local.Tests, DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests, DBTools.TDV.Local.Tests, DBTools.VTC.Local.Tests. Directory structure DBTools.Core/ +-- Alert/{Body,Composition,DesignTime,Domain,Selection,ViewModels,Views,Workflow} +-- AppRuntime/{Domain,Runtime} # Runtime contracts and the static accessor +-- Failure # FailurePrecedence +-- Guarding # Guard and analyzer marker +-- Hashing # SHA-256 operations +-- Json # Strict camel-case enum converter +-- Logging/{Composition,DebugMode,Files,LoggerWindow,Retention,Runtime,Sinks} +-- Notifications/{Composition,Domain,NotificationBanner,Runtime} +-- Paths # AppPaths +-- Progress/{Aggregation,Overlay} +-- Regex # Shared regex construction +-- Revit/{Composition,Context,DocumentSession,Execution,Transactions} +-- RevitInstance/{Identity,RevitYear} +-- Ribbon # ProductRibbon +-- SafeExecution/{Domain,Runtime} +-- Sandbox # SandboxMode +-- Settings/{Alerts,Catalog,Composition,DesignTime,Domain,Feedback,Persistence,RegexPattern,Reset,SettingsPack,State,Validation,ViewModels,Warnings} +-- TextFile # Text-file operations +-- Time # EasternTime +-- Tools/{Availability,Commands,Hooks,Manifest,Modules,Ribbon,Sandbox} +-- Transactions # Failure-definition contracts +-- UI/{ColorPicker,Commanding,DesignTime,Dispatching,FilePicker,Theming,Windows} +-- Tests # Core test projects Tests Project Target Content DBTools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests net10.0 Portable Core behavior that runs on Linux: Guard, strict JSON enums, safe-execution names and monotonic progress. References Core directly. DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests net10.0-windows Desktop Core and merged-owner behavior without Revit, including collectible composition activation, the progress overlay and the logger window dispatcher routing. DBTools.Core.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Revit-hosted fixtures. Has a test-only reference to DBTools.Presentation, which owns the overlay control and the structural preview. DBTools.Core.HostedTurns.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Fixtures that need real native Revit turns (the RevitHostedTurns category). Core test projects use explicit <Compile> membership. Test files mirror the owner folders under Tests/; when a test file moves, update the compile links in the Pure and Local projects in the same change. Revit execution and transactions Revit Execution and Progress Overlay owns the design of run scopes, call gates, queued turns, ITransactionRunner, transaction groups and the progress overlay.
