A branch is a DB Tools failure when its throwing method or a frame on its stack belongs to an assembly named exactly DBTools or starting with DBTools. (ordinal). Vendor code qualifies only as DBTools.HandyControl (the renamed HandyControl build) or DBTools.Presentation (which merges Helix). A raw HandyControl or HelixToolkit* assembly belongs to another add-in and never qualifies. A framework or Revit API failure raised from DB Tools code is therefore handled; another add-in's vendor failure is not. A bare DB Tools OperationCanceledException whose token was canceled is marked handled with a Warning log only: no banner and no handled-failure signal. The boundary presents and publishes the original outer exception, with its wrappers and causes, and returns the handled decision to the registry. An exception tree with no DB Tools branch stays unhandled and gets no notification. A window seen as closed keeps a weak tombstone and cannot be attached again. A closed WPF window that was never attached or seen is outside this registry; classifying it would need reflection or a new HWND. A lifecycle owner can subscribe through WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry to the handled-failure signal of its window. The subscription requires the attached per-window host and throws if it is missing. The notification carries the original failure and any presentation failure. Detaching clears the window's observers. WindowErrorPresenter owns the banner and logger-window show policy. WindowStaticRuntime configures and resets Core UI for App and Sandbox. It serializes the whole lifecycle and reports ready only after diagnostics, window error boundaries and progress overlays are all configured. It rejects duplicate or partial existing configuration before it changes anything. A failed configuration rolls back only what that attempt installed, in reverse order, so it can be retried; cleanup failures are kept with the primary failure. Reset attempts every Core UI cleanup step, clears readiness even when a step fails and reports cleanup failures in one aggregate. The progress-overlay capability owns its host registry and visual attachment, so this reset disposes every registered host. The progress capability exposes only a getter for the attached overlay-visibility state, so tool XAML can collapse airspace content. WindowRuntimeCapabilities.CreateSandbox(...) builds the Sandbox logger factory, logger, error-log surface, notification surface and a no-op progress capability inside the Core that owns the window interfaces. App startup configures its own notification, logging and progress capabilities. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/UI/Windows/Runtime/{WindowRuntimeCapabilities,WindowStaticRuntime}.cs, src/DBTools.Sandbox/Composition/AppRuntime.cs. Alerts public interface IAlertService { AlertResult Show(AlertRequest request); bool Confirm(string message, IWindowOwnerHandleProvider ownerHandleProvider, string title = "DB Tools"); T? SelectSingle<T>(AlertSelectionRequest<T> request) where T : class; IReadOnlyList<T> SelectMultiple<T>(AlertSelectionRequest<T> request) where T : class; } AlertServiceFactory and IAlertService are public. The internal AlertService, AlertBodyBuilder, AlertSelectionPolicy, AlertWindowPresenter and AlertWindowViewModel own request planning, body composition, selection, modal presentation and shell state. Confirm takes an IWindowOwnerHandleProvider; other alerts take owner and size policy in AlertWindowOptions. Implement IAlertBody for custom alert content. Alerts open with WindowStartupLocation.CenterScreen, which WPF centers on the work area of the owner's monitor in device pixels. An alert therefore opens on its owner's monitor (Revit or the DB Tools window that raised it) at any display scaling. WPF does not clamp the position, so an alert larger than the work area extends past it. Structural preview DBTools.Presentation.StructuralPreview.IStructuralPreview3D owns structural preview navigation and rendering. ERFT and the Super Girt Tool (SGT) pass immutable scene and emphasis snapshots and consume stable pointer events. Core compiles against Presentation; the Helix and SharpDX assets are private to Presentation. Each tool registers the viewport's synchronous disposal as a session cleanup. ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll releases the viewport handlers, timers, camera, material and device state and payload subscriptions before it closes the shell. See Structural Preview. Extension points Call gates: implement IRevitCallGate for another execution mode. Hooks: register IHookLifecycle implementations, or IViewActivationTask services for view-activated work. Settings packs: register packs with SettingsPackRegistration<TOptions, TContext>. Alert bodies: implement IAlertBody. Related pages Architecture Overview Project References DBTools.App

developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.title: DBTools.Presentation | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.summary: DBTools.Presentation DBTools.Presentation.dll is the WPF assembly that stays loaded for the life of the Revit process. It is staged at the root of each product year, beside DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Item Value Project src/DBTools.Presentation/DBTools.Presentation.csproj Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Target framework net10.0-windows (Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027) References WPF, DBTools.HandyControl; Helix, Serilog and the logging and DI abstractions are merged in Contents Presentation holds only types that must live for the whole process: theme dictionaries, resource keys, styles, converters and pack resources; controls whose code-behind is limited to binding, dependency-property, routed-event, input and lifecycle mechanics; the ModalWindow and ModelessWindow base types with their owner-handle contracts, and the tool window shells ToolWindowModalShell and ToolWindowModelessShell; tool-specific behaviors, converters and controls under Tools/<TOOL>/; the structural 3D viewport (see Structural Preview). Production source is under src/DBTools.Presentation, with namespaces DBTools.Presentation.* that follow the folder tree. The project also compiles four tool settings views linked from their tool folders; these keep their tool namespaces and do not make Presentation depend on the tool assemblies. Presentation does not reference DBTools.dll, Core, tool types, view models, commands, services or the Revit API. App, Core and the tools may reference Presentation. ColorPickerPopup exposes and binds dependency properties by property path, and popup dismissal updates the stable IsPopupOpen property. ProgressOverlayControl binds to the command that the host supplies. Tool windows Tool views are raw embedded XAML. ToolWindowHost creates a modal or modeless shell, parses the view inside ToolWindowReflectionScope and sets the tool's view model. Core's ToolWindowFactory runs WindowInitializer on the shell first, which installs owner, theme, progress and error handling, and then registers the session. Hosts call session.ShowDialog() or session.Show() and get named controls with session.Require<T>(name). When a session closes or is retired, Presentation tears down bindings, automation roots, resources and callbacks. See Theme System. UI Automation item lifetime Retirement does not clear cached automation peers. In WPF 10.0.0, item peers hold reference-type rows weakly (ItemAutomationPeer._item uses ItemWeakReference, and DataGridCellItemAutomationPeer._item is weak), and teardown cuts the strong column, row-item and DataContext references. Tool items in a DataGrid, ListBox or TreeView, their types and a collectible tool context can therefore be released after retirement, also while a UI Automation client is attached. Rows are held strongly, and a collectible tool assembly stays loaded, in these cases: the first item cached by a peer store has an unreliable hash code (for example ComponentResourceKey); the store switches to list mode and holds every later key strongly; the items are boxed value types; the ItemAutomationPeerKeepsItsItemAlive switch makes _item strong; a UI Automation client holds an item element, which keeps its control alive through ElementProxy._peer. Enumerating ItemPeersStorage or _WeakRefElementProxyStorage materializes the weak keys, so their contents do not show an owning reference. Resource URIs /DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Theme.xaml Raw and reloadable XAML declares stable namespaces with assembly=DBTools.Presentation. XAML compiled inside Presentation uses the form without assembly=. See Theme System for URI rules and Assembly Loading Contract for the distribution layout.

developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.title: DBTools.Sandbox | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.summary: DBTools.Sandbox DBTools.Sandbox is a standalone executable that validates one product year and hosts tool windows for UI development without Revit. It targets net10.0-windows for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; build/Distribution/RevitYearContract.cs defines the supported years. Source layout Path Contents App/Startup/ SandboxEntry (BCL-only entry point), CLIOptions, SandboxCandidate, the SandboxMode enum (Interactive, Headless) App/ The WPF application Composition/ Sandbox runtime services and SandboxWindowFactory Features/WindowCatalog/ The window catalog shown in interactive mode Runtime/ Sandbox logging and window runtime configuration Validation/ Candidate, manifest, metadata and window validators Tests/ DBTools.Sandbox.Pure.Tests Runtime Sandbox starts a new default-context process for each candidate year. The entry point checks the year directory before any Core, Presentation or WPF type loads, loads the candidate's top-level assemblies and Tools/ assemblies from their paths, and then starts WPF. The candidate files are the only product assemblies in the process; the project compiles against Core, Presentation and HandyControl without copying their runtime files. Sandbox reads window specifications from the tool manifests through Core's SandboxCatalog and hosts them in the stable Presentation window shells. At startup it calls DBTools.Core.Sandbox.SandboxMode.Activate, so SandboxMode.IsActive is true in this process; tool code checks it to avoid Revit-only services. Building real windows and checking their cleanup requires the Windows process. For the options, the validation steps and the manifest rules, see Sandbox Validator. See also Sandbox Integration and Assembly Loading Contract.

developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.summary: Elevation Tags Overview Elevation Tags aligns spot elevation text relative to leader endpoints in floor, structural, and ceiling plans. Manual alignment runs on the active view. Automatic alignment runs when a supported view activates. Architecture Ownership and registration Source: src/Tools/Structural/ElevationTags/. The manifest places the tool on the Common panel. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/ElevationTagsCommand Ribbon entry point and active-view availability App/Composition/ElevationTagsToolModule Settings and pack registration App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions Feature registration App/Composition/SettingsPackContextFactory Settings context and live type snapshots Features/AlignElevationTagsWorkflow Manual validation and completion toasts Features/ViewActivatedTask Supported-view automatic execution Features/ElevationTagsUpdater Shared inline call gate, transaction runner, and updater construction Features/AutoUpdater Filtering, layout, mutation, and counts Features/SpotElevationSymbolResolver Spot marker-symbol resolution Features/SpotElevationTypeProjector Live type snapshots for settings Settings/SettingsPackContext Pattern, type, and preview wiring and validation Settings/PatternContext Core RegexPatternListContext adapter Settings/TypeContext, TypeSelection Type filtering, navigation, and offsets Settings/PreviewContext Preview formatting and image state Settings/Views/ElevationTagsSettingsPackView.xaml Settings layout The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.ElevationTags. The module type is DBTools.ElevationTags.App.Composition.ElevationTagsToolModule. Command and availability both use DBTools.ElevationTags.App.Composition.ElevationTagsCommand. The button uses InlineUi, icon key align_elevation_tags, and order 20. The icon asset is Assets/align_elevation_tags_icon.png. Data and contracts Settings Settings use configuration section Tools.ElevationTags and pack key common.elevation_tags. Property Default Meaning AutoUpdateEnabled true Run on supported view activation TagNamePatterns Empty list Regex patterns. An empty or all-blank list uses the static defaults TypeOffsets Empty dictionary TypeAlignmentOffsets keyed by spot elevation type name The default pattern is: ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$ The UI permits up to three patterns and validates their syntax. At least one nonblank pattern is required to save settings. Runtime compiles nonblank patterns case-insensitively. Invalid patterns log warnings and are skipped. With no valid compiled patterns, no tags match. TypeAlignmentOffsets contains AlongLeaderOffset and PerpendicularOffset. Both default to zero for an unconfigured type. Runtime multiplies these values by view.Scale / 12. The signs follow the computed text side relative to the leader endpoint. Filtering AutoUpdater collects non-type OST_SpotElevations elements from the active view as SpotDimension instances. A match against any configured regex includes the spot. Candidate strings include the spot name, spot type and family names, and resolved marker-symbol type and family names. The matcher tests these strings separately. A failure reading a spot's names increments FailedCount. The first such failure in a run logs its exception. Leaderless spots, missing types, and Relative-base spots require no update. Results and errors AutoUpdater.Run() returns ElevationTagRunResult with: Field Meaning TotalSpotsInView Collected spots PatternMatches Spots accepted by name patterns UpdatedCount Spots whose position changed FailedCount Name-reading or per-spot update failures Candidate updates share the undo entry DB Tools - Align spot elevations, for both the Align command and the update on view activation. The updater catches per-spot update faults, counts them, and continues. The first update fault logs its exception. Collection, layout preparation, and transaction-level failures can propagate. The manual workflow shows a Warning toast when failures exist, Success when tags change, and Info for no spots, no pattern matches, or matching spots requiring no changes. See Limitations for cases that require no position change. Automatic updates log a summary warning for partial failures. Uncaught automatic-update failures reach Core's view-activation handling, which shows a runtime-failure banner and skips that task for the document session. This runtime failure does not set a persistent settings warning. Warning core.structural.elevation_tags disables DBTools.AlignElevationTagsInView and automatic updates. The settings context exposes the warning state and disables its automatic-update toggle while the warning is active. Workflows Use Open a FloorPlan, EngineeringPlan, or CeilingPlan view. Configure Elevation Tags in Settings. Run Align Elevation Tags, or enable automatic updates. The command requires an active view. An unsupported view produces a warning toast without running alignment. The settings preview redraws as per-type offsets change. Alignment algorithm Read the origin, leader end, current text position, and spot type. Resolve elevation and format its text using document units and the type's unit options. Measure the text with GDI+ using font, text size, width scale, and display DPI. Compute placement relative to the leader end and current above/below text side. Apply the configured per-type offsets. Write TextPosition when X or Y differs after rounding to two decimal places in internal coordinates. Z remains the existing text Z. The view factor is view.Scale / 12. The measured horizontal half-width receives margins of 2 * factor / 128 + factor / 8. The vertical margin is factor / 64. Placement below the leader also accounts for measured text height. The elevation base uses the type's displayed SPOT_ELEV_BASE value: Display value Calculation Project Base Point Subtract project base point Z only when project and survey point positions differ by at least 1e-9 on an axis Relative Skip alignment Other values, including Survey Point Use spot origin Z An Elevation Indicator becomes the prefix only when Elevation Indicator as Prefix/Suffix equals Prefix and the indicator is nonblank. Otherwise the measured prefix is EL. . The calculation does not append a configured suffix. Font defaults to Arial and width scale defaults to 1 when their parameters are absent. A units-format lookup failure logs once and uses default formatting. Troubleshooting Symptom Check No matches Compare patterns with spot, type, family, and marker-symbol names Automatic updates absent Check the toggle, warning state, supported view type, and runtime log Matching spots unchanged Check leader presence, elevation base, and rounded position Partial alignment Inspect the first filtering or update exception in the DB Tools log Testing Pure tests cover the runner, symbol resolution, settings state, preview, and manual summaries. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover the command, module, workflow, view activation, live updater, and type projection. See architecture and themes. Limitations Elevation-base and prefix comparisons require English display strings and use ordinal matching. No-change counts combine already aligned spots, leaderless spots, and spots with a Relative elevation base.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm-producti.title: GM Production Contracts | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm-producti.summary: GM Production Contracts These Global Mapper (GM) behaviors are performance or correctness requirements. Each section names the source that implements the contract and the effect of breaking it. A change to a contract is a product change; update this page with it. See Global Mapper for the tool design. Paths are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Usage index sampling cap Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/UsageIndexSource.Families.cs, QuerySampleInstanceIdsBySymbol The usage index samples one family instance per family type (symbol), at most 2500 instances (MaxSampleInstances in UsageIndexSource.cs). It streams view-independent (model) instances first and returns as soon as it has 2250 samples. Only when the model instances give fewer than 2250 samples does it add view-owned instances of the active view, up to the cap. Unbounded iteration scales with views times instances: a project with 200 views and 50,000 instances stalls for minutes. One geometry pass per usage kind Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/StyleMaterial/UsageStyleMaterialCollector.cs, QueryStyleMaterialUsageChunk Style and material usage are captured from the same sample. Instance geometry is requested once for styles and once for materials, both with IncludeNonVisibleObjects = true. Symbol geometry is requested only when the instance has no geometry. Style geometry uses the owning or active view; material geometry uses view-independent Fine detail. Sharing one geometry result between them changes coverage. The combined chunk shares element lookup and the traversal of family-dependent styles. One instance for parameter discovery Features/Families/Revit/FamilyScanner.ParameterNames.cs, QueryMappableParamNamesForFamily Parameter-name discovery reads the parameters of every type of the family and of one instance. Parameter definitions are family-level, so every instance has the same definitions; scanning more instances adds cost and no data. Deep scan runs only on request Features/DeepScan/Workflow/DeepScanWorkflow.cs A deep scan opens family documents with EditFamily, which takes seconds per family. It runs only from a user action: Scan Family on a family row, deep scan of all visible families, or deep scan of unscanned families with zero instances (after a confirmation). Background prewarm only reads the deep scan cache; it never starts a scan. See GM specification. Parameter discovery filter Revit/ParameterDiscovery/ParameterDiscoveryEligibility.cs Discovery excludes read-only parameters, built-in parameters (InternalDefinition with a valid BuiltInParameter) and blank definition names. It does not filter on UserModifiable, because Revit can report a parameter that the API can write as not user-modifiable. Removing the read-only or built-in filter offers parameters that cannot be written or should not be mapped. Adding a UserModifiable filter hides valid mapping targets. Simple style canonicalization UsageStyleMaterialCollector.RecordStyle; Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/UsageIndexSource.StyleMaterial.cs, BuildStyleCanonicalizationMap Style usage records the raw style ID and its canonical projection ID only. Recording every equivalent alias multiplies dictionary insertions per geometry object without improving the result. Style maps built once per usage build UsageIndexSource.StyleMaterial.cs, BuildStyleMaterialUsageAsync Style canonicalization, category projection and object-style classification run once per usage build, and their results are passed to each chunk of 25 instances (UsageChunkSize). Rebuilding them per chunk repeats a full FilteredElementCollector scan for every chunk.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.title: Global Mapper architecture specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.summary: Global Mapper architecture specification Overview Global Mapper (GM) collects Revit content, builds mapping intent, and executes reviewed replacement plans. This specification describes its state, execution, persistence, and lifetime contracts. Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. GM describes entry points and test surfaces. Architecture Composition and document scope App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory captures the launch UIDocument and Document, creates a QueuedModeless App run scope, and binds its concrete GmSessionDocumentGate once before resolving modeless work. The gate compares ordinal DocumentSessionKey values on each callback. The key uses the document hash code for session scoping. It does not guarantee collision-free identity. The persistence key is the nonblank document path, or that captured session key for an unsaved document. Unsaved documents load saved data only under their captured session key. AddGm() registers the concrete GM gate without replacing shared IRevitCallGate registrations. GM Revit readers, writers, family batches, transaction runners, and Commit Review consume the concrete gate. RevitMappingPlanExecutor rejects an invalid document or session-key mismatch before writers begin. RunCleanupAsync uses the underlying gate with CancellationToken.None so owned documents can close after authority or work cancellation ends. Commit Review uses the bound parent gate to create an InlineUi child scope. It binds the child gate once to the expected document before running apply services. One outer Revit callback contains planning, modal review, apply, finalization, and refresh. During that modal session, forced-queue, off-thread, or second-callback work is refused. AppSessionProjectionBuilder receives a host-neutral MappingProjectionContext, workspace/dialog state, a required IViewOps implementation, and feature services. The runtime wraps that same projection in MappingExecutionContext with its ExpectedDocument. The bound gate carries the session authorization key. Host-neutral panes and rows receive the projection context. Commit Review receives the execution context. Authorization identity and persistence identity have separate consumers. WindowSessionServices supplies the attached owner and progress overlay. ErrorNotifierFactory uses that owner. GmWindowAttachment supplies feature dialogs with a late-bound getter for the attached window. Design-time composition uses explicit host-neutral collaborators, including DesignTimeViewOps. AppSessionBuilder constructs startup, initialization, Deep Scan, preference clearing, background prewarm, Family Mapping commands, pane lifecycle, and disposal workflows. RowRefreshFactory builds one row collaboration graph per session. Its outputs include CrossPaneRowRefresh, RowRefreshCoreServices, CommitReviewRowServices, UIStateFactory, and OptionRenderingRefresh. App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences Usage rows, Family Mapping refresh, selected-family state, indicators, live-update suppression, row locks, and workspace events. It implements feature-owned ICommitReviewRowRefresh, IFamilyMappingCrossPaneCommands, and IDeepScanUsageRefresh. FilterRefreshWorkflow, StartupRowWorkflow, and PageActivationWorkflow consume that runtime. App/Sessions owns session records and runtime lifetime. Composition owns construction. Feature implementations do not import DBTools.GM.App. FamilyMappingFactory returns FamilyMappingViewModel, FamilyMappingScanWorkflow, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, FamilyMappingTypeCreation, and one MappingRowSet spanning family/type and supplied Usage rows. FamilyMappingScanStateApplier belongs to scan sequencing. The row builders and refresh owners receive the same row set. Public surface and resources GM production payload types default to internal. Manifest activation requires public GmToolModule and GmCommand. Public conflict projection values retain their public binding properties. Dependency objects, converters, selectors, and attached behaviors are stable public Presentation types. The design-time view models are internal with public binding/fragment properties. Sandbox and production consume the same raw resources and fragments. Compiled resource validation checks manifest logical names. Source reference Paths below are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Contract Source Launch and document gate App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory.cs, Revit/Document/GmSessionDocumentGate.cs Session graph App/Composition/Revit/AppSessionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/AppSessionProjectionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/RowRefresh/RowRefreshFactory.cs Modeless lifetime App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSession.cs, App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate.cs State and names Domain/ProjectState/ProjectStateStore.cs, Domain/ElementNames/ElementNamesCache.cs Persistence App/Persistence/StatePersistence.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateLifecycle.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateCache.cs Scan admission Features/DeepScan/DeepScanOrchestrator.cs, Features/DeepScan/Refresh/DeepScanRefreshWorkflow.cs Usage publication Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexLoader.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageMatchIndex.cs Options and similarity Features/Mapping/State/MappingOptionCache.cs, Features/Similarity/Naming/NamingSimilarity.cs Execution Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingPlanExecutor.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingApplyResultBuilder.cs, Features/Mapping/Revit/Execution/Batch/FamilyBatchExecutor.cs Review Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewApplyWorkflow.cs, Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewFinalizer.cs Intent identity Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentKey.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentStore.cs Data and contracts Domain and feature contracts Project state Domain/ProjectState owns ProjectState, family/type records, reference index/values, project parameters, scan state, projection, and the scoped ProjectStateStore. The store imports no feature or App namespace. CurrentProjectState and CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identify the loaded snapshot and its category in one replacement operation. IProjectStateBuilder and ProjectStateBuildRequest are inward contracts. App/State/ProjectStateBuilder queries Families, Usage, Shared Parameters, and Previews and projects their results into those values. Family-only refresh retains loaded Usage and Shared Parameters sections and invalidates derived usage caches before preparing rows. A failed build preserves published state. Commit Review planning builds the selected category plus pending-intent owner families without publishing. CarryForwardInto supplies loaded sections and unchanged-family Deep Scan evidence to that planning state. Duplicate detection also stays unpublished. CarryDeepScanEvidenceInto supplies only unchanged-family evidence to its fresh full state. The ProjectStateStore retains evidence across category-filtered state replacement. A rebuild restores it only when the family's type set and per-type instance counts remain unchanged. After commit, ReplaceProjectStateAfterCommit discards directly changed families and containing ancestors across all categories. Direct changes include mapped/owning families, families of mapped types, and material/object-style families found by AffectedFamilyResolver. Commit Review planning uses that same resolver. Its plan context owns planning identity and evidence. Discarding evidence removes scan state, type payloads, DeepScanResults, and fast parameter discovery together. Element names and categories Domain/ElementNames owns IElementNameQuery, ElementNamesCache, and ElementNameLookupKind. Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQuery implements the Revit adapter. App registers it with state/cache wiring. Categories registers curated-category services. Strict name loading requires a nonblank cached name for every requested ID. Blank entries are queried again. Omitted/blank provider values stay unresolved. GetResolvedFamilyName prefers cache, then project-state family name, and throws if neither exists. Display getters retain explicit ID/unavailable-name fallbacks. WorkspaceState.SelectedCategory is the single typed CategoryOption value exposed by IWorkspaceState. CategoryFilter derives its display label. Null and Id zero select every family. Other signed IDs select exactly that category, including negative built-in Revit IDs. Both IFamilyQuery methods use those rules. GetFamiliesAsync reuses state only when category identity matches, families exist, and all family names are nonblank. It still filters the reused result by the requested category. WorkspaceState.SortMode uses MatchingOptionSortMode through mutation, persistence, restoration, and option projection. CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identifies loaded state. FamilyMappingState.AppliedCategoryId identifies applied rows. Applying a different category resets category-scoped rows before application and records the category only after rows apply. Cancellation between state publication and row application therefore causes a reset on retry. Mapping intent, rows, and conflicts Features/Mapping/Domain owns immutable intent, conflict, operation, plan, and host-free execution values. It does not import mutable Rows types. MappingIntentKey validates its nine-field shape through named factories and FromPersisted. It rejects invalid zero identities while retaining signed category IDs such as -2000011. The Rows package owns row-to-intent translation, projection, origin mutation, and family-apply behavior. Conflict/Rows owns row conflict matching. Detection consumes an immutable MappingSelectionSnapshot. MappingConflictWorkflow hydrates returned MappingIntentKey values into loaded rows. MappingConflictTarget defines three closed variants: a positive element selection, a type-parameter policy, or a display-only message. Resolution chooses an original side or an explicit MappingConflictBulkAction. Display labels and sentinel IDs do not encode executable policy. Duplicates implements Mapping-owned neutral selection/resolution contracts without exporting its own selection types. Mapping owns projection/execution contexts, row signals, navigation values/lifetimes, MappingUpdateSuppression, and OriginClearSuppression. Mapping Domain/Planning owns nested-family, style, and type-reference plan language. Commit Review's CommitReviewDocumentEditBuilder owns mutable family-batch assembly. Mapping's neutral composition registers MappingIntentStore. Commit Review composition registers CommitReviewPlanVerifier. Revit/Composition registers mutation adapters, attached by App's AddGm root. Shared Parameters implements Mapping's focused embed port and uses Mapping operation identities. Domain/Parameters/FamilyParameterDiscoveryResult carries normalized ScopedParameterName values, complete/partial state, and contextual read errors. Family Mapping and Shared Parameters publish choices only from complete discovery. Duplicate parameter scoring requires complete discovery on both sides. Instance/Type suffixes are display labels. Parameter mappings retain scope and require equal source/target scope. Element identities Revit family, type, instance, material, style, view, and category IDs use long. Revit boundaries use ElementIdConverter.ToLong and FromLong. Saved-mapping and UI-state JSON accept integer-valued number tokens, including values in the 32-bit range. Family-document materials resolve by name rather than host numeric ID. Counts, indexes, depths, enum/order casts, synthetic duplicate group IDs, SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher sequence IDs, and MappingOption.StableStringId hashes use int. SharedParameterValueCopier rejects Map From values outside Int32 for Revit Integer storage. ElementId parameter destinations parse Map From text as long. Persistence and saved mappings Domain/Cache owns tool-wide cache paths, metadata, and recovery policy. App/Persistence owns document UI-state storage and session persistence sequencing. StatePersistence requires both IUIStateCache and ISavedMappingStore in production. Design-time projection does not construct unused persistence. JSON writes flush a unique sibling temporary file and publish it atomically. Cancellation or I/O failure preserves the last good snapshot. Only confirmed missing files/directories count as absent. Access, sharing, invalid-path, and other I/O faults propagate. UI-state and Deep Scan snapshots are disposable caches: malformed, invalid, or old snapshots are discarded and logged. Saved mappings are user data and use strict nullable-ingress validation with contextual failures. Cache results are immutable hit/miss values. Hits always contain data. IUIStateCache serializes asynchronous writes and clears across scoped instances with a process-wide mutation gate. StatePersistence serializes document loads, clears, and saves and tracks separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. An older open session cannot restore either snapshot after another window clears it. A freshly loaded window can persist new state. UIStateLifecycle attempts enabled close writes independently, retains failures in write order, and resets one-shot suppression even on failure. Confirmed clears drain before close persistence and disposal. PaneStateProjector supplies SavedAt. Saving preserves the supplied timestamp. Saved Mappings validates exact document identity and every persisted key before admission. Parameter mappings retain ScopedParameterName scope. The persistence port exposes load, save, and clear. MappingIntentStore owns merging. Commit Review constructs the restore workflow, merges persisted intent, and reapplies through row owners. Clearing saved mappings follows this order: Remove saved origins/selections from loaded rows. Clear mapping intent, duplicate intent, and the in-memory persisted list. Clear storage. Run the required App-bound refreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear operation. CrossPaneRowRefresh rebuilds loaded Usage rows, refreshes Family Mapping rows, reconciles indicators under suppression, releases suppression, refreshes locks, and publishes cache status. Reapply calls Usage, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, Shared Parameters, and row locks directly. Option cache and similarity MappingOptionCache keys candidates by mapping kind, source ID, category, ordered target ID/name pairs, and source label. Category lookup does not fall back to general entries. Prewarm uses the same identity. Candidate snapshots use private read-only lists, so replacing entries cannot mutate earlier results. NamingSimilarity.Normalize and numeric-suffix stem comparison retain letters/digits in invariant lowercase. Numeric-suffix siblings with equal cleaned stems score 1.0 before Dice evaluation. Dice uses lowercased raw-name bigrams, including punctuation and whitespace, with multiplicities. Its score is twice the multiset intersection divided by the sum of raw lengths minus two. For a raw length below two, equal raw lengths score 1.0 only with equal nonempty cleaned stems. Other short-name pairs score zero. Each scoring pass owns its immutable name-profile cache. Deep Scan Deep Scan owns family scans, projection, usage resolution, feature cache, and refresh workflow. A user scan collects a complete family batch and finishes cache preparation before one validated ApplyBatch admission. Usage refresh data is prepared before completed scan state publishes. Cancellation or required failure before admission preserves the prior projection. Host lookup completeness is separate for styles, materials, and families. An item failure marks only its domain incomplete and prevents partial singleton-name resolution or resolver-cache reuse. Other complete requested domains remain usable. Affected families retain warning diagnostics and incomplete usage. Unexpected collector/category traversal failures abort construction. Partial parameter discovery invalidates fast choices, is omitted from duplicate scoring, and removes prior reusable cache entries before admission. A later complete query can repopulate choices. Partial usage remains visible but cannot become reusable complete cache data. DeepScanCacheCoordinator removes prior reusable entries for incomplete parameter discovery or usage scans before admission. Failure to resolve a removal identity or remove an entry propagates and prevents admission. A cache write failure without required removals logs a warning. Cache operations use a local persistence gate plus an exclusive per-file process lock. Each batch reloads authoritative disk state once while holding both. Startup hydration reads eligible families against one load. User scan removes/writes its family batch with one load and one atomic save. This serializes owners across Revit processes. Disposal drains persistence before releasing the DI-root owner. Snapshot admission validates entries and parameter/usage completeness flags as a whole. It discards incompatible snapshots rather than salvaging entries. Clear Cache holds a session-lifetime registration through deletion, projection/UI refresh, and completion. It shares session-operation admission with scans. Shutdown drains it before disposing collaborators. A confirmed clear increments DeepScanOrchestrator's generation after disk deletion and before projection clearing. Hydration rejects its whole candidate batch if that generation changes or the captured ProjectState reference changes during reading. It never replaces an already completed family scan. CrossPaneRowRefresh implements IDeepScanUsageRefresh: apply Usage data, rebuild loaded rows when needed, reconcile Family Mapping state/indicators under suppression, then refresh locks. DeepScanRefreshWorkflow invalidates options and awaits the App-bound Shared Parameters authoring rebuild. That rebuild evicts authoring snapshots and rebuilds the loaded tree with pending intent and selection. Completion events describe changed cache state and publish even when rebuilding faults or cancels. The outcome then propagates to the operation boundary. Eligible-cache hydration finishes only after its queued UI refresh runs. AuthoringRebuildWorkflow serializes rebuild and application. If evidence invalidates during a build, including the first build, it builds again before applying. Disposal cancels held/queued rebuilds and prevents later application. Duplicates The Duplicates feature owns detection, selections, rows, resolution, tree, pane state, and type mapping. Detection/DuplicateDetectionEngine calls the family, style, material, and shared-parameter matchers, assigns aggregate group IDs, and returns DuplicateDetectionResult. The feature's Domain, Selection, Rows, Resolution, Tree, Pane, and TypeMapping folders own their respective contracts and behavior. SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher lives beside family/style/material matchers under Detection/Matching. CurrentDuplicateDetection owns the last fully completed artifact. Detection collects its unpublished full state, executes stable DuplicateKind stages, hydrates names, then publishes and returns the same artifact reference. Earlier failure/cancellation preserves the prior artifact. Family-row counts use that same detection state. The immediate rebuild receives the artifact explicitly. Other readers inject CurrentDuplicateDetection. Cached refresh waits for cross-dispatcher rebuilds. A reentrant request replaces the queued request. The outer refresh runs the latest queued rebuild before returning, including propagating its failure. PreviewDuplicateMatcher matches style/material candidates only when both resolve to the same signature. Unavailable previews never match, including each other. Duplicates imports neither Shared Parameters nor Commit Review. Families and Family Mapping Families' neutral composition registers FamilyQuery and IFamilyQuery. Its Revit composition registers FamilyDocumentService, FamilyScanner, and scanner ports. FamilyDocumentService owns document lifecycle/query, not Mapping material preparation. Families consumes its own IFamilyInstanceCountQuery, implemented by Usage's live source. A thrown Document.Close or false result is a cleanup failure under the shared strict close policy. FamilyMappingViewModel owns binding state and interactions. FamilyMappingScanWorkflow owns asynchronous scan/cache/post-commit sequencing and its private scan-state applier. FamilyMappingRowRefresh owns symbol projection, row build/refresh, saved-mapping reapply, and usage reconciliation. Ordinary category navigation reuses a category snapshot or matching loaded state. RescanFamiliesAfterCommitAsync discards every category snapshot and rebuilds from the document, including when category identity stays unchanged, so newly created types reach rows. App's CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences cross-pane work. Usage Usage owns indexing, matching/options, preview cache/versioning, rows, selection, traversal, and pane state. AppSessionProjectionBuilder constructs one UsageIndexLoader and FamilyUsage after session state, names, and operation gate exist. The loader retains those collaborators. It is not a context-free service. RebuildPlanningUsageIfNeededAsync returns Task and builds only a missing index when usage intent exists. RebuildUsageAfterCommitIfNeededAsync returns true only when it builds the index. UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder starts and drains five catalog/index tasks, aggregates non-cancellation faults, and creates an unpublished candidate without touching the match index. Name resolution, project-state usage storage, and Deep Scan refresh preparation precede publication. Index publication aligns the match index, target universe, hydration generation, and option cache. UsageMatchIndex shares one in-flight family hydration among concurrent callers. An index publication invalidates hydration started against the prior generation. UsageIndexPublished runs synchronously on the publishing thread, including workers. RowRefreshPublicationWiring dispatches row projection to the UI thread. Rows track publication version. Detect suppresses publication-driven duplicate rebuild and rebuilds once after scanning, retaining the keep target. Passive option projection suppresses intent capture. An unavailable saved target remains disabled for review. An explicit edit can clear or replace it. UsageViewModel owns target selection and bound collection/preview mutation. Selection-family flow performs one family lookup, name hydration, and row population. UsagePreviewService owns calculation, caching, and request-version order. UsageWorkflow consumes IUsageIndexLoader and its own rows without App/Family Mapping imports or row locks. App PageActivationWorkflow suppresses live-plan updates across loading, reconciliation, and indicators, then refreshes locks and cache state after suppression. Shared Parameters and UI execution Shared Parameters owns domain values, authoring, formulas, Revit adapters, rows, tree, views, and pane state. SharedParameterDuplicateReconciler owns stateful duplicate-row mutation and reentrancy. SharedParameterConflictProjector performs stateless tree/Commit Review projection. Map From reads numeric formula inputs at the Revit boundary. The preview evaluator does not parse displayed parameter text. Measured values use Revit's display unit. Preview output uses 15 significant digits. Numeric preview accepts signed/unsigned E/e exponents, including substituted invariant G15 values. Unresolved identifiers/functions produce preview-unavailable. Revit still validates authored formulas. Formula mode returns zero from the value copier without target resolution or writes. The embed applier counts authored formulas separately from value updates: one formula has authored=1, updated=0, affected=1. MapFrom retains copied-value counts. Detached Usage selection-preview and authoring property notifications use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync. The shared boundary owns logging/banners without rethrowing into WPF dispatch. Shared-parameter group/category/authoring work and contested overlay admission retain the UI context before collection mutation. Preview failures propagate to their owning command/tree-selection boundary for one report. Commit Review planning and continuation Commit Review planning resolves names, builds planning state, loads parameter groups, and prepares rows/usage inside one ISessionOperationGate operation. Collaborators do not reacquire that non-reentrant gate. The gate releases before the review dialog opens. Refresh takes a separate operation. Planning cancellation remains control flow. Other faults can produce invalid-plan state. Commit Review receives closing state and MappingSessionContext with IWorkspaceState rather than mutable App state. Planning/DocumentEdit owns mutable batch assembly. Report/OperationRows/OperationRowProjector produces family, pending, result, and error rows. Workflow owns apply/finalization. Revit/CommitReviewSessionFactory composes the child scope, planning, transaction groups, and modal presenter through the bound document gate. CommitReviewRowServices is feature-owned and constructed by App's row composition. Commit continuation uses ICommitReviewRowRefresh, implemented by CrossPaneRowRefresh. It returns Refreshed, Canceled, or NoSelectedCategory. Only a successful family scan proceeds to usage preparation, family reconciliation, and row locks. Canceled stops through cancellation. NoSelectedCategory skips refresh without a success log. Committed mappings remain persisted in either case. The refresh workflow consumes ISessionOperationGate for busy state. Commit-and-continue invalidates authoring snapshots, duplicates, and cached family views before rescanning. Returned outcomes rebuild the applied Shared Parameters tree. A successful continuation rescans Duplicates immediately when that page is active. View operations and catalogs ViewOps owns navigation. A positive missing element ID returns false without changing view or selection. Nonpositive IDs are argument errors. Unexpected Revit faults propagate. Previews owns cross-feature material/style catalogs and preview values. Line-style eligibility The shared line-style query checks the capability required by Revit commit. A grouped curve is restylable only when its group and every enclosing group have exactly one placed instance of their type. Attached detail groups also check their parent model group. Multi-instance groups are excluded before capture with their type name, placed count and Edit Group reason. GM never enters Edit Group mode and never ungroups elements. A style used only by those excluded members has no selectable source targets, even when the style remains available as a target for other sources. The writer captures every pair's population before the first pair mutates the document. Curves with no alternate Lines projection style, no resolvable projection or a non-Lines current style are also excluded. The query retains scalar curve IDs and per-source target intersections for restylable curves. It does not retain Revit wrappers for excluded members, and readback never revisits them. Each successful pair's affected count equals its pre-apply Usage quantity. A defensive group-edit failure at commit rolls back only that pair and surfaces the reason. Workflows Session operations and shutdown Domain/SessionOperation/ISessionOperationGate exposes serialized work, overlay progress, busy state, and UI cancellation. App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate implements admission and cancel-and-drain. MappingUpdateSuppression separately controls nested live-plan suppression. SessionOperationProgress carries operation progress or the Hidden no-display value. The Domain/Workspace IWorkspaceSignals port carries feature requests for whole-window refresh. App/Sessions/WorkspaceSignals implements that port, alongside WorkspaceState implementing IWorkspaceState. An operation failure remains primary. Caller cancellation propagated through the linked work token is translated back to the caller token. Teardown independently attempts stopped-step logging, busy-state reset, and busy-text reset. The resets run directly or in one dispatcher call. An aborted or unscheduled dispatcher call produces one teardown failure. The linked cancellation source is always released. One failure propagates unchanged. Multiple failures aggregate in primary-first order with contextual teardown wrappers. A failing StateChanged subscriber cannot hide the work failure or skip the other reset. BackgroundPrewarm and OptionRenderingRefresh retain their transitive task and cancellation source. Replacement cancels and drains the active pair before starting the next. The session refuses ordinary close while Commit Review or Type Mapping owns an interaction. The first admitted close publishes closing state, cancels Mapping/startup, observes startup, and retains one terminal shutdown task. Repeated closes join that completion. The shutdown workflow independently attempts prewarm drain, option-rendering drain, confirmed preference-clear drain, session-operation cancel-and-drain, close persistence, and synchronous graph disposal, in that order. It then issues one terminal Close. Closed performs idempotent view-model cleanup and App run-scope disposal. Failures retain lifecycle order and do not skip later cleanup. Pane and scope collaborators remain alive until running work drains. Dev Mode retirement is synchronous and requires Idle for immediate collection. Commit Review reports Busy, so reload waits for Keep, Roll back, X, or cancellation followed by close. Revit shutdown can force ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll. Retirement diagnoses pending work, aborts owned dispatcher operations, cancels without draining, rolls back an open apply group through the inline commit gate, disposes child/session scopes, and skips close persistence with a log entry. It opens no dispatcher frame. An existing normal-close task stops before its next stage when retirement takes over. DevModeStatus exposes Idle or Busy: <operations> in the root UI Automation ItemStatus. It includes name lookup, navigation, both auto-zoom debounces, duplicate rebuilds, Type Mapping, Commit Review, cache posts, and pending page selection. App, Family Mapping, and Shared Parameters navigation use Mapping-owned NavigationLifetime leases. Leases start inside admitted callbacks or around awaited execution. Both feature auto-zoom debounces use 200 ms and the lease token. Disposal cancels outside the lifetime lock and prevents later selection, activation, or zoom. Core alerts use observed nested modal loops and diagnose reload during a dialog. Mapping execution RevitMappingPlanExecutor validates document identity and supplies document operations to MappingPlanExecutor. MappingPlanExecutor owns the stage loop, capture boundaries, and result builder. Result accounting The MappingApplyResult constructor validates and snapshots recorded operation results. Succeeded operations require positive affected counts. Skips require zero. Failed operations can retain counts for writes completed before failure. Root succeeded/failed/skipped and affected totals derive from one recorded-result snapshot. Caller collections cannot mutate the completed result. Family success requires changed work and a successful reload. Failed-rule totals and fatal operation diagnostics must agree. Exception-backed diagnostics retain the original exception internally. MappingApplyResultBuilder logs each exception reference once with operation context. Commit Review receives stable operation text, codes, IDs, and family context. Exception types, messages, and stacks stay in logs. Writer exceptions are attributed to every unrecorded operation owned by that writer. Family cleanup always attempts close and retains close diagnostics after primary errors. Cancellation plus cleanup failures propagate primary-first through family-batch and outer writer containment. Skipped group-owned references produce Mapping warnings. An Edit Group restriction rejecting a line-style transaction at commit fails that pair. Successful sibling results retain their affected counts, but Commit Review rolls back an attempt with fatal mapping diagnostics. Writer failures A writer exception after all owned operations are recorded is a workflow failure. The result builder logs writer/stage context once and rethrows the original exception with its stack. Recorded operations alone cannot produce a successful final result in this case. With unrecorded owned operations, the executor records their failures and continues to later writers. Population capture Replacement capture precedes the first mutation that can change its population. ApplyContext captures the original symbol populations, target occupancy and type-parameter source values before the writer loop. Host material references are captured at the fixed boundary after Host recreation and before Nested Families or Type Replacements, including plans with no Host operations. They refer to recreated element IDs without consuming values introduced by later type-parameter migration or family reloads. Each family document captures all applicable material, object-style and nested-symbol references before its operation loop. Missing sources are explicit capture results. An absent source in a traversed family is zero work with a non-fatal reason. A missing host source or an ambiguous family material name remains an error. Apply never discovers an incoming population. Family material capture includes writable type parameters and the per-type defaults of instance material parameters. Revit does not allow formulas on Material data type parameters. Formula-determined parameters are outside this material replacement population. Reference kinds are explicit. Blank type names are valid and match ordinally. Capture does not change FamilyManager.CurrentType. Transactional apply restores the captured type. Object-style capture identifies the actual subcategory parameter or boundary curves of each filled region. Family-owned execution uses BatchOperationSet keyed by MappingOperation.OperationId and FamilyBatchResult.ResultsByOperationId. Style and prepared-material payloads use the same IDs. Nested, style, material, and embed dispatch uses canonical operation types and direct appliers. Intermediate counts must be nonnegative, and succeeded plus failed documents cannot exceed attempted. Invalid producer output fails validation. Family document lifetime Family-owned batch execution discovers the complete applicable family tree and captures each original population before applying any family mutation. FamilyBatchDocuments retains one edit document for each family identity through capture, apply, and reload. Discovery spans the whole commit. After discovery, documents with no applicable work in themselves or their descendants are closed before apply. Remaining documents close after their last root-batch use. Final cleanup closes anything left, including after cancellation. Each release closes in reverse open order and reports individual close failures. Discovery logs the peak and retained counts and reports progress per root. Cleanup uses the underlying Revit gate without requiring the launch document to remain active or the work token to remain uncanceled. EditFamily creates independent copies, so no captured element key is carried into a second edit session. Family element references use UniqueId within their retained document plus parameter identity. Family type references use explicit reference kind, family type name, and family parameter name. Built-in parameter identity uses the typed Revit enum without narrowing its underlying 64-bit value. Document-local ElementId values remain diagnostics and population indexes only. Missing keys produce a diagnostic and do not trigger a live rescan. Shared family identity and reload Shared nested families use a name/category identity. Nonshared copies include their embedding path. Discovery opens the project's shared definition when one exists, so a parent's stale embedded copy cannot become the original population for another root. If the same shared family is reached through several roots, applicable operation populations are merged and each normalized operation is applied once. An equivalent alias receives a merged notice. If its representative fails, the alias is reported as failed as well. Conflicting targets for the same source fail preflight. After a nested or root reload, the load allowlist selects FamilySource.Family only for shared identities changed by that target traversal. Unchanged shared children use FamilySource.Project, which preserves the target document's existing child instead of reloading a stale source copy. Parent material capture excludes shared-symbol projections: the child owns those values and only surviving writes count. Before reload, project-owned shared material projections are restored from the target document explicitly. Revit can otherwise propagate those type values even when the shared-family load callback selects Project. Nonshared symbol overrides remain part of the parent population. Family results Family-document success requires both changed work and a successful reload. A failed family traversal or reload marks every operation actually executed in that traversal as failed, including merged aliases. An affected count can show writes made before the failure. The original exception remains attached to the diagnostic for logging and review. Family-document attempt/success/failure counts include every examined root and child document, including zero-work captures. A reload or close failure keeps the completed affected counts and marks the affected document operation results failed. Material projection ownership A parent FamilySymbol's material type value is a projection of the child's authored FamilyType value. When that child has the same planned material operation, the child owns the write and its count. For nonshared children, root-only operations and traversal-depth leaves retain their parent-side references. Shared projections are always child-owned. Missing captured host references produce a nonfatal diagnostic. Line-style verification Line-style query snapshots retain curve IDs and per-source offered intersections, not Revit element wrappers or target sets per curve. A line-style apply performs one fresh discovery sweep, then verifies actual styles by reading the captured IDs. Complete original-source intersections are regrouped under the final source styles. Unexpected population splits or missing curves fail verification for the committed pairs. Their operation results retain the committed affected counts, and the writer returns the errors instead of throwing away those operation results. Commit Review and the subsequent accepted Usage refresh share this result. A rollback does not publish it. CommitReviewLineStyleLifecycle exports it once, and only while the session's query cache still holds the snapshot that was current when post-apply verification succeeded. Explicit Detect and Usage refresh boundaries invalidate prior snapshots. Object-style attribution identifies the family returned by LoadFamily, its retained name, and its ownership of original instances. Style availability depends on the family category and kind. Post-apply verification Commit Review checks operation identity and successful operation results for all replacement kinds, including runtime replacements created by Create Type. Symbol and line-style counts can be checked against incoming populations. Family material and object-style Usage count families while operation results count references. An overlapping successful target is therefore checked through its operation result and writer readback, not by equating those different quantities. Commit Review results and finalization Result Contract Completed Requires MappingApplyResult and derives success from Outcome Canceled Contains neither Mapping result nor failure prose WorkflowFailed Requires a nonblank reason. Can retain a rolled-back Mapping result for diagnostics Warnings can complete successfully and remain committable. Only positive succeeded operations without fatal diagnostics project applied or persistable intent. Verification requires no planned type, host, style, or material source references to remain. Otherwise the verifier's four-field failure summary blocks mapping projection. One Global Mapper: Apply session group stays open through modal review. Apply and Retry Apply execute and verify inside an inner attempt group. Failure or cancellation rolls back the attempt and permits retry. Retry reuses the reviewed plan but constructs a new apply context and rereads the document. Keep + Continue and Keep + Close GM assimilate the session group into one Undo entry before recording mappings. Roll back, X's rollback answer, cancellation, and abnormal exit roll it back. An unknown rollback outcome propagates to the error banner rather than asserting that nothing was kept. Active-view refresh follows successful verification. A refresh warning does not disable Keep. After review closes, RefreshAfterReviewAsync refreshes GM after any admitted attempt, including failed or rolled-back attempts. Type replacements retain their selecting intent key, so acceptance records intent for its actual owner. Apply transactions log each Revit failure at Warning with definition ID and failing elements. Pre-commit issues retain their validation label. Family-document material replacement resolves source and target by material name. Errors retain planned operation ID and host source/target IDs. Family-document material IDs and affected elements are diagnostic details. Report grouping uses the owning operation even when operations share a host pair or family documents assign different IDs. Reloaded family identity Family-owned apply retains the family ID returned by Revit reload. Accepted mappings use that identity, including existing saved and pending mappings for the same family. Rollback leaves mapping identities unchanged. MappingApplyResult.ReloadedFamilyIds snapshots changed root identities. Finalization remaps applied/persistable family keys and targets before merging. MappingIntentStore also remaps existing saved/pending intents, manual family-apply state, and usage links. One replaced identity must not retain a second saved mapping. Host replacement Each host replacement is atomic per instance. Placement and required facing, hand, and point-rotation transfer must finish before source deletion. Ordinary parameter copies use best-effort transfer. A failed replacement becomes an item error only after its subtransaction reports a completed rollback. If rollback throws or reports any other status, the primary and rollback failures escape together so the enclosing transaction aborts instead of committing an uncertain document state. ParameterValueTransfer reads the target after Parameter.Set returns false. It accepts the copy as a no-op only when its storage type and value exactly match the requested source value. It applies no numeric tolerance to Double values. A remaining mismatch becomes a nonfatal HostParameterCopyWarning with the source instance, parameter, and reason. Setter exceptions remain failures. These warnings appear only after the replacement subtransaction commits. A later required-state failure rolls back and retains the fatal replacement error. Commit Review preserves each distinct diagnostic, opens the operation diagnostics section, and reports Completed with Warnings. It counts nonfatal diagnostics. Within each diagnostic-code group, it includes distinct messages in first-seen order. Code groups sort by descending diagnostic count, then by code ignoring case. Host parameter transfer treats a writable instance Phase Created value as instance-owned even when the family symbol exposes the same built-in parameter ID. The type-bound rule excludes generated IfcGUID. Revit read scheduling GmSessionDocumentGate validates Action callbacks as synchronous before wrapping their launch-document check. It rejects async void before Core can see only the synchronous decorator. Generic results also undergo synchronous-result validation. Independent reads for one action start together. Startup waits for every family-category, shared-parameter-category, and parameter-group read to settle. Ordinary startup faults take priority over cancellation. Aggregate faults contribute their non-cancellation leaves recursively. A single ordinary fault keeps its identity and stack. Multiple ordinary faults form an aggregate in family-category, shared-parameter-category, then parameter-group order, regardless of completion order. Other exception wrappers keep their context. With cancellation alone, the first cancellation in that order keeps its token. Family expansion starts view and parameter-name reads together and awaits them in original order, so the first read's failure or cancellation remains primary. Selected-type instance examples are read once through type selection. Core's queued-turn policy determines which waiting calls share a callback. Testing See Global Mapper testing for fixture ownership, hidden-desktop dialog hosting, model baselines, and run commands. Limitations Family-tree discovery retains edit documents through capture and applicable writes, so peak open-document count grows with the discovered tree. Grouped curves are eligible only when each enclosing group type has one placed instance. Family-document material replacement resolves by name, not host numeric ID.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper (GM) Overview Global Mapper finds duplicate or related Revit content, captures mapping intent, and previews and applies replacements through Commit Review. Its main window is modeless. Commit Review is modal and keeps a reversible apply group open until the user keeps or rolls back changes. The architecture specification defines state, capture, execution, and lifetime contracts. The user guide describes mapping workflows. Architecture Source and registration Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.GM. manifest.yml registers: Surface Value Module DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmToolModule Command and availability DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmCommand Run profile QueuedModeless Ribbon Common panel, Global Mapper, order 30, icon key gm Main raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmWindow.xaml, Modeless Commit Review raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmCommitReviewWindow.xaml, Modal Sandbox uses internal design-time view models with public binding properties: DBTools.GM.App.DesignTime.GmWindowDesignTimeViewModel and DBTools.GM.Features.CommitReview.DesignTime.GmCommitReviewWindowDesignTimeViewModel. Generated src/Tools/Common/GM/MAP.md indexes source files and manifest values. Ownership Owner Responsibility App/Composition Service registration, session and row graph construction App/Sessions Workspace implementations, attachment, close, shutdown, modeless lifetime App/Startup, App/Navigation Initialization, page activation, prewarm, pending navigation App/Persistence, App/State UI-state sequencing and feature-to-domain state construction Domain Project state, identity, element names, parameters, categories, workspace, cache and operation contracts Features/Categories Curated categories Features/Families Family inventory and document lifecycle Features/FamilyMapping Family/type rows, nested usage, scan, selection, and type creation Features/Mapping Intent, row-to-intent translation, conflicts, plans, and replacement execution Features/CommitReview Review planning, modal workflow, reports, verification, finalization, refresh port Features/DeepScan Family scanning, completeness, cache, hydration, refresh Features/Duplicates Detection, matching, selections, tree, and type mapping Features/Usage Indexing, options, matching, preview, selection, and usage rows Features/SharedParameters Authoring, formulas, parameter operations, rows, and tree Features/Similarity Name scoring and score presentation Features/Previews Material/style catalogs and preview values Features/SavedMappings Strict persistence envelope, clear, and reapply Features/ViewOps View and element navigation Revit Tool-wide document and name adapters Feature packages own their local domain, planning, execution, Revit, views, and workflow where present. App composes cross-feature sequences through feature-owned ports. Features do not import App. WPF presentation GmWindowPresenter loads App/Views/GmWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. Its binding source is App/ViewModels/GmWindowViewModel. Commit Review binds to Features/CommitReview/ViewModels/GmCommitReviewWindowViewModel. The runtime and design-time view models expose raw fragment bytes for six feature panes. Stable GmRawViewConverter parses those fragments. OneTime fragment bindings use the nearest categoryTabs ancestor. The host assigns shell and raw-root DataContext synchronously before the first dispatcher pump, so the first DataBind/layout pass can materialize each pane. OneTime retains it across tab switches. Feature panes bind to their feature view models. Parent commands, category selection, and empty-state labels address the shell DataContext. Stable WPF registrations, controls, converters, selectors, attached behaviors, and shared resources live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/GM/, namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.GM. Each raw view merges Presentation’s Resources/Theme.xaml and references stable dictionaries with versioned ResourceUri values. GmViewResources.xaml owns Mapping and Similarity styles without a second theme merge. Payload views have no code-behind, dependency properties, or implicit payload-type templates. Bindings use INotifyPropertyChanged sources or OneTime for immutable values. Raw templates use string keys with explicit fallbacks. GmViewXaml exposes embedded bytes for raw-XAML tests and hosted views. App Pure reads the GM assembly's fixed logical resources directly. Commit Review owns one Revit callback around planning, ShowDialog, finalization, and refresh. Core WindowOwnerModalityScope disables Revit and other top-level windows through that callback and restores only the windows it disabled. During planning, the GM owner remains available for its overlay and Cancel action. ShowDialog disables that owner while the review dialog is visible. User close returns the session finalization. Forced retirement returns none. IsRetired is true for both outcomes and cannot distinguish them. Keep triggered from WPF Closing queues the final Close because WPF rejects reentrant Close there. Duplicate Type Mapping uses a registered modeless shell owned by GM, with Manual startup and a taskbar entry. Commit Review also retains Manual startup, an explicit finalization decision, and a cleanup close gate. Cleanup requests cancellation, waits for a safe rollback boundary, and propagates cancellation, timeout, or rollback failures. A failed cleanup leaves the review window open. Row refresh and owner closure follow successful cleanup. Design-time shared-parameter composition uses the production feature/projection graph with explicit host replacements, including NoopFamilyParameterQuery. Authoring receives a registered parameter-signature provider. Data and contracts The architecture specification defines project state, mapping intent, persistence, and execution results. Workflows Startup performance Startup logs Information-level elapsed time for five overlay steps. Usage indexing logs each catalog/index source duration and completion state. Failure or cancellation records the interrupted step and elapsed time, including queued Revit-call time. Overlay visibility is not the timing source. Family population counts use one symbol-count sweep. Type IDs retain collector order and cache per project state. View-owned collection discovers owner IDs through a quick filter, then visits eligible owners with instances, retaining Revit view-visibility filtering. Style/material indexing share one capped sample and 25-instance chunks with separate geometry options. Family-dependent styles are visited once per usage build. Each option-building pass owns immutable name profiles and retains numeric-suffix and multiset-bigram scoring. Testing Pure tests mirror App, Domain, and Features owners. Test builders, external fakes, and assertions live in Tests/Support. Project-state and name-cache tests live under Tests/Domain. Duplicate projection tests live under Tests/Features/Duplicates. The root Revit name adapter mirrors its complete path at Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQueryTests.cs. CommitReviewPlanContextTests mirrors Features/CommitReview/Planning. Saved mappings, authoring, and usage matching also mirror their subjects. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSessionTests.cs launches the production session through its queued App run scope and GmWindowViewModelBuilder. It observes the raw view in the stable shell on the dispatcher. Normal-close tests overlap close requests and await shared completion, shutdown, one Closed event, cleanup, and scope disposal. Retirement tests wait for Idle, retire synchronously, and check collection without another dispatcher pump. ForcedRetirement_AfterApply_RollsBackTheOpenGroupAndReturnsWithoutHanging retires after a real apply and checks model restoration and group finalization before child-scope disposal in the same Revit turn. Revit-hosted Commit Review tests use testing/TestSupport/GM/Fakes/HiddenCommitReviewDialogHost in place of ShowDialog to satisfy hidden-desktop window ownership. Its dispatcher frame ends on retirement. IToolWindowSession.Closed does not complete after forced retirement, so awaiting that event would retain the Revit callback until timeout. A 60-second deadline retires a session left open and fails the test. GM Revit-hosted fixture models, named views, family symbols, line styles, materials, and expected production outcomes are required repository baselines. Missing baselines and false production results fail with the model path and running year. Fixture teardown and transaction-group finalization failures also fail and are aggregated with a primary test failure when both occur. DBTools.GM.Pure.Tests.csproj contains owner-local fixtures and shared test support and references the desktop DBTools.GM.csproj. The production assembly grants the Pure assembly internal access. Revit references are compile-only; loading a Revit-typed member requires a Revit host. Run the supported gates through the repository wrappers: ./build.sh BuildApp ./build.sh BuildTests ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 The Pure project targets net10.0-windows and requires Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App. Revit-hosted tests use the local scope through the daemon fleet. Limitations The session key uses the document hash code, which can collide. The specification describes family-document and line-style limits.

developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) Overview Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) copies drafting views between the active Revit document and a library .rvt file. Teams keep standard drafting views in the library and import them into projects. Export to Library copies drafting views from the active document to a library file. Import from Library copies drafting views from a library file to the active document. For a workshared library, TDV creates a local copy, and after an export it synchronizes the changes with central. Architecture Project structure src/Tools/Common/TDV/ ├── App/ │ ├── Composition/ # TdvToolModule, commands, AddTdv() │ ├── DesignTime/ │ ├── Persistence/ # CachePaths │ ├── Sessions/ # WindowSession, WindowSessionDialogRunner │ ├── ViewModels/ # TdvWindowViewModel partials │ └── Views/ # TdvWindow.xaml ├── Assets/ ├── Features/ │ ├── Library/{Domain,Operations,Settings,Workflow} │ ├── Preview/{Operations,State} │ └── Transfer/{Domain,Execution,Operations,ViewModels,Workflow} ├── Tests/ # DBTools.TDV.Pure.Tests, DBTools.TDV.Local.Tests ├── DBTools.TDV.csproj └── manifest.yml App/Composition holds the manifest entry points and DI. App/Sessions/WindowSession creates a registered stable modal shell through Core's ToolWindowFactory and owns the owner provider, logger display, alerts, banners, initial load, cleanup on close and result projection. WindowSessionDialogRunner owns the modal-loop result and retirement. App/Views/TdvWindow.xaml is embedded raw XAML with the header, grid, preview and actions sections inline. The library settings view (Features/Library/Settings/Views/LibrarySettingsView.xaml) is also raw XAML, loaded with ToolWindowXaml.LoadElement. Both resources have explicit logical names and contain only stable or framework WPF types. TdvWindowViewModel is the App orchestration edge. CachePaths supplies cache roots to the Library and Preview features. Transfer is one Revit-facing service split over partial files: shared guards (Transfer.cs), catalog queries (Transfer.Queries.cs), apply-selection orchestration (Transfer.ApplySelection.cs), per-row steps (Transfer.Execution.cs) and per-run accounting (Transfer.RunState.cs). The run state holds duplicate destination names, deferred successes, cancellation, rollback and unknown-finalization reporting and the final TransferResult. The split adds no service or transaction boundary. The drafting-view operations are in Features/Transfer/Operations/DraftingView: DraftingViewReader (enumeration and name lookup), DraftingViewTypeResolver (type lookup and creation of missing destination types) and DraftingViewWriter (create, copy, clear and overrides). Features/Preview/Operations/PreviewExporter and PreviewImageExporter export previews. TransferSession binds one Transfer to a destination and source document for the window. Transfer commands are split by direction. ExportTransferWorkflow and ImportTransferWorkflow make the document and outcome decisions of their direction.
