LibraryTransferWorkflow owns catalog selection, library open, close warnings and host reactivation. The Library workflow uses the ILibrarySelectionDialog port; the Transfer workflows use the ITransferDialog port. WindowSession implements both: it presents library selection, loads the embedded TDV view, shows the shell modally with the application IWindowOwnerHandleProvider and projects the window counts and errors into TransferDialogResult. LibraryDocumentService does the Revit document open, save, sync and close calls; LibraryCatalog validates library paths from the current settings snapshot. Service registration TdvToolModule registers the services through ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddTdv(). Registrations are scoped because they depend on run-scope services (IRevitCallGate, ITransactionRunner). The composition root supplies the current Revit year and the library-file year probe. services.AddScoped<Transfer>(sp => new Transfer(gate, tx, logger)); services.AddScoped<Func<LibraryCatalog>>(sp => () => new LibraryCatalog( settings.Get(settingsSection).Files.ToList(), RevitInstanceIdentity.RevitYear, RevitYearProbe.Probe)); services.AddScoped<LibraryDocumentService>(sp => new LibraryDocumentService(gate, logger, CachePaths.LibraryLocalsRoot, RevitInstanceIdentity.RevitYear, RevitYearProbe.Probe)); services.AddScoped<WindowSession>(sp => new WindowSession(transfer, alerts, loggerFactory, loggerWindowHost, ownerHandleProvider, windowFactory)); services.AddScoped<ILibrarySelectionDialog>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<WindowSession>()); services.AddScoped<ITransferDialog>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<WindowSession>()); // LibraryTransferWorkflow, ExportTransferWorkflow and ImportTransferWorkflow follow. Service Purpose Transfer Revit transfer operations and catalog queries LibraryCatalog Library path validation from a snapshot of library entries LibraryDocumentService Library document open, save, sync, close and host reactivation, with an App-supplied cache root ILibrarySelectionDialog Port for library selection (Library feature) ITransferDialog Port for the modal transfer window and its result (Transfer feature) WindowSession Implementation of both ports: owner reuse, modal window lifetime and result projection LibraryTransferWorkflow Catalog selection, library open, document cleanup and host reactivation Transfer methods Method Description BuildViewItemsAsync(destination, source, ct) Collects the drafting views of the source document. ApplySelectionAsync(TransferRequest) Runs the transfer in one continuous Revit API callback. WouldConflictAsync(destination, name, replace, ct) Checks a destination name for a conflict. ExportPreviewAsync(source, sourceViewId, tempDir, ct) Exports a preview image of a view. Manifest id: DBTools.TDV assembly: DBTools.TDV moduleType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvToolModule order: 0 panel: Common sandboxWindows: - id: DBTools.TDV.Main displayName: "Transfer Drafting Views" group: "Common" xamlResource: "DBTools.ToolViews.TDV.TdvWindow.xaml" windowKind: Modal width: 1400 height: 700 minWidth: 1200 minHeight: 600 showInTaskbar: true startupLocation: CenterScreen designTimeViewModelType: "DBTools.TDV.App.DesignTime.TdvWindowDesignTimeViewModel" designTimeViewModelAssembly: "DBTools.TDV" designTimeViewModelVisibility: Public tool: settings: configSection: Core.MasterLibrary settingsPacks: - key: core.library title: "Library Files" warnings: - id: core.library.invalid title: "Library Paths Invalid" message: "One or more saved library file paths are invalid. Fix the paths and save the settings to re-enable import/export." disableTools: - DBTools.ExportToLibrary - DBTools.ImportFromLibrary ribbonTools: - internalName: DBTools.ExportToLibrary commandType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvExportCommand availabilityType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvExportCommand runProfile: InlineUi displayText: "Export\nTo Library" iconBaseKey: export tooltip: "Export drafting views to the library" controlKind: StackedButtonItem splitGroup: library_transfer order: 0 - internalName: DBTools.ImportFromLibrary commandType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvImportCommand availabilityType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvImportCommand runProfile: InlineUi displayText: "Import\nFrom Library" iconBaseKey: import tooltip: "Import drafting views from the library" controlKind: StackedButtonItem splitGroup: library_transfer order: 1 Data and contracts Capabilities Import and export of drafting views, several views in one batch. View type mapping: each row selects a destination drafting view type, or Retain Original. Conflict detection while editing: names that exist in the destination, and duplicate destination names in the current selection. Replace mode for views with the same name. A preview of the selected view, with pan and zoom. One destination transaction group per batch, bound to the explicit destination document (also a non-active library). Per-view progress during transfer. Callback requirement Transfer.ApplySelectionAsync must start inside an active Revit API callback, and the supplied call gate and transaction runner must keep the whole transfer in that callback. Before it reads a document or starts the destination group, it throws OperationCanceledException if the request token is canceled and InvalidOperationException ("TDV transfer requires one continuous Revit API callback.") if RevitCallGateApiContext.IsActive is false. Both ribbon commands use the InlineUi profile. The query methods (BuildViewItemsAsync, WouldConflictAsync, ExportPreviewAsync) can each queue as one complete operation. ApplySelectionAsync also checks that the source and destination are valid, open documents and not the same document. The run-start log entry contains a run ID and the title and path of the source and destination. Destination names TDV does not add suffixes to destination names. A row fails when its destination name is blank (DestinationNameRequired), exists in the destination while Replace is off (DestinationNameConflict), or duplicates the destination name of another selected row (DuplicateTargetName). View types The row View Type list contains the drafting view types of the destination: the host document for an import, the library document for an export. Retain Original resolves to the drafting type name of the source view. If the destination has no type with that name, TDV duplicates an existing destination drafting ViewFamilyType and gives the duplicate that name. If the source type name cannot be read, the row fails with SourceTypeNameUnavailable. Settings Library options The Core.MasterLibrary section stores LibraryOptions: public sealed class LibraryOptions { public IList<LibraryFile> Files { get; set; } = new List<LibraryFile>(); } public sealed class LibraryFile { public string? MainPath { get; set; } // primary library .rvt path public string? FallbackPath { get; set; } // alternative path, for example another network location public string? Alias { get; set; } // short name in the library picker } Settings pack LibrarySettingsContext gives the settings page a tree of library files with add and remove for files and fallback paths, path validation as the user edits, and pending-change tracking. The settings-pack factory receives the Revit year and year probe from the TDV composition root, so settings validation matches the runtime checks. LibraryTransferWorkflow receives a Func<LibraryCatalog> from the composition root and does not read the settings type. Each tree row shows a validation icon (green check or red error), a tooltip with the full path, and a short display text: the root, the file name and the last three folder levels. Path validation LibraryCatalog marks a path invalid, with a failure reason, when: the file does not exist (File not found); the extension is not .rvt (Not a .rvt file); the year probe cannot read the saved Revit version (the probe's failure reason; TDV logs the exception); the saved version differs from the session (Revit version mismatch (file: {0}, current: {1})). An invalid path raises the core.library.invalid settings warning, which disables both ribbon commands. Warnings are evaluated at startup, so the commands can be disabled as soon as Revit starts. LibraryDocumentService.OpenLibraryAsync checks the version again before it opens the file and throws InvalidOperationException ("Library file was saved in Revit {0} but the current session is Revit {1}. ...") on a mismatch. The command's ISafeExecutor boundary shows it as a banner. The check prevents two failures: for a workshared file, WorksharingUtils.CreateNewLocal() fails with a version error; for a non-workshared file, Revit upgrades the library file when it opens it. Open failures propagate through the import or export workflow to the command boundary; they are not treated as a canceled library selection. Errors Per-view error codes (TransferErrorCode) Code Description Unknown Unspecified error, or the finalization outcome is unknown DestinationTypeMissing Destination view type not found SourceTypeNameUnavailable Source view type name cannot be read CreateViewFailed Destination view could not be created or prepared CopyElementsFailed View elements could not be copied OverridesFailed Graphic overrides could not be copied ValidationFailed Row validation failed ClearDestinationViewFailed Contents of the existing destination view could not be cleared MetadataCopyFailed View scale or description could not be copied DestinationNameRequired Destination name is blank DuplicateTargetName Another selected row has the same destination name DestinationNameConflict Destination view exists and Replace is off TransactionRolledBack Revit discarded the attempted changes of the run Result reporting After each transfer, TDV shows: a banner on the TDV window (success or warning) with the selected, processed and result counts; a summary alert with the selected, processed, added, replaced, failed and not-attempted counts, a table of per-view issues when there are failures (rows can be copied to the clipboard), and the buttons Accept and Transfer More and Close Tool. TransferResult carries SelectedCount, ProcessedCount, Added, Replaced, FailedCount, UnprocessedCount, Cancelled, FinalizationOutcome (Unknown, Committed, RolledBack), Errors and ErrorDetails. AllChangesDiscarded is true only for RolledBack. Transfer logs include the identifiers and names of the selected views (a bounded list). Row state flows from Transfer to the row view models and XAML triggers as TransferRowState. TDV logs each per-view failure with its exception and records only the stable code and message in the row result. Success callbacks and committed add and replace counts are published only after a Committed outcome. A rollback marks attempted rows discarded. An unknown finalization sets the projected successes to zero, marks attempted rows failed with Unknown and reports that the destination state is not verified. Library close Save and sync always attempt to close the library document. Document.Close(...) == false is a failure of a required close. A single save, sync or close failure keeps its original exception. When the operation and the close both fail, TDV throws one ordered AggregateException with the operation failure first. Best-effort cleanup (TryCloseAsync) returns false only when Revit refuses to close the active document. Other cleanup failures propagate; after a failed export, TDV reports one ordered AggregateException with the export failure first and the cleanup failure second. Workflows Per-view steps For each selected row, TDV: validates the destination name before the transfer transaction; creates or prepares the destination view with the selected view type; copies the view scale and description parameters; copies the elements of the source view, except skipped categories; copies element graphic overrides from source to destination. If a step fails, the per-view transaction rolls back and the row is recorded as failed. DestinationTransactionGroup receives the destination Document at begin, rejects item and finalization calls for any other document and runs each item transaction against that document. Import (library to host) and export (host to a non-active library) therefore use the same real Revit group; the group is never resolved from ActiveUIDocument. It creates the Revit group through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin. Successful row states and the add and replace counts are held until the group reports Committed. A RolledBack outcome marks the attempted rows discarded. An unknown or failed finalization withholds success and claims neither commit nor rollback. Operation, finalization and disposal failures stay ordered in the logged exception chain; the row result keeps its stable per-view error code and message. Sources: src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Execution/{DestinationTransactionGroup,Transfer.ApplySelection,Transfer.RunState}.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Domain/TransferResult.cs. Copying view contents TDV collects the elements owned by the source view and copies them with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements and a UseDestinationTypesHandler (an IDuplicateTypeNamesHandler that keeps destination types when type names collide). Groups are copied before other elements; group members are paired with their copies so overrides apply to them. Skipped elements: viewports, elements whose category name is Title Blocks, Viewports, Views, Schedules or Guide Grids, and elements whose name contains ExtentElem. The category check compares English category names. Drafting views are collected with: new FilteredElementCollector(doc) .OfClass(typeof(View)) .WhereElementIsNotElementType() .Cast<View>() .Where(v => v.ViewType == ViewType.DraftingView && !v.IsTemplate) UI Main window (TdvWindow) The registered modal shell has the title "Transfer Drafting Views", an initial size of 1400 × 700, a minimum size of 1200 × 600, centered placement, a taskbar entry and a resizable layout. The Sandbox manifest declares the same dimensions, taskbar visibility and placement. The raw view has these sections: TransferHeaderView: conflict warning, type filter, search and separator. TransferGridView: the transfer grid and row visuals. TransferActionsView: status, selection and transfer actions, and errors. TransferPreviewView: the preview panel, cursor-relative wheel zoom, mouse panning, a zoom button and zoom on image update. The main view merges Presentation's theme once at its root; the library settings view merges its own. String item lists and tooltips use explicit text templates. Row-state triggers compare enum names as strings. PreviewZoomBehavior (Presentation) zooms on image update, deferred until layout. DBTools.Presentation.Tools.TDV.TdvPanZoomBehavior handles mouse pan and zoom and releases capture, cursor state and subscriptions on retirement. Window lifetime ProgressOverlay.For(session.Window) attaches after the view loads and before the dialog shows. The normal Closed notification clears UI actions, cancels outdated preview and conflict requests, disposes the view model and deletes its cache files. The host then retires the session and releases subscriptions, behavior state, the initializer, the overlay registration and the owner. Cleanup and the result depend on the Closed notification, also for a window closed before ShowDialog; an early normal close still allows library-document cleanup. Late callbacks and catalog results do not touch a disposed view model. A load failure after close shows no alert and logs no load error. If the load-error alert cannot be shown, the window still requests close. Dev Mode retirement logs a pending load, preview, conflict refresh or transfer instead of canceling it. Idle retirement is synchronous and does not pump the dispatcher. The library settings page uses stable tree selection and a focus-request counter. Selecting a main library entry whose alias is empty or whitespace focuses and selects the alias text at Background priority. Entries with an alias, and fallback entries, do not take focus. TdvWindowViewModel Property Type Description Items ObservableCollection<TransferRowViewModel> Filtered rows ViewTypeFilters ObservableCollection<string> View type filter values Search string Search text SelectedViewTypeFilter string Selected view type filter SelectedItem TransferRowViewModel? Selected row PreviewSource ImageSource? Preview image PreviewPlaceholderText string Text shown when there is no preview HasAnyConflict bool A row has a naming conflict Status string Status text (Selected: 0 | Replace: 0 | Adds: 0) AddedCount, ReplacedCount int Result counts Errors ObservableCollection<string> Result messages Command Description ApplySelectionCommand Runs the transfer. Enabled when a row is checked and no checked row has a conflict. ClearSelectedCommand Clears all checks. ClearSearchCommand Clears the search text. TransferRowViewModel Property Type Description SourceViewId long Revit element ID of the source view ViewName string Editable destination name ViewType string Selected destination type; an empty value selects the first available type ViewTypeName string Source type name AvailableViewTypes ObservableCollection<string> Destination drafting view types Checked bool Selected for transfer Replace bool Replace a view with the same name HasConflict bool Naming conflict HasTypeWarning bool Source type unavailable RowState TransferRowState Pending, Success, Failure or Conflict The row view model has no Revit or WPF visibility types. TransferProjector owns conflict refresh (duplicate and blank names) and projects transfer results onto rows. The designer uses its own design-time row type (DesignViewItem) with the same binding shape and does not reference the production row or domain types. Preview Loading is debounced by 200 ms. PreviewCache keeps up to 32 exported images in first-in-first-out order; a cache hit does not refresh its position. Zoom Extents fits and centers the image in the viewport. Exports are cropped to the non-background pixels, so extents-based zoom targets the real content. The background is RGB 43, 44, 61. The placeholder text distinguishes "no row selected" from "preview export failed". Each debounced request owns one cancellation source. Every result (image, unavailable, exception) checks that token and the request sequence before it publishes, so a superseded request can log its fault but cannot replace the latest preview. Expected cancellation logs no stack trace. Source: src/Tools/Common/TDV/App/ViewModels/TdvWindowViewModel.Preview.cs. Cache locations Transient files are under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\TDV\ (AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("TDV")): LibraryLocals\: workshared local copies, one per operation, deleted after the operation closes the library document. Preview\: preview images of one window. Command flows The library picker is an alert sized 520 × 420 (minimum 480 × 340). Each entry shows <name> - <path>: the name is the alias, or the file name up to the first _R (LibraryCatalog.TrimLibraryName) when there is no alias, and the path is shortened to its last two folders (LibraryPathFormatter.FormatPath). When some configured paths are invalid, the message reports how many. TDV opens library files with Application.OpenDocumentFile(...), without activating them, so the host model stays active during transfer and cleanup. Export Check that library paths are configured. Select a library file. For a workshared library, create a local copy under LibraryLocals\. Open the library document. Show the TDV modal session for view selection and run the transfer to the library. If views were added or replaced: for a workshared library, synchronize with central with the comment DB TOOLS - ADDED [n] DETAILS AND REPLACED [n] DETAILS. and close; otherwise save and close. If nothing changed, close without saving. Reactivate the original document. Show a warning only when Revit refuses to close the library because it is active. Any other close failure propagates, so an export is never reported as successful after a required close failed. Import Check that library paths are configured. Select a library file. For a workshared library, create a local copy under LibraryLocals\. Open the library document. Show the TDV modal session for view selection and run the transfer to the active document. Close the library without saving. Show a cleanup warning if the library document could not be closed. Testing DBTools.TDV.Pure.Tests and DBTools.TDV.Local.Tests cover, among others: TransferRowViewModelTests, TransferProjectorTests: row state, duplicate and blank names, and result projection. LibraryCatalogTests: path validation and catalog projection. TransferTests and the Transfer fixture in Transfer.ExecutionTests.cs: Revit-hosted transfers between source and destination documents. The Transfer fixture in Transfer.ApplySelectionTests.cs: Revit-hosted admission tests with real scopes, gates, transaction runners and destination groups: an off-thread call with an inherited API context, a canceled request, and a drafting-view transfer between two models. LibraryDocumentServiceTests: Revit-hosted document lifecycle: non-workshared library open, rejection of a Revit-year mismatch (through the injected year probe), aggregation of save-and-close failures, refusal to close the active library, and host reactivation. The workshared round-trip fixture creates a temporary central model, opens a local workspace, creates a drafting view, calls SyncAndCloseAsync, reopens the central through the service, checks the saved view, and verifies local-workspace removal. Non-workshared cases use temporary copies of test models. Limitations Library files must be saved in the running Revit year. Transfer requires one continuous Revit API callback and distinct open source and destination documents. Category exclusions compare English category names. Destination-name conflicts require a rename or Replace; TDV does not allocate suffixes. Architecture Overview DBTools.App Transfer Drafting Views (user guide)

developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft-.title: ERFT technical specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft-.summary: ERFT technical specification Overview The Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) calculates vertical offset changes for structural columns and beams against a triangulated floor or roof bottom surface. It modifies offset parameters, not level parameters. All lengths and coordinates in domain calculations use feet. Source: src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. See ERFT for composition, presentation ownership, and use. Architecture Selection and Planning prepare AdjustmentPlan; Execution writes offsets and Persistence stores the system. ERFT architecture lists owners and the preview host. Data and contracts Plan and identity Features/Domain/Adjustment/AdjustmentPlan contains: State Contents Target HostTargetId, LinkedTargetId, LinkInstanceId, TargetGeometry, TargetDisplayName Sources Lists of ColumnAdjustment and BeamAdjustment Hierarchy FramingGraph Rounding ToleranceFeet, default 1/48 ft. RoundingMode, default Nearest Profiles ProfilesByTypeId and ProfileExtractionFailuresByTypeId Storage SystemId, initialized from a GUID Revit element, type, level, link, and graph identities use long. Target IDs and connection IDs are nullable where absent. Mesh indices and counts use int. JSON numeric IDs in the 32-bit range deserialize as long. ColumnAdjustment retains element/type identity, type name, base/top points, original top offset, and top-level identity/name. Calculation supplies target elevation, raw delta, rounded delta, new offset, status, and optional error text. BeamAdjustment retains element/type identity, type name, endpoints, original endpoint offsets, and reference-level identity/name. Each endpoint has a Free, ToColumn, or ToBeam connection and optional owner ID. Calculation supplies endpoint target elevations, deltas, rounded deltas, new offsets, status, and optional error text. Hybrid means one ToColumn end and one ToBeam end. Statuses are Pending, NoChangeNeeded, and Error. RequiresModification requires Pending and a rounded delta magnitude greater than 1e-9 at an affected end. Plan pending counts include only rows requiring modification. A Pending row without a required write contributes to no-change counts. Target geometry Features/Operations/TargetGeometry/Revit/TargetGeometryReader resolves host or linked targets. A linked target uses RevitLinkInstance.GetTotalTransform and requires a loaded link document. Geometry extraction uses Medium detail and ComputeReferences = false. It traverses solids, triangulates faces, and retains separate bottom-surface and full-element meshes. A bottom face has host-transformed normal Z at most -0.1, sampled at the midpoint of its UV bounds. No usable bottom surface returns no target geometry. Unexpected geometry faults log context and propagate. TargetSurface contains Vertices, TriangleIndices, Bounds, display/category names, ElementVertices, ElementTriangleIndices, and optional LinkTransformMatrix. Coordinates used by calculation are in the host frame. The link matrix contains 16 doubles in column-major order: [basisX.X, basisX.Y, basisX.Z, 0, basisY.X, basisY.Y, basisY.Z, 0, basisZ.X, basisZ.Y, basisZ.Z, 0, origin.X, origin.Y, origin.Z, 1] TransformLinkPointToHost requires exactly 16 values and applies the upper 3×3 basis plus translation. Features/Domain/TargetSurfaceProjector.ProjectToSurface visits every triangle, finds its nearest vertex, edge, or interior point, and retains the nearest point by squared 3D distance. GetTargetElevation returns that point's Z. An empty mesh returns no projection. See Limitations for projection behavior outside a triangle and mesh traversal cost. Framing graph FramingGraphBuilder.ResolveConnectionsAndBuildGraph resolves connections and emits ColumnToBeams, BeamToBeams, and ProcessingOrder. Connection tolerance is 0.5/12 feet (half an inch). Connect free beam ends to column top points within the tolerance, inclusive. For remaining free ends, find the closest other beam segment at a strictly smaller distance than the tolerance. Reject an edge that would form a dependency cycle, log a warning, and leave that end Free. Emit columns first, then topologically sort beam dependencies. Column connections use the first qualifying column in input order. Beam candidates use 3D distance to a segment with the projection parameter clamped to [0,1]. A nearly degenerate segment uses its start point. Each endpoint is independent, so hybrid connections are supported. Ready beams that frame to columns precede other ready beams. Element ID breaks ties. If unresolved dependencies remain, the builder logs and appends remaining beam IDs in sorted order. Adjustment and rounding Features/Planning/Adjustment/AdjustmentEvaluator.CalculateAdjustments follows ProcessingOrder. It keeps adjusted column-top and beam-end elevations in dictionaries without mutating Revit. For a column: targetZ = nearest surface point Z delta = targetZ - originalTopZ roundedDelta = round(delta, tolerance, mode) newTopOffset = originalTopOffset + roundedDelta adjustedTopZ = originalTopZ + roundedDelta For each beam end: Connection Target elevation ToColumn The connected column's adjusted top Z ToBeam Interpolated Z on the supporting beam's adjusted segment Free Nearest target-surface point Z Missing dependency elevations produce Error. For beam interpolation, only XY determines the segment parameter: dx = supportEnd.X - supportStart.X dy = supportEnd.Y - supportStart.Y t = clamp(((query.X - supportStart.X)*dx + (query.Y - supportStart.Y)*dy) / (dx*dx + dy*dy), 0, 1) Z = adjustedStartZ + (adjustedEndZ - adjustedStartZ)*t When XY length squared is less than 1e-10, use adjustedStartZ. The query's Z does not influence interpolation. Each new endpoint offset is its original offset plus rounded target-minus-original-Z delta. RoundingEvaluator.ApplyRounding uses: Mode Rounded delta Nearest Math.Round(delta / tolerance) * tolerance, including .NET's midpoint-to-even rule Up Math.Ceiling(delta / tolerance) * tolerance Down Math.Floor(delta / tolerance) * tolerance Up and Down refer to signed numeric direction, including negative deltas. At helper level, nonpositive tolerance or an undefined mode returns the raw delta. UI and stored-data admission reject invalid settings before normal use. IsWithinTolerance tests abs(delta) < tolerance/2. Columns with a rounded delta within that interval become NoChangeNeeded. Beams become NoChangeNeeded when both rounded deltas satisfy it. Missing target geometry marks every row Error. Profiles and preview MemberProfileExtractor creates temporary placements for unique source types and extracts section loops. It owns each temporary instance immediately after creation, before commit and geometry bake. Creation, bake, and cleanup transaction starts/commits must return Started/Committed. Any subsequent creation, commit, disposal, bake, or extraction fault reaches cleanup. Concurrent extraction and cleanup failures preserve both causes. Expected ProfileLoops/* conditions return structured per-type failures. Unexpected faults and cancellation propagate. One Info summary reports total, extracted, and unsupported counts. Per-type progress uses Debug. PreviewSceneBuilder.Build renders adjusted endpoints using extracted profiles. Missing profiles omit affected members and log counts. No successful profile still permits target-only preview. Target selection prefers bottom-surface TargetSurface. Full TargetElement is a fallback only when that mesh is unavailable. No usable mesh throws Preview/TargetMeshMissing. Mesh Color Opacity Target #4080C0 0.12 Pending member #00CC00 1.0 No-change member #808080 0.7 Error member #CC0000 1.0 PreviewProjector maps meshes, colors, tooltips, IDs, and bounds into immutable StructuralScene3D snapshots. It clamps opacity to [0,1] and uses a fixed Vector3.UnitZ exterior normal. A null mesh, empty vertices, incomplete triangle indices, out-of-range indices, or non-finite vertices throws InvalidOperationException. Missing or invalid RGB/ARGB hexadecimal color text throws FormatException. RGB input receives an opaque FF alpha prefix. A leading # is optional. The projector does not replace invalid mesh or color input with default data. The Presentation presenter owns camera/navigation, device lifetime, hit testing, and cleanup. ERFT selects PreserveAngle and FitRedefinesHome. See preview interaction. Storage formats Features/Persistence/StorageSchema/Revit/StorageSchema defines public-read/public-write String fields: Schema GUID Fields DBTools_ERFT_V2 C736C6F5-34C8-4E50-A890-E5420C3E5391 Tag, SystemId, MemberRole, OriginalOffset, Timestamp DBTools_ERFT_System_V2 06C087B9-DA5B-4E3B-9496-13C7C8732B0E SystemIdString, DataJson Vendor is DBTools. Element Tag is ERFT, MemberRole is Column or Beam, and Timestamp is UTC round-trip text. OriginalOffset contains an invariant number for columns or start;end invariant numbers for beams. Lookup validates schema name and required simple String fields before use. Apply removes legacy element entities at B2C3D4E5-F6A7-4B8C-9D0E-1F2A3B4C5D6E and legacy system entities at C3D4E5F6-A7B8-4C9D-0E1F-2A3B4C5D6E7F only when vendor/name identify DBTools_ERFT or DBTools_ERFT_System respectively. It deletes an emptied DataStorage carrier and logs removals. Foreign registrations under those GUIDs remain untouched and log a warning. This cleanup shares the apply transaction. SystemPlanRepository.Save(Document, StoredPlan) and Load(Document, systemId) return structured failures for expected missing/duplicate/incompatible storage states. Duplicate records for a system fail explicitly. Unexpected Revit repository faults log the system ID and propagate. StoredPlan serializes target IDs/name, ToleranceFeet, RoundingMode, Columns, Beams, SystemId, and Timestamp. Stored columns retain ElementId, OriginalTopOffsetFeet, NewTopOffsetFeet, and AppliedDeltaFeet. Stored beams retain ElementId, original/new endpoint offsets, and applied endpoint deltas. CreateSnapshot includes rows with Pending status before the writer changes statuses after commit. It does not store geometry or profiles. StoredPlanMapper.Deserialize requires serialized tolerance, mode, both collections, and SystemId. Both collections and every member must be non-null. Element IDs must be positive. SystemId must be nonblank and match the DataStorage key ignoring case. A positive host target or a positive link-instance/linked-target pair is required. Tolerance must be positive and rounding mode defined. No schema-version migration participates in admission. Null display name or timestamp normalizes to empty text. Failure code Condition Storage/EmptyPayload Blank JSON Storage/InvalidJson Malformed JSON or missing required serialized members Storage/NullPayload JSON null Storage/IncompatiblePayload Invalid collection/member identity, tolerance, or enum Storage/SystemIdMissing Blank payload SystemId Storage/SystemIdMismatch Record key and payload disagree Storage/TargetMissing No positive target identity Workflows Selection and preparation Features/Selection/Revit/TargetSelectionPicker first picks a linked Floor or RoofBase. Esc switches to host selection through Selection/HostTarget/Revit/HostTargetSelectionFilter. Esc during host selection cancels launch. Each picker owns a yellow guidance banner and disposes its handle in finally. SourceSelectionFilter admits host FamilyInstance elements with: Category Requirement Structural Columns LocationPoint Structural Framing LocationCurve containing a Line, and StructuralType other than Brace SourceSelectionPicker excludes structural materials matching \bconcrete\b, case-insensitively, and reports the filtered count. It reads the instance material, then the type material when absent. Missing or blank material names do not match. Unexpected inspection failures retain element context and propagate. SourceSelectionCollector compares selected and extracted counts. Any extraction mismatch fails with Selection/SourceExtractionFailed. SourceSelectionValidator requires a selected column or a selected beam connected to a column. Beam-only validation extracts model columns and evaluates cloned beam values, so validation does not alter the live plan's connections. No connection produces Selection/NoColumnConnection. Features/Planning/PlanPreparation/Revit/PlanPreparationBuilder prepares the target, source values, framing graph, profiles, and initial adjustments before opening the window. Tolerance and window behavior Presets are 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1 inch, plus Custom. The default is 1/4 inch. Custom text parses with invariant culture and must be finite and at least 0.01 inch. Invalid input appears inline and disables Apply. ErftWindowViewModel.CanApply also requires a positive pending count and zero errors. The modal window contains the target/re-pick control, rounding controls, 3D preview, column/beam comparison grids, summary, Cancel, and Apply. Both grids end with a stretch Status column and a minimum width. Re-pick calls HideForPick, performs selection, recomputes the plan, and shows the same shell and preview presenter. An expected apply failure leaves the dialog available with error feedback. Successful apply reports modified and unchanged element counts, then closes the window. WindowSession.Interaction ignores duplicate Apply and Re-pick requests while IsApplyInProgress is true. The view model's close gate blocks Cancel and ordinary close during that interval. An apply exception triggers a gated-close bypass and propagates when the interaction result is collected. A concurrent close failure is retained with the apply exception. Escape clears both grid selections and marks the key event handled, so it never closes the window. The Cancel button has no IsCancel route. A mouse-down outside a grid row clears both selections regardless of button. Alerts WindowSession uses the active ERFT window as the owner for apply alerts. If that session is absent or retired, it uses the injected owner-handle provider. Selection diagnostics always use the injected provider. Event Presentation No plan to apply Info alert Expected apply failure Error alert Apply success Success alert with modified column/beam and unchanged counts Selected or stored target geometry extraction failed Top Warning banner Source extraction failed or source selection invalid Warning alert All stored sources missing Error alert Some stored sources missing Warning alert with missing count Invalid stored tolerance or rounding mode Error alert Alerts use the tool name as title and window title, with a default OK button. Apply transaction AdjustmentPlanExecutor rejects row errors with Apply/PlanHasErrors. With no pending writes it returns all elements unchanged without invoking the writer. AdjustmentWriter selects RequiresModification rows, sorts columns by ID, and applies beams in graph order followed by any omitted beams in ID order. One ERFT Apply Adjustments transaction performs: Purge recognized legacy ERFT entities. Obtain and validate the element schema. Set column FAMILY_TOP_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM. Set beam STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END0_ELEVATION and STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END1_ELEVATION. Tag changed elements and save the system snapshot in DataStorage. Missing elements/parameters, read-only or wrong-storage parameters, and a false Set result fail apply. Offset, tag, and storage writes must all succeed or the transaction rolls back. After commit, changed rows become NoChangeNeeded. Cancellation propagates. Expected FramingAdjustmentFailureException becomes a structured result. Other exceptions retain their chain and reach the safe-execution boundary. Contextual edit App/Composition/ErftContextualRibbonInjector adapts Core's contextual ribbon runtime. It targets Modify tabs for Structural Columns, Structural Framing, Multi-Select, Multi, or Multi-Category. Eligible selected elements have a supported category, compatible V2 entity, Tag ERFT, and a SystemId. Selection evaluation logs only when (hasErftElements, systemCount, buttonCount) changes. Missing-schema logging occurs once until a schema becomes available again. Selection-hook safe execution suppresses start/completion noise and banners. Edit clicks require a system ID, an initialized ExternalEvent, and an Accepted raise result. The event executes through ISafeExecutor with ErrorOnly notification and an owned InlineUi App run scope. Multiple systems use the system selector. The repository loads the chosen system. A failed repository load logs its code/context and shows this banner before returning: Cannot edit the selected ERFT system because stored plan data is missing or invalid. {Error.Tag} The banner retains the repository failure tag. Edit does not enter new-flow selection. The scope resolves FramingAdjustmentWorkflow and clears its current RevitRunScope before disposal. EditReconstructionBuilder resolves stored source IDs and reads current geometry/offsets. Partially missing sources produce diagnostics and permit remaining sources. No resolvable sources prevents reconstruction. EditReconstructionValidator rejects nonpositive tolerance and undefined modes with Edit/InvalidStoredTolerance or Edit/InvalidStoredRoundingMode. Reconstruction retains SystemId and stored rounding settings, then recomputes adjustments against the target. Re-apply uses current offsets, rather than adding a stored applied delta again. Failures FramingAdjustmentFailure carries expected codes, messages, and context, formatted with [SpecFail/*] tags. These results represent expected contract failures, not every runtime exception. Unexpected selection, material inspection, extraction, cleanup, reconstruction, repository, and apply failures propagate with context. Cancellation is not converted to failed data. Testing See ERFT testing for the single fixture inventory, model requirements, and commands. Limitations Target elevation uses the nearest point in 3D, including triangle edges and vertices; it does not use a vertical intersection. Projection visits every triangle. Legacy storage is removed in the apply transaction without migration.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) Overview ERFT adjusts host structural column and beam offsets to follow a host or linked floor/roof bottom surface. It preserves level associations, previews calculated changes, and applies offsets and storage in one transaction. See the technical specification for geometry, rounding, storage, and failure contracts, and the user guide page for the window. Architecture Ownership Source: src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. The manifest registers DBTools.ERFT, module DBTools.ERFT.App.Composition.ErftToolModule, and command/availability DBTools.ERFT.App.Composition.ErftNewCommand. The command uses InlineUi, icon key erft, and order 60 on the Testing panel. Owner Responsibility App/Composition Command, module, registration, contextual ribbon adapter App/Sessions/WindowSession Modal shell, alerts, banners, and lifetime App/ViewModels Tolerance, row selection, commands, and binding state App/Views/ErftWindow.xaml Raw embedded view Features/Domain Plan values, target projection, and framing graph Features/Selection Source rules, diagnostics, and Revit pickers Features/Operations Revit column, beam, target-geometry, and member-profile readers Features/Planning Preparation, edit reconstruction, target re-pick, adjustment, and rounding Features/Execution Apply orchestration and Revit writer Features/Persistence JSON, schemas, and system DataStorage repository Features/Preview Domain meshes and stable scene projection Features/State/AdjustmentPlanStore Current plan state Features/Workflow/FramingAdjustmentWorkflow New/edit/re-pick/apply interaction through feature-owned IWindowSession Feature decisions remain behind IWindowSession and WindowSessionAction. App implements their typed presentation methods. ERFT production has no dependency on another tool. A missing active document returns Failed before opening the window. The per-run DI scope owns and disposes WindowSession on every exit path. The workflow does not dispose it. Normal-close cleanup diagnostics belong to the shared window host. ERFT logs failures from its own close-and-retire release path without replacing the caller's primary failure. The shell explicitly sets the title Extreme Roof Framing Tool and loads the raw EmbeddedResource DBTools.ToolViews.ERFT.ErftWindow.xaml. The view merges its theme directly and uses the stable string-based EnumMatchConverter for rounding radio buttons. Preview PreviewSceneBuilder creates target and member meshes. PreviewProjector maps them into StructuralScene3D snapshots. DBTools.Presentation.StructuralPreview owns device lifetime, camera state, navigation, hit testing, hover tooltips, emphasis, outlines, target crease edges, and cleanup. DBTools.Presentation.Tools.ERFT.ErftPreviewOptions chooses the preserve-angle camera and fit-as-Home policy. The initial look direction is parallel to (0, 20, -10), with Z up. The camera home angle does not derive from the target mesh. Scene bounds include every rendered mesh vertex. Geometry updates within unchanged bounds preserve Home. Changed bounds fit the scene at the current angle and capture a new Home. Zoom to Fit also replaces Home and the viewport's default camera. Re-pick retains the current angle rather than constructing a new camera. Hover text uses the themed WPF ToolTip with a 16-pixel cursor offset. Member identities use element:<ElementId> and connect preview clicks to comparison rows. Targets are non-pickable context. Empty-space clicks clear row selection. Target hover does not replace member tooltips. Selected members use cyan emphasis and a 1.6-pixel all-edge outline. Target fill opacity is 0.12. Target and member edges use the palette’s cyan-gray color. The stable presenter owns lighting and camera bounds constraints. Status remains visible while the scene prepares or degrades. Navigation buttons disable when no scene exists. Both grids use a final stretch Status column with a minimum width. Thrown zoom/reset exceptions log a warning and appear in the preview status line. Fit failures log a diagnostic; reset without a Home attempts Zoom to Fit. A projection failure clears the rendered scene and shows its cause until the scene changes or the presenter becomes unavailable. Without a specific reason, the placeholder reads 3D Preview is unavailable: the presenter is unavailable. A graphics-device or WPF D3DImage failure permanently disables the presenter for that window. StructuralPreviewDevice releases resources once and does not forward Reinitialize to the native effects manager. It does not substitute WARP for the D3DImage bridge. The placeholder asks the user to update the graphics driver or enable GPU acceleration and reopen the tool. Preview navigation disables, but adjustment, Apply, Cancel, and target re-pick remain available outside an active apply. Re-pick retains the unavailable presenter and does not retry graphics initialization. Profile extraction reports expected unsupported geometry per type. Unexpected geometry, transaction, cleanup, or cancellation faults propagate. One Info summary records total/extracted/unsupported counts. Per-type progress is Debug. Selection-hook logs suppress per-event start/completion banners and report evaluation changes only when state changes. Data and contracts The technical specification defines AdjustmentPlan, target meshes, graph ordering, rounding, element tags, and system storage. Workflows Use Run Extreme Roof Framing on the Testing panel. Pick a linked floor or roof. Press Esc to switch to host target selection. Pick a host target if needed. Esc at this stage cancels launch. Select source columns and beams, then Finish. Review the target, comparison rows, tolerance, and preview. Apply when the tolerance is valid, at least one row requires modification, and no row has Error status. Sources must be point-based structural columns or straight non-brace framing in the host document. Material names matching \bconcrete\b case-insensitively exclude members. The source set needs a column or a beam that connects to a model column under ERFT's hierarchy rule. Unsupported extracted sources fail launch rather than disappearing from the plan. Edit ERFT on contextual Modify tabs restores a selected system's stored plan and settings. Missing or incompatible storage fails edit launch. Re-pick hides the window with HideForPick, selects another target, and reuses the same shell and preview presenter with the rebuilt plan. Re-applying calculates from current model geometry and offsets. During apply, a second Apply or Re-pick request is ignored. Cancel and window close are blocked. A successful apply reports its result and closes the window. An expected apply failure keeps the window open. A thrown apply exception closes the window and propagates to safe execution. Escape clears both comparison-grid selections and does not close the window. Cancel has no WPF IsCancel route. Clicking an empty area of either grid with any mouse button clears both selections. See the alert and preview contracts for event severity, ownership, and validation. Testing Pure tests cover graph construction, target projection, adjustment/rounding, storage admission, scene projection, window selection, close gating, modal lifetime, and injected device creation failure during re-pick and Apply. Core tests exercise presenter recovery and resource release without a GPU. Presentation's hosted StructuralPreview3DTests covers fit-as-Home through the renderer. Revit-hosted FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests uses gm_test_model.rvt and transient host floors with real beam and column instances. It covers seed viability, target extraction, calculation, offset writes, tags, and DataStorage inside rolled-back transaction groups. A Revit 2027 case checks legacy-schema cleanup on 2027/Regression/realtest_model.rvt without saving the model. Linked-target behavior requires a Revit-hosted check with a loaded linked floor or roof. ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects DBTools.ERFT.Local.Tests -y 2026 ./test.sh test --tool ERFT --scope local -y 2026 --fixture FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests Limitations Unsupported member profiles omit those members from the preview. With no successful profiles, the preview contains only the target. Graphics failure requires a new window to initialize another presenter; calculation and Apply remain available in the existing window.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.title: Record Set technical specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.summary: Record Set technical specification Overview Record Set builds a package from selected RVT host files and their file-based external references. It copies files, optionally processes DWG Xrefs, and rewrites references in copied RVT files through TransmissionData. The source is src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. Record Set describes application composition and window interactions. Architecture Domain values describe files and plans. Planning constructs ordered work; Execution dispatches filesystem, CAD, and Revit operations. Record Set architecture lists composition and presentation owners. Data and contracts Data contracts Features/Domain owns these values: Type Contents SourceFile Read-only Name, Path, LinkType, and nullable 64-bit LinkId. Mutable Discipline, Building, CadHandlingMode, BindType. Manual child list HostModel HostFile and read-only Links collection ExternalReferenceKey NormalizedPath plus typed LinkType PlanOptions Nullable AutoDiscoverCadXrefs and AllowCadRepath PlanContext TargetFolder, SelectedHosts, Options, and computed CommonLinkKeys ExecutionPlan Ordered Items, TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes, Summary, Fingerprint PlanSummary Hosts, UniqueLinks, CopyBytes, PredictedOutputBytes, Items PlanMessage Info, Warning, or Block severity and text SourceFile.CreateHost, CreateDiscoveredLink, and CreateManualCadXref construct source values. Discipline defaults to empty. Building defaults to -. Blank building input normalizes to -. CAD mode defaults to Inherit and bind type defaults to Bind. Destination paths belong to immutable PreviewDestination projections, rather than mutable source-file properties. Enum Values LinkType Rvt = 0, Dwg = 1, Other = 2 CadHandlingMode Inherit = 0, AddXrefs = 1, BindAll = 2 BindType Bind = 0, Insert = 1 ExecutionStatus Ok, Cancelled Inherit resolves to AddXrefs during planning. A null PlanOptions flag follows Core Console availability independently for each preview. The UI initially shows unchecked flags, publishes their effective values after preview, and preserves explicit user choices for the window lifetime. These options are not persisted. Destination rules PlanningService.BuildContext counts normalized source-path/type occurrences. Keys appearing at least twice become common links. Identity uses the complete normalized path and type, not just a filename. The count includes repeated references within one host. TargetPathRules computes intended paths: File Destination Host with building {target}/{building}/{discipline}/{name} Host without building {target}/{discipline}/{name} Noncommon link with building {target}/{building}/{discipline}/Linked Files/{name} Noncommon link without building {target}/{discipline}/Linked Files/{name} Common link {target}/Common Linked Files/{name} Blank or - building omits that segment. Empty discipline adds no directory segment. The destination allocator compares normalized paths. Reusing the same source/destination needs no extra copy. A different source colliding with a destination receives name (2).ext, then (3), and so on, with a warning. Allocation fails when the counter exceeds 10,000. Mappings and preview projections use the allocated destination. Safety policy PolicyReader loads the embedded resource DBTools.ToolConfigs.RecordSet.recordset_policy.json from Policies/recordset_policy.json. It does not load a user-side policy file. JSON member Shipped value or rule allowed_target_roots Nonempty required list. Shipped root is \\fileserver\Projects verify_after_copy Required Boolean, shipped false min_free_bytes Required nonnegative number, shipped 10,737,418,240 denied_extensions .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk, .exe allowed_extensions Optional deny_globs Required list, shipped *backup*.rvt, *.old, ~$* paths.enable_long_paths Required Boolean in required paths object, shipped false delete_mode Defaults to quarantine. No plan action consumes it require_sentinel_for_delete Defaults true. No delete action consumes it Configured string entries must be nonblank. Roots must be absolute Windows drive-letter paths or complete UNC server/share paths. Relative, drive-relative, root-relative, and incomplete UNC roots fail admission. Malformed or incompatible policy throws. It is not normalized into valid data. Preview checks the target against admitted roots. Execution reloads policy and checks it again. The containment predicate admits equality with the root and descendants. Before acquiring the lock, execution checks every output-bearing plan path: directories, copy destinations, CAD repath hosts/roots, bind hosts, Revit hosts, and mapping destinations. Copy sources, mapping keys, Revit source hosts, and Bind All source paths remain source paths. Execution requires free space minus max(TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes) to meet MinFreeBytes. Safe filesystem operations resolve existing file and directory redirects before checking containment. Recursive copies carry destination checks into every nested operation. Lock, sentinel, and manifest mutations repeat containment checks. Copies overwrite existing destination files and preserve the source file's UTC creation, last-access, and last-write timestamps. Optional verification compares SHA-256 hashes, including every allowed file in a copied directory. It verifies copied bytes before later CAD/Revit mutations. Workflows Host import and reference reading FileSelectionWorkflow owns OS pickers. HostImporter normalizes picks, rejects existing or repeated hosts, and calls PlanningService.ScanHost with empty discipline and building -. A RevitOperationException or scan warning rejects that host and returns an ordered issue. Owner-token cancellation propagates. The application displays issues and adds only accepted hosts. RevitOperations implements IExternalReferenceReader and ITransmissionWriter. It strips long-path prefixes before passing paths to Revit. Missing TransmissionData or external-reference collections fail with operation and host context. Reference reading uses desired data when IsTransmitted is true and last-saved data otherwise. Library references (PathType.Content, including library-located keynote or assembly-code tables) are omitted. Absolute references retain their stored path. Relative references resolve against the source host folder. For a workshared local, the base is the file-system central folder from BasicFileInfo.CentralPath. Without a usable file-system central path, resolution uses the reference's saved absolute path. A moved package with intact relative structure therefore resolves its own files. The scan creates discovered links using their resolved paths and host metadata. It classifies RVT, DWG, and Other external references. It does not recursively scan linked RVT models. Plan construction and limits Features/Planning/Preview/PreviewPlanBuilder.BuildPlanAsync performs these stages: Find Core Console and resolve nullable CAD flags. Plan hosts and non-CAD links under the file policy. Plan each distinct DWG destination once, using its first occurrence's CAD options. Append Revit repath operations for copied hosts with allowed mappings. Check sources, count bytes, estimate bound output, enforce limits, and compute the fingerprint. Denied hosts or links produce warnings. Missing planned source paths produce Block messages. Directory copies count only policy-allowed files. TotalBytes counts each distinct source/destination copy pair, including repeated copies of one source to different destinations. PlanSummary.UniqueLinks is the number of distinct copy-source paths, including host paths. Hosts is the selected-host count. Items includes directory and message items. Limit Value Result when exceeded PlanningLimits.MaxTotalBytes 80 × 1024³ bytes Block PlanningLimits.MaxTotalItems 10,000 Block PredictedOutputBytes starts at TotalBytes. For Bind All, the estimate adds allowed discovered Xref sizes beyond the copied host DWG size. Estimate failure produces a warning and retains the existing estimate. These are preview limits, not guarantees of final package size. Plan items and progress Plan items are typed records. PlanAction supplies their dispatch identity. Record Data Fingerprint action Fingerprint keys Weight FsCreateDirItem Path fs_create_dir path 1 FsCopyItem Source, Destination fs_copy src, dst 3 CadCopyItem Source, Destination cad_copy src, dst 3 CadRepathItem Host, Xrefs (CadXrefRepath Name, StoredPath, NewPath) cad_repath host, xref:{name} as {stored}>{new} per Xref 2 CadBindAllItem Host, BindType, Xrefs (CadXrefRepath) cad_bind_all host, bindtype as invariant numeric enum text, xref:{name} as {stored}>{new} per Xref 4 RevitRepathItem Host, SourceHost, Mapping revit_repath host, source_host, map:{source} per mapping 2 UIWarnItem Message ui_warn msg 0 UIInfoItem Message ui_info msg 0 Progress increases after an item completes, using its weight divided by the total weight, with a minimum denominator of 1. It is an operation estimate, not byte progress. Each item emits an action string and ordinally sorted key=value fields separated by |. Revit mappings use map:{source} keys. Fingerprinting hashes successive UTF-8 item segments with SHA-256, without an extra separator between segments, and keeps the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It records plan identity for the audit output. Execution does not use it as a content checksum. CAD planning For AddXrefs, the planner copies the DWG and allowed manual Xrefs beside it. With discovery enabled and Core Console available, CadXrefDiscovery lists the Xrefs of the DWG, then of every found Xref DWG, breadth first. Each DWG gets one ICadPreviewer.ListXrefsAsync run per preview, also when several linked DWGs or the Bind All estimate reach it, and a cycle ends at a DWG already listed. Paths compare without case. A block table also lists the Xrefs nested in its attached Xrefs. CadXrefDiscovery keeps an entry for a DWG when the DWG inserts it in model space, a layout (Inserted) or one of its own block definitions (InsertedInBlock), or when no such referenced, attached, found Xref of the DWG lists an entry with the same name. Other entries belong to the Xref that lists them. PreviewPlanBuilder then walks the result from the linked DWG: A not-found Xref adds the Warning Xref {name} in {dwg} not found: {stored path}. A policy-denied Xref adds Policy denied CAD Xref: {file}. Every other Xref file is copied once, as CadCopyItem, into the folder of the linked DWG copy, with collision suffixes when necessary, and appears in the preview tree as a discovered DWG. Each Xref adds the Info Xref {name} in {dwg} ({stored path}): copy to {target-relative copy}, repath to {new path}., or ..., path unchanged. when repath is disabled. With repath enabled, each copied DWG with at least one copied Xref gets one CadRepathItem. Its entries map the stored path, exactly as discovery reported it, to the copy relative to the folder of the DWG copy, with a .\ prefix for the same folder. A copied Xref DWG whose destination is also the destination of a linked DWG is not walked further; the linked DWG's own planning owns its CAD mode. Other Xref DWG copies join PlannedCadDestinations. Preview tree CAD actions apply only to linked DWGs and their manual Xrefs. Discovery failure adds a Warning message, uses heuristic copying and plans no repath. Disabled discovery or unavailable Core Console also uses heuristic copying: copy existing sibling directories named xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg, or cad. Each source/destination directory pair is copied once. Heuristic copying does not rewrite Xrefs. The planner emits Info messages Auto-discover CAD Xrefs disabled. when discovery is disabled with Core Console present, or AutoCAD Core Console not found. DWG Xrefs copied by heuristic only. when Core Console is absent. Explicitly enabling both discovery and repath without Core Console produces Block. BindAll requires Core Console. Without it, preview produces Block and schedules no bind operation. With it, the plan copies the DWG and runs discovery for it, also when AutoDiscoverCadXrefs and AllowCadRepath are false. rs-bind-all-xrefs binds every Xref of the copy, so the plan approves the bind only when discovery lists the complete graph and the file policy admits the found file of every direct and nested Xref, also when the stored path already equals the found path. An empty graph and a graph with cycles can be approved. Each refusal adds a Block that names the linked DWG path: Bind All blocked for {dwg}: CAD Xref discovery failed: {error} for a failed listing of any reached DWG; Bind All blocked for {dwg}: Xref {name} in {drawing} not found: {stored path} for a null or blank found path; Bind All blocked for {dwg}: Policy denied Xref {name} in {drawing} ({stored path}): {found path}. {drawing} is the full path of the DWG that owns the Xref. A refused DWG gets no bind work and no size estimate, and its Block prevents execution. Approved bind work has no manual or discovered Xref copy work. The source drawings can change after the preview, so ExecutionPlanExecutor checks the graph again before each BindAllAsync call. A new CadXrefDiscovery lists the copy and every DWG that its Xrefs reach. The bind work's source paths first apply to the Xrefs of the copy, with the name and stored-path match of rs-apply-paths. The file policy of the run must admit every Xref, with the preview rules. Otherwise the item throws InvalidOperationException before the bind, with Bind All blocked for {copy}: {reasons}, reasons joined by ; , or Bind All blocked for {copy}: CAD Xref discovery failed: {error}. The run then fails and the copy stays unbound. The check and the bind are separate Core Console runs, so a source change between them can race the check. It lists each Xref that the DWG itself owns and that stores a path other than its found full path, mapped to the found source path: a relative path does not resolve from the copy, and nested Xrefs then resolve from the source folder of their parent. The bound-output estimate reuses the discovery listings of approved bind work. An estimate failure adds the Warning Bind selected for {dwg}, but size estimate unavailable: {error}. Selecting BindAll clears manual children. Bind and Insert select AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 and 1 respectively. Bind preserves Xref-prefixed names. Insert merges names and can produce naming conflicts. Core Console boundary CoreConsoleRuntime.FindCoreConsole searches: An existing path from ACCORECONSOLE. accoreconsole.exe in PATH order. AutoCAD 2026, 2025, and 2024 under C:\Program Files\Autodesk. DWG TrueView 2025 under the same directory. Each run extracts the embedded DBTools.ToolCad.RecordSet.rs_xrefs.lsp to a unique temporary .lsp file and attempts deletion in finally. Deletion failures log a Warning. CoreConsoleRunner writes its other temporary files under one stem in the temporary folder: {stem}.scr, {stem}.input.txt and {stem}.result.json. The .scr file loads the script and calls one function: accoreconsole.exe /i "<input.dwg>" /s "<stem>.scr" (load "<script.lsp>") (princ) (<function> "<stem>.result.json" ["<stem>.input.txt"] [<arguments>]) (princ) Arguments use forward slashes and cannot contain a double quote; input lines cannot contain a line break. The input and result files are UTF-8 without a byte order mark. The runner starts both redirected reads immediately, returns standard output, standard error, the exit code and the result text, and deletes the temporary files. Cancellation terminates the owned process tree, observes terminal stream completion and deletes the files. CoreConsoleRuntime.RunScriptAsync accepts a run only when the exit code is 0 and the result file holds a JSON object with "ok": true and the members the caller reads. A missing, empty, malformed or failed result throws InvalidOperationException with the function, DWG, reason, exit code, result text, standard error and standard output. Standard output and standard error are diagnostics only: their encoding is not fixed, and NUL characters are removed and each is cut to its last 2,000 characters in the message. Function Input Result file rs-list-xrefs none xrefs: name, path (stored), found (full path or empty), overlay, inserted, inblock rs-repath-xrefs Three lines per Xref: name, stored path, new path changed, unmatched, failed (name and stored path after the change) rs-bind-all-xrefs The same lines, with source paths; argument BIND or INSERT changed, unmatched, failed, bound, unbound The script uses core AutoLISP and AutoCAD commands only, because Core Console has no ActiveX layer. It writes the result with (open result "w" "utf8"), which needs the Unicode AutoLISP engine (LISPSYS 1 or 2). rs-list-xrefs reads the block table with tblnext. Group 70 flag 4 marks an Xref and flag 8 an overlay; group 1 is the stored path. found is findfile of the stored path (relative paths from DWGPREFIX), then of the file name in DWGPREFIX. inserted is true when ssget "X" finds an INSERT of the block name, with wild-card characters escaped. inblock is true when a block definition of the drawing has an INSERT of it; the script walks each block definition with entnext from its -2 group and skips Xref blocks, blocks from an Xref (group 70 flags 4 and 16) and the layout blocks. rs-repath-xrefs reads the input with read-line. For each entry whose block is an Xref with the given stored path, it runs -XREF Path with the escaped name and the new path, cancels a command that is still active, and reads the stored path back. A changed path must equal the new path, without case. Only when every entry changed does it run QSAVE and check that DBMOD is 0; then ok is true. rs-bind-all-xrefs first changes the listed paths as rs-repath-xrefs does. Only when every entry changed does it set BINDTYPE and run -XREF Bind *. It then lists the Xrefs that remain, and only when none remain does it run QSAVE and check DBMOD. CadPreviewer requires every listed Xref to have a nonblank name and an empty or fully qualified found path, which it normalizes. CadExecutor.RepathXrefsAsync and BindAllAsync also require changed to name every listed Xref, and BindAllAsync requires an empty unbound. Execution rechecks Core Console availability for each CAD repath or bind item. If it is missing, the executor logs the affected DWG path and throws InvalidOperationException rather than using heuristic copying. Before the lock, execution checks that each repath host and each Xref copy that a new path names are under the target. Revit repath RevitRepathItem.SourceHost preserves the source reference base while Host names the copied RVT. Mapping keys are normalized source paths and values are allocated output paths. The writer reads effective references, skips Content references, and matches against the source base. It sets desired paths while preserving effective loaded/unloaded state. TransmissionWriteResult.UpdatedCount is zero for no matching changes. The writer leaves the copied RVT untouched in that case. A positive count causes TransmissionData to be written with IsTransmitted = true. A rewritten workshared copy opens detached and cannot create new locals while transmitted. Reference failures preserve operation, host, reference ID, old/new path context, and original causes through RevitOperationException. Owner cancellation remains cancellation. Execution, cancellation, and audit files ExecutionPlanExecutor.ExecuteAsync validates preconditions, creates runtime metadata, acquires the lock, writes the sentinel, executes items in order, and writes an outcome manifest. It always attempts lock release after successful acquisition. The UI passes CancellationToken.None and shows a non-cancelable overlay. Lower owners honor supplied cancellation at work boundaries. Execution is not dispatched to a worker thread. Outcome Result Successful execution ExecutionStatus.Ok, ok manifest Owner cancellation before lock acquisition Cancelled, empty run ID and manifest path Owner cancellation after acquisition Cancelled, cancelled manifest, lock release Unexpected fault or foreign cancellation Attempt failed manifest, release lock, propagate failure Manifest-write, diagnostic, or lock-release failures remain visible with the primary failure. A cancellation-manifest failure preserves both cancellation and write exceptions. Preflight failures fault the returned task and create no manifest. The UI displays (none) when no manifest exists and preserves known sentinel state for pre-lock cancellation. Runtime paths are: {target}/.recordset.lock {target}/.recordset_sentinel {target}/_recordset_manifests/{run_id}.json Run IDs use UTC yyyyMMdd-HHmmss plus four random lowercase hex characters. The lock uses FileMode.CreateNew, FileShare.None, and UTF-8 contents: run_id={run_id} fingerprint={fingerprint} Acquisition invokes no external log callback after creation. A write/dispose failure attempts partial-lock deletion before propagating. After acquisition, logging and all later work are inside the release boundary. The sentinel is opened or created and remains after completion. There is no package deletion or quarantine plan action. SafeOperationRuntime.TrashRoot names _RS_TRASH/{run_id} but execution does not use it. The manifest has this shape: { "run_id": "20260113-154200-a1b2", "fingerprint": "0123456789abcdef", "target_root": "C:\\Output", "utc": "2026-01-13T15:42:00Z", "summary": { "hosts": 1, "unique_links": 3, "copy_bytes": 1000000, "predicted_output_bytes": 1500000, "items": 8 }, "status": "ok" } SafeWriteManifestRequest carries only the five summary scalars and Status. Execution projects these from PlanSummary. Operations does not depend on the planning aggregate. The manifest records summary and status. The lock prevents concurrent Record Set executions at one target. Inspect the log and manifest before cleaning output or retrying a failed run. Remove a stale lock only after establishing that its execution is no longer active. Manage Items The Options menu opens discipline or building catalogs through ManageDisciplinesCommand and ManageBuildingsCommand. ManageItemsWindowViewModel exposes AddCommand, RenameCommand, and DeleteCommand. Add trims NewName and requires nonblank input. It ignores case-insensitive duplicates and clears NewName after adding. Rename requires a selected item and nonblank RenameTo, trims the replacement, and rejects case-insensitive duplicates. It replaces the item in place, invokes the rename callback, selects the replacement, and clears RenameTo. Delete requires a selection, removes the item, invokes the delete callback, and clears selection and RenameTo. MetadataCatalogWorkflow returns the ordered catalog edits for the App view model to apply to host/link metadata. The dialog's default Close button closes without accepting a separate result payload. UI contracts PreviewWorkflowState requires a current preview, allowed target, and no Block messages before Execute can run. Async Add Hosts, Sync Preview, and Execute commands use nonthrowing safe execution and restore busy state. Debounced preview handles expected owner cancellation separately. For Ok and Cancelled results, the production overlay reports completion and an alert shows status and manifest path. An execution failure shows no completion alert. RecordSetWindowViewModel runs Execute through RunWithoutThrowingAsync with SafeExecutionOptions.ErrorBanner and a null notifier, so the failure is logged and the logger window is surfaced, but no banner appears and the exception does not propagate. Execution progress appears in the main window overlay. Testing See Record Set testing for fixture boundaries and window lifetime requirements. Limitations CadLiveTests exercises rs_xrefs.lsp in AutoCAD Core Console when ACCORECONSOLE names an existing file. See Record Set testing for selection and generated drawings. The AutoCAD command reference does not list the -XREF Path prompts; the script answers with the Xref name and then the new path, cancels a command that is still active, and accepts a change only when the block table reads back the new path. Bind is accepted only when no Xref block remains. Execution leaves completed file mutations in place after a failure; its manifest is not a rollback journal. Containment checks and filesystem writes are separate operations, so concurrent path replacement can race validation.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.title: Record Set | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.summary: Record Set Overview Record Set copies Revit host files and external references into a target directory and rewrites copied references. It previews an ordered plan before executing filesystem, CAD, and Revit TransmissionData operations. Execution copies files and rewrites references in plan order. See the technical specification for formats, ordering, safety checks, and CAD limitations, and the user guide page for the window. Architecture Source ownership Source and manifest: src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. The manifest places Record Set on the Testing panel with InlineUi, order 60, and icon key recordset. Command and availability use DBTools.RecordSet.App.Composition.RecordSetCommand. The module is DBTools.RecordSet.App.Composition.RecordSetToolModule. Owner Responsibility App/Composition Module, command, registration, AppLauncher, and AppLaunchDependencies App/Views Main raw view and RecordSetWindowSession App/ViewModels Binding state, RecordSetWindowServices, debounce, and interaction sequencing App/DesignTime Designer binding surface and DesignTimeSampleFactory Features/Domain Files, hosts, plan options, plan items, summaries, and messages Features/Planning Host import, plan context, destination rules, preview Features/Execution Progress workflow, preflight, item dispatch, outcome handling Features/Operations Filesystem, Windows paths, Revit and CAD ports/adapters, safe-operation requests Features/Policy Embedded policy loading and file filtering Features/Metadata Catalog editing and neutral CatalogEdit results Features/ManageItems Catalog editor view, view model, and modal session AppLauncher constructs RecordSetWindowServices beside its consumer, RecordSetWindowViewModel. MetadataCatalogWorkflow returns ordered edits. The App view model applies them to host rows and linked-file metadata. Feature workflows do not import App row types. Stable controls and the byte converter live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/RecordSet/. Raw views merge the versioned Presentation theme and contain stable WPF types. Designer sample construction reuses PreviewTreeBuilder and locates the selected DWG by file identity at any depth. Presentation and lifetime The main modal shell loads DBTools.ToolViews.RecordSet.RecordSetWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. It uses title Record Set, size 1240 × 780, minimum 980 × 640, CenterScreen placement, and a taskbar entry. Manage Items loads DBTools.ToolViews.RecordSet.ManageItemsWindow.xaml with a bound title, size 520 × 420, minimum 420 × 300, CenterOwner placement, and a taskbar entry. Its Close button is the default button, so Enter closes the dialog. Both Close buttons use ButtonCommandCloseBehavior.ExecuteAndClose and honor the session close gate. User close returns false. With Debug Mode on, the logger window opens after the main dialog closes. Tree containers bind IsSelected and IsExpanded two-way. The stable selected-item behavior reports view selection through a OneWayToSource binding to SelectedTreeNode. A rebuilt preview reselects the same SourceFile and expands only its ancestor chain. Explicit selection changes or a missing file cancel pending reselection. Right-click selects and focuses a row or tree item. Right-clicking a Hosts row other than the current item makes it the sole selection, including when it already belongs to a multi-selection. Rows allow logical focus but remain outside Tab navigation. Options opens below its button. CAD actions require a selected DWG leaf. Manage Disciplines, Manage Buildings, Auto-discover CAD Xrefs, and Allow CAD repath remain disabled until hosts exist. Metadata Add new choices defer the prompt, preserve the prior value on cancellation, and never store the sentinel as metadata. Plan-message bindings use OneTime. CAD bind commands accept the view's string values Bind and Insert. Retirement releases the preview timer and deferred prompts synchronously. Active preview or execution work produces a Dev Mode retirement failure. Idle retirement disposes the view model and services without a dispatcher frame. Data and contracts The technical specification defines file identity, destination allocation, plan items, policy, and output manifests. Workflows Use Choose an allowed target folder. Add host RVT files. Assign discipline and building metadata in the Hosts grid. Review the destination tree and Info, Warning, or Block messages. Configure DWG actions through the selected DWG's context menu. Run Execute when the preview is current and has no blocking messages. Duplicate host picks produce issues and are skipped. A host with a failed reference scan is rejected. It does not become an empty row. Canceling a file or folder picker preserves the current state. Target, host, metadata, and CAD changes invalidate the preview immediately. RecordSetPreviewSyncCoordinator debounces automatic refresh by 350 ms at DispatcherPriority.Normal. Preview planning runs through Task.Run and publishes on the UI context. Execution remains on its caller context and uses a non-cancelable progress overlay. Busy state disables editing, CAD actions, options, and ordinary window close. The footer reports Root, Free, ACAD, and Sentinel status. Root is Pending, Allowed, or Blocked; Sentinel is Pending, Present, or Missing. ACAD shows the Core Console path or Unavailable. Testing The Pure project references the normal desktop tool project, which owns its source and resource mapping. Pure fixtures cover domain, planning, preview, execution, filesystem policy, CAD process handling, view models, and catalog editing. Most CAD fixtures replace accoreconsole.exe with a .cmd file that copies a prepared result file to {stem}.result.json and the input file to the scratch folder, and the planner fixtures use a fake ICadPreviewer. CadLiveTests runs the embedded rs_xrefs.lsp through CadPreviewer, CadXrefDiscovery, PreviewPlanBuilder and CadExecutor with real AutoCAD Core Console. Each test is ignored unless ACCORECONSOLE names an existing file. The fixture does not search PATH or Autodesk installation folders. Select it with ./test.sh test --tool RECORDSET --scope pure --fixture CadLiveTests on a machine with AutoCAD. The fixture creates DWGs in a temporary folder and removes that folder in teardown. It checks a relative attachment, a nested attachment and an Xref inserted only inside a local block, their planned copies and stored-path maps, repath readback, and Bind All from source-relative paths. Readback occurs after removing the source drawings. It exercises CAD plan items directly, without opening a Revit host.
