The fixture script uses these AutoCAD command sequences: LINE: first point, next point, end input. SAVEAS: default file format, filename, with FILEDIA=0. -XREF Attach: filename, insertion point, X scale, Y scale, rotation. REFPATHTYPE=1 selects relative paths after the host has a filename. -BLOCK: name, Mode/Convert, base point, selected Xref insert, end selection. QSAVE: save the named drawing without a filename prompt. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover TransmissionData and WPF application behavior. WPF fixtures share WindowRuntimeScope, which releases only runtime state it installs. The hosted bootstrap supplies the Revit owner. Modal tests use ToolWindowDialog.Show with synchronous callbacks and a ten-second watchdog. The watchdog cannot interrupt native code or callbacks that do not pump the dispatcher. The CAD selection test uses a modeless test session to await preview/edit cycles outside a modal callback. It checks the selected node, ancestor expansion, CAD state, and manual Xrefs after rebuilds. Production remains modal. The execution fixture checks real copied bytes, the manifest, and lock release. Filesystem tests cover destination junctions and redirected manifest paths. Limitations Execution has no UI cancellation action and can leave partial output on failure. Inspect the log and outcome manifest before retrying or removing output. CAD script limitations are specified in the technical specification.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc-s.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc-s.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) specification Overview This page specifies the data contract of View Template Comparer (VTC): what it reads from a view template, how it keys and compares settings, and how it applies, copies and stores them. The VTC developer guide describes the architecture. Architecture TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter read snapshots. TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares them; TemplateApplier applies selected changes. TemplateStorage owns cached JSON. See VTC architecture for composition and views. Data and contracts Scope VTC compares two view templates of the current document. Category edits stay staged locally until Process. Imported categories are ordinary category rows on their own tab. Revit-link settings are limited to settings that the public Revit API can both read and write. VTC reads and writes a setting through the public API or does not handle it. Tabs The tree follows the Visibility/Graphics dialog. SettingTab values: ModelCategories AnnotationCategories AnalyticalModelCategories ImportedCategories Filters RevitLinks Worksets DesignOptions CategoryTabClassifier sends a model category with a positive ID (an imported DWG, SAT or similar category) to ImportedCategories. Internal categories, which the dialog does not show, are classified as model categories. Other category types keep their native tab. Imported categories Extraction emits imported parents and their layers and subcategories as CategoryGraphicsData. Layers and subcategories inherit the imported parent's tab. Imported rows keep SettingType=CategoryOverride and use the same compare pipeline as every other category. There is no import-specific apply path. Inline edit, Inspector edit, Preview, pending overrides, batch apply, merged save and snapshot apply all use the standard category path. A selection whose side is missing resets visibility and graphics as for any other category row. Revit links Data TemplateSnapshot.RevitLinks is a list of RevitLinkSetting records: public sealed record RevitLinkSetting( long LinkElementId, RevitLinkTargetKind TargetKind, // RevitLinkType or RevitLinkInstance string LinkName, string LinkDisplayName, RevitLinkSettingKind SettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue Value); Each row is one target and one native setting. VTC extracts both RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance targets; they are keyed, labeled and copied separately. Setting kinds RevitLinkSettingKind has 11 values, all members of RevitLinkGraphicsSettings: Kind Kind LinkVisibilityType ColorFill LinkedViewId ViewRange ViewFilterType Phase NestedLinks PhaseFilter ObjectStyles ViewDetailLevel Discipline The adapter binds all 11 kinds directly to typed public API members for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. Extraction RevitLinkSettingsAdapter.Extract enumerates link targets, reads View.GetLinkOverrides(...) (a new RevitLinkGraphicsSettings when there are none) and emits one row per setting kind. Simple settings use the native LinkVisibility or ElementId value. Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level and Discipline use their public getter and setter and are stored as one row each. Linked element names are read from the linked document when it is loaded. These names identify Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter across models. Keys and comparison RevitLinkDiffEvaluator keys each row as link.{type|instance}.name.{LinkName}.{SettingKind}, for example link.type.name.ARCH_Model.rvt.LinkVisibilityType. LinkName is the only cross-model key. Compare, save, load and apply all use it; there is no element-ID key. If a key is ambiguous within a target kind, compare throws InvalidOperationException ("Revit link key '...' is ambiguous. ..."). TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares typed SettingValue cases. DiffTreeBuilder groups the rows under Revit Links by LinkDisplayName, with one leaf per setting kind. Library storage TemplateStorage stores saved templates as JSON in the VTC cache directory (AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("VTC")). It is the only code that derives cache file paths. Callers use logical template names. A rooted name, or a name with a path separator, is rejected before any path is derived. SavedTemplateInfo exposes only the name and modification time. Load and save accept only one complete TemplateSnapshot shape: required top-level members and collections must be present, explicit nulls and invalid nested elements are rejected, and the same validation runs before an in-memory snapshot is saved. There is no normalization and no recovery of other formats; incompatible data raises TemplateStorageException. Saved Revit-link rows must have a non-blank LinkName and LinkDisplayName, defined TargetKind and SettingKind values and a value valid for the kind: a visibility mode from 0 to 2, no mode for linked-view IDs, a detail level from 0 to 3, a defined discipline, and no enum value for other kinds. GetSavedTemplates returns an empty list when the cache directory does not exist, without creating it. Other enumeration failures raise TemplateStorageException (operation enumerate). TemplateExists returns false for a missing file or directory. Other probe failures raise TemplateStorageException (operation probe), so the save is refused instead of overwriting. Only SaveTemplate creates the directory. An existing name is replaced only after the user answers Replace; otherwise the file is written with overwrite disabled, so a template that another process saved under the name after the probe is kept and the save fails with TemplateStorageException. MergedTemplateBuilder writes RevitLinks rows like any other diff rows. Revit-link rows take part in Preview, Process, Create Merged and merged save. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Domain/Template/TemplateSnapshot.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/Library/Operations/TemplateStorage.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/RevitLinks/. Workflows Apply and copy Apply Applying a Revit-link row reads the current link overrides, changes only the selected setting and writes the settings back with View.SetLinkOverrides(...). Targets are resolved by LinkName only. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are remapped by linked-element name. Dependent rows first set the required top-level visibility mode. A selection whose side is missing resets only that setting to its host default. Applying from the Revit-link modal uses BatchApply in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one sub-transaction per setting and one Undo entry. A missing comparison key is an ElementNotFound conflict; an unexpected fault rolls back the whole apply. Copy The context menu of a concrete link group or leaf row (not the Revit Links tab root) has Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... Opening the modal from a leaf row shows the full group of that link target, so the modal always shows all 11 kinds. A successful modal apply refreshes the main comparison. The modal and the copy command work on one template side. RevitLinkActionSourceResolver selects the only side with a value, or a viable selected side, and reports "no Revit-link value" or a real two-sided ambiguity without showing UI. On ambiguity App asks which template to use; it never defaults to Left. Copy uses TemplateRuntime.GetRevitLinkTargets() and CopyRevitLinkSettings(...) and always copies all 11 kinds. Each target is copied in its own transaction; the transactions run in the Copy Revit Link Settings transaction group (started through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin) and are assimilated into one Undo entry. An expected failure skips only that target and is logged; an unexpected fault rolls back every target. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are copied by finding the source linked-element name in the target linked model; raw linked-document IDs are not copied across models. If the source linked document is unloaded and the name is not available, the raw ID is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. Otherwise copy fails. Testing See VTC testing for Pure and Revit-hosted fixture inventories. Limitations A Revit-link key must be unique within its target kind. Cross-model Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter remapping requires the linked-element name. When the source link is unloaded, raw IDs are reused only for the same linked model; copying to a different linked model fails.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc.h.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc.h.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) Overview View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two Revit view templates of the current document, stages category edits locally, and applies the selected differences and eligible pending overrides through one command, ApplySelectedChangesCommand (button label "Process"). It can also create a merged template and save templates to a local library. The data contract (tabs, imported categories, Revit-link settings, keys, apply and copy rules, library storage) is in the VTC specification. Architecture Source: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/. The manifest registers DBTools.VTC on the Testing ribbon panel with InlineUi, order 50, and icon key vtc. Command and composition VtcCommand is the Revit entry point. It validates the command context and calls App/Composition/VtcWindowLauncher. VtcWindowLauncher owns the modal launch: it resolves the document's templates, shows an alert when there are none, has VtcWindowCompositionFactory build the collaborators, and creates VtcWindowSession through Core's ToolWindowFactory. After the dialog closes it opens the logger window when Debug Mode is on. It always retires the comparer and linked-file windows; a dialog failure is reported before any retirement failure. VtcWindowCompositionFactory creates one graph per document: TemplateExtractor, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, TemplateDifferenceEvaluator, TemplateApplier, TemplateMaterializer, TemplateStorage (cache directory AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("VTC")) and the one document facade, TemplateRuntime. TemplateRuntime (Revit/Template) resolves template IDs and exposes compare, extract, batch apply, create merged, apply model, Revit-link targets and copy, and line and fill pattern queries. App batch-session code depends on the App/Sessions/ITemplateSessionRuntime port, which TemplateRuntime implements. VtcWindowSession owns the modal window session. ToolWindowFactory supplies the stable shell for the raw VTC view. Comparison owns the workspace, Inspector and Preview views; Library owns its workspace view; the Revit-link modal reuses the Comparison diff control. AlertPresenter is the only alert boundary in App. Composition gives the alert service only to the presenter; view models and workflows use the presenter for standard alerts, custom requests and selections. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow handles App session reactions for Process and Library work. The App view model owns Revit-link prompts, modal hosting, refresh and result presentation. TemplateRuntime passes Revit-link batch apply and copy, and the classification of expected conflicts, to Template Apply. VtcWindowCommandRuntime reports a refused operation through SafeExecutionRefusalReporter as VTC {operation}. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateRuntime.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/TemplateApply/Execution/TemplateApplier.Operations.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/App/Composition/VtcWindowCompositionFactory.cs. Source layout VTC has several features under Features/, each with its own domain, planning, state, Revit and UI code: Path Content Features/Comparison Diff tree (DiffTreeBuilder, DiffTreeIndex, DiffTreeNode, DiffTreeProjector), preview projection, window comparison state (VtcWindowComparisonCoordinator), category tab classification and RevitLinkActionSourceResolver Features/Library TemplateStorage, SavedTemplateInfo, TemplateStorageException Features/RevitLinks RevitLinkDiffEvaluator, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, RevitLinkTargetResolver, the Revit-link settings window Features/TemplateApply TemplateApplier partials, pending overrides (PendingOverrideState), apply results and conflicts, MergedTemplateBuilder, SnapshotSelectionPolicy, pattern rendering and override editors Features/TemplateComparison.cs, Features/TemplateDifferenceEvaluator.cs Host-neutral comparison result and evaluator Domain/ Tool-wide vocabulary: TemplateSnapshot, SettingDifference, SettingValue, SettingTab, RevitLinkSetting, RevitLinkSettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue, RevitLinkTarget, RevitLinkTargetKind and the graphics data types Revit/Template TemplateExtractor, TemplateMaterializer, TemplateRuntime App/ Composition, sessions, view models, views and design-time data TemplateDifferenceEvaluator is host-neutral. TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter own the Revit mechanics behind TemplateRuntime. SettingDifference.LeftValue and RightValue hold typed SettingValue cases. Compare, apply and App code pattern-match these cases. Display settings use VTC enums (DetailLevel, DisplayStyle, PartsVisibility, ViewDiscipline, ShowHiddenLinesMode); conversion to Revit enums happens only at the Revit API boundary. SettingPreviewItem and DiffTreeProjector.ViewFilter are Comparison contracts, so feature projections do not import App view models. DiffTreeNode holds comparison and display state only. PendingOverrideState holds pending override DTOs with no tree or UI dependency. TemplateApplyResult is the only apply outcome; the App view model (TemplateApplyOutcomeProjection) projects it onto setting keys for row feedback and filters and stores no outcome on comparison nodes. DiffTreeBuilder only builds a tree from differences. DiffTreeIndex keeps the rebuilt roots and owns key lookup, canonical node paths, selection collection in tree order and Revit-link subtree queries for the coordinator, the preview projection and the Revit-link modal. MergedTemplateBuilder (Features/TemplateApply/Planning/MergedTemplate) builds the merged TemplateSnapshot from the comparison result, the selections, the base side and the name. View-model operations only orchestrate effects. App composes outcome templates into Comparison views at runtime; Comparison raises only selected-node, override-edit and preview-setting requests for App to coordinate across panes and modals. Views VTC views are raw XAML EmbeddedResource items with explicit logical names: DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.VtcWindow.xaml (main view) DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonWorkspaceView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonInspectorView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonPreviewView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.DiffViewControl.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.LibraryView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.RevitLinkSettingsWindow.xaml VtcWindowSession loads the main resource through ToolWindowFactory and owns the one-time owner attachment and cleanup. VTC has no custom close gate and no native pick loop. Shared resource dictionaries are in DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC/: VtcDiffViewStyles.xaml and VtcComparisonViewStyles.xaml. The namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.VTC holds the converters VtcConflictConverter and VtcRawViewConverter. VtcResourceTemplateSelector resolves App outcome templates and returns an empty template in a standalone view. Alert bodies use full type-name string keys with TypeNameTemplateSelector. Every content and item slot has an explicit template; immutable record values bind OneTime and mutable view-model state uses INotifyPropertyChanged. Each raw view merges Theme once, before the VTC dictionaries; the shared dictionaries do not merge Theme. Vtc.TreeView is based on the implicit TreeView style with VTC overrides; each tree sets its own scrolling and virtualization. Named item selectors set TextSearch.TextPath for prefix typing and automation names on their template text. SavedTemplateInfo, ViewFilterOption, LinePattern, FillPatternData and TemplateOption return their display label from ToString(), so automation peers and text fallbacks show the label. Preview navigation is available only for navigable setting keys. Double-click override editing responds to the left mouse button only, on eligible rows. Keyboard focus moves to the comparison row after the Inspector tab loads. Pending focus and close requests are canceled on retirement. The linked dialog's context-menu selection commands bind to its own view model. The raw linked view has the automation name "Linked file override differences". The main window initializer uses the log prefix VtcWindow. Data and contracts The specification defines tabs, typed setting values, imported categories, Revit-link identity, and library storage. Workflows Process and merged templates ApplySelectedChangesCommand applies the selections and eligible pending category overrides in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one SubTransaction per setting so an expected conflict rolls back only that setting. An apply failure becomes a per-setting conflict only after its sub-transaction confirms RolledBack. If the rollback throws or reports another status, the batch stops with a BatchApplyException that contains the apply failure and then the rollback failure. An unconfirmed rollback never publishes a pending-override conflict key. Create Merged (TemplateRuntime.CreateMergedTemplate) runs template creation and the pending-override batch in one transaction group, Create Merged View Template, started through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin and assimilated into one Undo entry. Expected per-setting conflicts are reported and the new template is kept. Any other fault rolls the group back and leaves no template, so a retry with the same name works. TemplateMaterializer copies the Left template with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements and a duplicate-type handler that keeps destination types, so Revit shows no dialog. It catches no copy failure: a fault rolls back the group and reaches RunOrReport as an Error alert. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow.SavedTemplates treats template extraction or merge and the cache save or delete as the change. After that change, the list refresh has its own error boundary: a refresh failure is logged with the template name and shows one warning that the cache operation succeeded; success is shown only after the refresh succeeds. Both save commands ask Replace saved template 'X'? through AlertPresenter before they overwrite an existing name; Cancel writes nothing. Testing DBTools.VTC.Pure.Tests (no Revit host): DiffTreeBuilderTests, DiffTreeIndexTests, DiffTreeNode*Tests, DiffTreeProjectorTests: grouping, selection state and change notification, including imported-category tabs and Revit-link grouping by link name. PendingOverrideStateTests, PendingCategoryOverrideTests: staging, eligibility, restore, clear, merge-save application and failed-pending collection. TemplateApplyOutcomeProjectionTests: keyed conflict and success projection for row feedback and result filters. TemplateStorageTests: the real storage service with a temporary cache directory, including imported-category data and RevitLinks rows. The project references the VTC product assembly directly, not DBTools.App. TemplateDiffEvaluatorTests, RevitLinkDiffEvaluatorTests: snapshot comparison over SettingDifference rows. RevitLinkActionSourceResolverTests: sole-side, selected-side, ambiguous-side and no-value resolution. AlertBodyTemplateProviderTests: the provider and its raw DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml resource (WPF only). VtcRawXamlParseTests: the linked-file view's accessible name and its view model passed to the composed diff view. Raw comparison view tests use the registered ToolWindowFactory session and the stable behavior bindings. Revit-hosted tests (the local scope) in DBTools.VTC.Local.Tests open the Global Mapper (GM) and Super Girt Tool (SGT) test models, create temporary templates and roll back every change after each run: VtcWindowViewModelTests: Process, Create and link flows around real template extraction, apply and creation, alert orchestration and the Revit-link modal and copy. RevitLinkBaselineTests: extract and apply round trips of LinkVisibilityType and LinkedViewId on RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance targets in sgt_test_model.rvt. RevitLinkExtendedTests: the other RevitLinkGraphicsSettings members on the SGT linked model. RevitLinkSnapshotRemapTests: snapshot compare and apply with deliberately mismatched target and linked-element IDs, LinkName pairing and linked-element-name remap failures. ImportedCategoryRoundTripTests: imports a shared CAD file inside the rollback scope and checks that imported categories use the normal category compare and apply path. SgtModelExtractionTests, GmModelExtractionTests: extraction from existing views and presence of link targets in the open models. Limitations Comparison requires two view templates in the same document. Revit-link settings are restricted to the public API; linked-element remapping requires a resolvable name or the same-model ID condition in the specification.

developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.summary: Analytical Snap To Level Overview Analytical Snap To Level moves selected analytical members to a chosen level elevation. Beams move both endpoints. Columns move the endpoint nearest the target elevation and retain the other endpoint. X and Y coordinates remain unchanged. A column tie moves the start endpoint. Related tool: Framing Joins. Architecture Registration manifest.yml registers DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel with the command and availability type DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.App.Composition.AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand. The button uses InlineUi, icon key analytical_snap, and order 20 on the Structural panel. The assembly is DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel. Data and contracts Snapper API The public snapper boundary is: public AnalyticalSnapper(ITransactionRunner tx, Document doc, ILogger logger); public (int ProcessedCount, IReadOnlyList<(ElementId ElementId, string Reason)> Skipped) Run(ICollection<ElementId> selectedIds, Level targetLevel); AnalyticalSnapper.Run(ICollection<ElementId>, Level) returns ProcessedCount and an ordered list of (ElementId, Reason) skips. AnalyticalSegment.SnapTo owns the pure endpoint rule. AnalyticalSnapper resolves the typed Revit structural role, constructs the adjusted line, and calls SetCurve. A processed member counts even when its endpoint elevations already match the target. Skips and diagnostics Reason Constant on AnalyticalSnapper Condition not an analytical member NotAnalyticalMember Missing element, wrong category, or wrong runtime type role not supported RoleNotSupported Structural role is neither Beam nor Column not straight NotStraight Curve is not a Line would collapse WouldCollapse Adjusted length is less than Application.ShortCurveTolerance The completion alert groups skips in first-seen reason order. Each group shows its count and at most ten element IDs, followed by and N more when needed. The non-analytical group shows only its count. Debug logs include the target level, per-element skip or success, and final totals. Workflows Use Select analytical members. Run Analytical Snap To Level on the Structural panel. Choose a level from the elevation-sorted level picker. Read the processed and skipped counts in the completion alert. The ribbon accepts any nonempty selection through CommandAvailability.HasSelection. Processing requires OST_AnalyticalMember and an AnalyticalMember instance. See Limitations for supported roles and curves. The tool has no persistent settings. Execution Source: src/Tools/Structural/AnalyticalSnapToLevel/. App/Composition/AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand resolves Features/AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflow. The workflow uses IAlertService for the level picker and completion alert, ITransactionRunner for changes, a window-owner provider, and a typed logger. It ensures the logger window through ILoggerWindowHost after successful completion when Debug Mode is enabled. All members run in one DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level transaction. Unexpected failures, including a SetCurve refusal, propagate to safe execution and roll back the entire run. An empty selection or a missing level choice produces SafeExecutionRefusedException. The level picker returns no choice when the document contains no levels. Testing Pure tests cover endpoint geometry through AnalyticalSegmentTests and AnalyticalSegmentEdgeCaseTests. Revit-hosted workflow tests cover skip-summary behavior. Revit integration tests live under Tests/Integration/Revit/ and exercise the command, workflow, and analytical curve changes. developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.title: Combined Foundation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Overview Combined Foundation Tags updates pier/footing association parameters and moves combined tags to footing corners. Source: src/Tools/Structural/FoundationTags/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.FoundationTags. Architecture Ownership App/Composition/FoundationTagsToolModule binds settings, registers the pack, and delegates feature registration to ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddFoundationTagsFeatures. Features/UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsWorkflow and Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsWorkflow own manual execution and completion reporting. Queued result-selection gates receive the workflow logger. Pure geometry types are Point2D, FoundationTagsPoint, FootingCornerPoints, and NearestPointResult. FoundationTagsGeometry owns SelectCornerByViewOrientation, FindNearestPoint2D, and IsValidCornerName. Commands Ribbon command Identity Split-button order Update Combined Foundation Tags DBTools.UpdateCombinedFoundationTags 0 Move Combined Tags DBTools.MoveCombinedFoundationTags 1 Both use InlineUi on the Structural panel in split group foundation_tags. Their command and availability classes are UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsCommand and MoveCombinedFoundationTagsCommand under App/Composition. Icon keys are update_combined and move_combined. Organize Foundation Types occupies order 2 in the same group. Data and contracts Settings Configuration section: Tools.FoundationTags. Pack: structural.foundation_tags, titled Combined Foundation Tags. AutoUpdateEnabled defaults to true. Pattern lists default empty and resolve to: Property Default pattern TagFamilyPatterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ PierFamilyPatterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ FootingFamilyPatterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ The UI allows three patterns per group through Core RegexPatternListContext. It validates syntax and tracks pending changes. FamilyNameClassifier compiles the configured patterns for both workflows. Workflows Update Features/CombinedFoundationTagsUpdater collects visible FamilyInstance elements from the active view. Configured family patterns classify piers and footings. Updates affect host-document instances. Compute each pier's top as Top Level elevation plus Top Offset. Write Foundation Pier Top by GUID. Find the nearest pier to each footing using XY location points, within two feet inclusive. Write that pier's type mark to Associated Pier and its top to Associated Pier Elevation. Publish current-run result IDs and timestamped selection sets. A missing or invalid Top Level records a pier failure. Missing Top Offset uses zero. Piers without LocationPoint cannot participate in nearest-point matching. Equal-distance ties retain the first candidate. Without a pier, the updater clears the association text to an empty string. It keeps a stored elevation and reports failure because these length parameters cannot be cleared. Parameter.ClearValue requires HideWhenNoValue, which the shipped definitions do not set. An elevation without a stored value needs no clearing. Double writes compare values rounded to two decimal places in internal feet. String comparison is ordinal. UpdateParameterWriter returns failures for missing, read-only, wrong-storage, or rejected parameter writes. The updater records these failures and continues. A footing can appear in both Modified and Failed sets when one parameter changes and another fails. Unexpected exceptions escape the parameter transaction and roll back the run. Parameter writes and selection-set publication use separate transactions inside one transaction group. The group assimilates to one Undo entry. A selection-set failure preserves committed parameter writes, then propagates after assimilation. Other failures attempt group rollback and preserve concurrent cleanup faults. UpdateRunResult contains UpdatedCount, FailedCount, and read-only snapshots of Modified and Failed IDs. The manual workflow offers Select Modified and Select Skipped when updates exist. Those banner actions check that the source document is still active before selecting IDs. With no updates, it shows an Info or Warning toast without selection actions. Selection sets use DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (...) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (...) names with Eastern-time timestamps. Repeated names receive suffixes starting at (2). Pruning retains five sets across both kinds, ordered by descending element ID. Move Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsRunner collects visible IndependentTag instances, resolves a tagged host or linked structural foundation, and filters tag family/type names by the configured patterns. Only the host tag moves. Linked footing geometry transforms into host coordinates. The desired name is the trimmed tag name, or its type name when the tag name is blank. Supported values are case-insensitive Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right, and Bottom Left. The runner tessellates fine-detail footing geometry, including nonvisible objects, in the instance's local frame. Local XY extents define four rectangular corners. FoundationTagsGeometry.SelectCornerByViewOrientation labels them against the view's RightDirection and UpDirection. The edge most aligned with view-right becomes horizontal. A tie uses the second declared edge. The tag retains its current Z. Unsupported names, missing point locations, and geometry without usable corners are skips. All candidate moves share DB Tools - Move Combined Foundation Tags. Unexpected transform, geometry, tessellation, or tag-write errors log the tag ID and propagate, rolling back every move. MoveRunResult separates moved, skipped, candidate, total-view-tag, structural-foundation, and pattern-rejection counts, with rejected-name samples for diagnostics. Prerequisites and repair Manual commands and automatic updates validate shared parameters without modifying them. The required definitions are owned by Features/Prerequisite/PrerequisiteRequiredParameters: Parameter GUID Type Instance category Initial group Associated Pier 7f6c2c2a-46ab-4e78-9bf6-9b9c2ef8f7d1 Text Structural Foundation Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation 6d9b0f7f-4f7a-44a4-9c5c-0c0f4bf0da21 Length Structural Foundation Identity Data Foundation Pier Top 93de44b8-bb7c-4e58-a7e0-9a3a1c8e4d70 Length Structural Columns Constraints Invalid prerequisites activate core.structural.combined_tags and refuse manual commands with SafeExecutionRefusedException. Safe execution shows a Warning banner and logs a Warning without a stack. Unexpected validation faults remain errors and do not assert invalid prerequisites. Use Settings → Combined Foundation Tags → Refresh to inspect the active document. Use Install/Repair or Install/Repair Required Parameters to repair it. A successful repair clears the warning and re-enables the commands. Construction of the settings context is passive and shows a Refresh prompt. SettingsRuntime receives the settings host's UIApplication explicitly. Refresh replaces immutable RequiredParameters status rows. Their six column bindings use OneTime. HasWarning belongs to the session context and is not persisted in FoundationTagsSettings. Install/Repair uses embedded definitions in group DBTools.Structural.FoundationTags. It creates a temporary shared-parameter file, restores Revit's original shared-parameter path, and attempts temporary-file deletion. The embedded definitions supply the required parameters. Repair deletes conflicting definitions with the same required name and a different GUID, including duplicate-name collisions. It preserves other categories and the existing group when extending a binding. An instance binding already containing the required category remains unchanged. A type binding becomes an instance binding with its existing categories plus the required category. Revit drops the type values and the installer logs a Warning naming the parameter. The updater accesses these parameters by GUID. The warning disables Update, Move, and Organize Foundation Types. Its title is Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. Clear it after resolving the prerequisite issue. Automatic updates and monitoring CombinedFoundationTagsAutoUpdateTask runs Update in FloorPlan and CeilingPlan views when enabled and no warning blocks it. Invalid prerequisites set the warning and show a banner once per document session through PrerequisiteBannerLedger. NotApplicable and TransientNotReady evaluations skip execution. An unexpected runtime fault sets no prerequisite warning. Core's ViewActivationHook suppresses the failed task for that document session. PrerequisiteMonitorTask checks prerequisite state and schedules an Idling retry for transient initialization states. PrerequisiteRetryCoordinator retains each original event source and detach callback. Evaluation faults log and can be checked again on the next view activation. The monitor disposes its own retry coordinator at synchronous App shutdown. An injected coordinator remains caller-owned. Disposed lifetimes reject scheduling. Failed-detach entries retain cleanup state without retry work. A late Idling event can retry detachment. Testing Pure tests cover geometry, rotated views, corner names, regex classification, prerequisite lifecycle, and write results. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover commands, modules, updates, moves, monitoring, repair, and settings. ./test.sh test --tool FoundationTags --scope local -y 2026 Limitations Association updates use host-document pier and footing instances. Move supports host tags referencing host or linked foundations and only the four listed corner names. Length values cannot be cleared with the shipped shared-parameter definitions.

developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.title: Framing Joins | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.summary: Framing Joins Overview Framing Joins allows or disallows joins at both ends of selected structural framing instances. The tool has no persistent settings. Architecture Source The implementation and manifest are under src/Tools/Structural/FramingJoins/. The project references Core and the Revit API. Data and contracts Commands Command Manifest identity Operation Allow Join DBTools.AllowJoinSelected Calls StructuralFramingUtils.AllowJoinAtEnd for ends 0 and 1 Disallow Join DBTools.DisallowJoinSelected Calls StructuralFramingUtils.DisallowJoinAtEnd for ends 0 and 1 Both commands use InlineUi and the Structural panel's framing_joins split button. Their manifest order is 0 and 1, respectively. The icon keys are allow_join and disallow_join. Availability uses CommandAvailability.HasStructuralFramingSelection. Workflows Use Select structural framing elements. Run Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the completion banner for the processed instance count. Execution App/Composition/AllowJoinSelectedCommand and DisallowJoinSelectedCommand resolve Features/FramingJoinsWorkflow through their CommandService registration. The workflow receives ITransactionRunner, ILoggerWindowHost, a window-owner provider, and a typed logger through dependency injection. The workflow reads the current selection, filters by OST_StructuralFraming, removes duplicate IDs, and retains only elements that resolve to FamilyInstance. An empty selection or a selection without usable framing instances produces SafeExecutionRefusedException. FramingJoinTargetBuilder owns the category filter. FramingJoinsWorkflow.ExecuteCore owns the endpoint loop. All targets run in one transaction named DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. The count increases after both endpoint calls succeed. It counts processed instances, including instances whose join state already matches the request. An endpoint failure logs the exception and element ID, then throws InvalidOperationException with the original cause. The transaction rolls back the complete batch. A successful batch shows a six-second completion toast and ensures the logger window when Debug Mode is enabled. Testing Pure fixtures FramingJoinTargetBuilderTests and FramingJoinsWorkflowTests cover filtering and endpoint execution. Revit-hosted fixtures FramingJoinsCommandTests and FramingJoinsWorkflowRevitTests cover command and Revit integration. Limitations The tool processes FamilyInstance elements in Structural Framing. It does not alter joins for other selected elements.

developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.title: Joist Girder Weights | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.summary: Joist Girder Weights Overview Joist Girder Weights estimates pounds per linear foot and writes the result to a writable Double parameter named Wt. It scans structural framing in the active document. The ribbon command runs manually. A view-activation task runs automatically when enabled. Architecture Ownership and registration Source: src/Tools/Structural/JoistGirderWeight/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/JoistGirderWeightToolModule Module, settings pack, hooks, and warning registration App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions Dependency registration App/Composition/UpdateJoistGirderWeightsCommand Manual command Features/Workflow/WeightUpdateWorkflow Settings retrieval, update, completion/configuration banners Features/AutoUpdate/AutoUpdateTask View-activation execution Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderClassifier Family and load-name classification Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightUpdater Revit collection, validation, and writes Features/Load/Operations/ElementLoadReader Parameter and unit resolution Features/Load/LoadParser Text parsing Features/Load/LoadResolutionEvaluator Load group ambiguity and precedence Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightEvaluator Pure formula Features/JoistGirder/Settings/Views/JoistGirderWeightSettingsView.xaml Settings view manifest.yml registers assembly DBTools.JoistGirderWeight and module DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.App.Composition.JoistGirderWeightToolModule. The command uses InlineUi, icon key joist_girder, and ribbon order 30. The asset is Assets/joist_girder_icon.png. Data and contracts Inputs The configured regex tests the family name. It tests the type name only when the family name is blank. The default family pattern is: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ It matches G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder, and Vulcraft Joist Girder. Input Resolution Constraint Number of joists Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Greater than 1 Span Cut Length, Length Positive internal feet Depth Depth Positive internal feet Load Total/point load, or dead plus live load Nonnegative kips Output Wt Writable Double on the instance or type Numeric aliases are checked in the listed order, with instance then type lookup for each name. Load resolution prefers instance parameters over same-named type parameters. It rejects multiple populated matches in any Total, Dead, or Live group, even when a Total value exists. One Total value takes precedence over Dead plus Live. Without Total, exactly one Dead and one Live are required. Force-typed Double values convert from Revit internal units to kips. Unitless numeric values are kips. Text uses invariant numeric parsing and accepts these units: Units Conversion to kips Omitted, k, kip, kips Unchanged lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds Divide by 1000 kN, case-insensitive Multiply by 0.2248089431 Examples are 10, 10 kips, 10000 lb, and 45 kN. Blank, negative, malformed, or unsupported-unit text produces an input issue. Formula Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightEvaluator.EstimateWeight(n, load, lengthFeet, depthFeet) returns lb/ft. The calculation converts length and depth to inches. panelSpacing = lengthInches / n numberOfPanels = n - 1 totalReaction = loadKips * numberOfPanels / 2 maxMoment = totalReaction * lengthInches / 2 For even n, subtract loadKips * panelSpacing * i for integer steps starting at 1 while i < numberOfPanels / 2. For odd n, subtract loadKips * (panelSpacing / 2 + panelSpacing * j) starting at 0 while j < numberOfPanels / 2. effectiveDepth = depthInches * 0.95 chordForce = maxMoment / effectiveDepth requiredArea = chordForce / (50.0 * 0.6) topChordWeight = requiredArea * lengthInches * 0.28356 * 1.06 bottomChordWeight = topChordWeight * 1.13 webWeight = topChordWeight * 0.7 weightPoundsPerFoot = (topChordWeight + bottomChordWeight + webWeight) / lengthFeet 50.0 is the stress constant in ksi. 0.28356 is steel density in lb/in³. The remaining constants are depth, connection, and member multipliers. Settings Configuration section: Tools.JoistGirderWeight. Pack key: structural.joist_girder_weight, titled Joist Girder Weights. Property Persisted default Effective default AutoUpdateEnabled true true FamilyNamePattern Empty string Family pattern above DeadLoadPattern Empty string (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) LiveLoadPattern Empty string (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) TotalLoadPattern Empty string (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) For example, the Total pattern matches Point Load, Panel Point Load, Total Load, and Total Load - User Defined. Features/DefaultPatterns owns defaults. Settings/SettingsPackContext derives from SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<JoistGirderWeightSettings> and owns pattern editing, empty-value defaulting, regex validation, snapshots, and baseline comparison. The Core base owns the toggle, warning, pending-change, and notification state. Workflows Update and failure behavior JoistGirderWeightUpdater validates candidates and computes weights before opening a transaction. Invalid candidates become skipped items. Valid candidates share Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. An unexpected transaction or setter exception propagates and rolls back that transaction. Updated increments after each setter call returns. See Limitations for count semantics. The returned summary contains Candidates, Updated, Skipped, and up to five sample issues. Zero candidates returns an empty summary. All-invalid candidates return skipped counts. The manual workflow displays an Info toast when nothing updates, Warning for mixed updated/skipped results, and Success when all candidates update. Configuration exceptions produce a ten-second Warning toast. Automatic execution catches configuration exceptions, sets the configured warning, and shows a banner. Other runtime faults propagate to Core's view-activation handling. Warning core.structural.joist_girder disables DBTools.UpdateJoistGirderWeights and automatic updates. Testing Pure tests cover the evaluator, classifier, patterns, load parsing and resolution, and settings context. Revit-hosted updater and workflow tests use real Revit parameters and roll back model changes. The workflow fixture supplies a WPF owner for banners and closes its own windows after each test. ./test.sh test --tool JoistGirderWeight --scope local -y 2026 Limitations The formula estimates weight; it does not select manufacturer sections or validate SJI load tables. Updated counts reflect attempted writes whose setters did not throw, including a false Parameter.Set result that leaves the value unchanged.

developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.summary: Organize Foundation Types Overview Organize Foundation Types renames foundation family types, assigns type marks, and merges types with equal dimensions. It processes all matching types in the active document. It does not use the current selection or persistent settings. Architecture Registration and ownership Source: src/Tools/Structural/OrganizeFoundationTypes/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/OrganizeFoundationTypesCommand Manifest command, active-document availability Features/FoundationType/OrganizeFoundationTypesWorkflow Confirmation, organizer invocation, completion alert, Debug logger window Features/FoundationType/FoundationTypeOrganizer Collection, dimension comparison, rename, merge, deletion Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkGenerator Mark generation and pure formatting helper Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkPolicy Preserve or overwrite mode manifest.yml registers DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes as an InlineUi split-button item in foundation_tags, order 2, icon key organize_types. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags occupy orders 0 and 1. The structural.foundation_tags pack's core.structural.combined_tags warning disables all three commands. A typical documentation workflow runs this organizer, then Update Combined Foundation Tags, then Move Combined Tags. Data and contracts Families and parameters The family-name comparison uses StringComparison.Ordinal. Family Category Dimensions Prefix Sort order Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P b * h Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Diameter Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Width, length, thickness Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Width, length, thickness All sorts are ascending. Dimensions use Double parameters. Type marks use the String parameter Type Mark. Dimension text uses Revit's feet-and-fractional-inches formatter. Missing dimension parameters display ?. Duplicate keys use the nullable raw dimension values. Marks and names Family group Mark format Name format Example Rectangular pier P-{n}, starting at 1 {b}x{h} ({mark}) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Round pier RP-{n}, starting at 1 {d} DIA. ({mark}) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing or pile cap {prefix}-{widthFeet}.{n}, starting at 0 {width}x{length}x{thickness} ({mark}) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) widthFeet is the floor of the width in internal feet. Each family group maintains its own ordinal set of marks encountered during processing. Generation searches from the starting counter for an unused mark in that set. It does not reserve marks on types that have not yet been processed. The confirmation asks whether to overwrite existing marks. Yes selects TypeMarkPolicy.OverwriteExistingTypeMarks. No selects PreserveExistingTypeMarks. Preserve mode generates marks only for blank values, but still renames types and merges duplicates. SetParam leaves a missing, non-String, or read-only Type Mark unchanged, so a generated name does not guarantee a mark write. Workflows Processing and transactions Collect and sort the four family groups. Compare each type's dimension tuple with retained types in its group. For a duplicate, reassign its instances to the retained type. For a retained type, assign its mark when permitted and rename it. Delete successfully merged source types after processing the group. The first successfully retained type for a dimension tuple becomes the merge target. Dimension comparison is exact. Each rename/mark operation and duplicate reassignment runs through a nested transaction-runner call. A failed reassignment rolls back that type's changes and records a skip. The organizer deletes a duplicate only after all its instances change type. All groups share the outer DB Tools - Organize Foundation Types transaction. A deletion error logs at Error and propagates, rolling back the complete operation. Per-type failures log at Debug and increment the skip count. The final warning and completion alert include skipped totals and up to five type id: reason samples. The alert also reports renamed and merged counts. Testing Pure TypeMarkGeneratorTests covers sequential numbering, gaps, width groups, prefixes, and invalid arguments. Revit-hosted OrganizeFoundationTypesTests covers confirmation, completion reporting, duplicate merges, and document changes inside a rolled-back fixture transaction group. Limitations Family names must match the four listed names exactly. Dimension equality is exact, including missing values; missing dimensions can therefore cause types to merge.

Orientation analysis and resolved members Resolved member contracts Preview (Elevation, Section and 3D) and placement read the same resolved data. ResolvedMemberContractResolver builds one ResolvedMemberContract per member: identity (role, type, opening key and edge), orientation (warm-state key, canonical and probe rotation, Flip, Y and Z justification), the world line and frame, and the normalized section geometry from the exact warmed state. Preview does not compute transforms, signs or depths of its own. Opening members are listed once as OpeningMemberSegmentContract values (OpeningMemberContractCatalog); preview meshes, hit testing and placement enumerate that list, so segment order and index are the same in every preview mode and in the placed members. The resolver also derives the secondary section axis from the role and wall frame, so girts, headers and sills face the same way in the preview as when placed, also on mirrored or rotated walls. Warmed profile states Profile warming (ProfileWarmStateProbe) places temporary instances and captures one exact state per key of quarter-turn rotation, Flip state, raw Y and Z justification and horizontal or vertical axis mode (MemberProfile.ExactStatesByKey). Each probe applies the parameters in a fixed order: cross-section rotation (plus the wall compensation below), then Flip Facing, then Y justification and Z justification, then zero offsets, then one regeneration. Placement applies a resolved orientation in the same order. Rotated walls WallRotationCompensationEvaluator takes the wall's along-axis azimuth, finds the nearest right angle and returns the negated residual as compensation. Vertical roles (jambs) are probed at each canonical quarter turn plus that compensation; horizontal roles (girts, headers, sills) are probed at the canonical quarter turns only. Rows keep the canonical quarter-turn values (0, 90, 180, 270). Placement adds the compensation to the cross-section rotation of vertical members only. Opening frame direction When the wall frame is swapped relative to the linked wall (IsFrameSwapped), live openings are mirrored along the wall: start and end become length − end and length − start. Preview and placement use the resulting along-wall distances; there is no separate branch for mirrored links. Seating rules Orientation analysis (FamilyOrientationAnalyzer) tries each Y and Z justification pair on a probe instance, regenerates once per pair and measures web and flange seating. Web seating mode (WebSeatingMode): open sections (Channel, Zee, Angle) in horizontal roles use EdgeContact; HSS sections and jamb roles use FaceCoplanar. Zee and Angle types are not offered for opening roles. Seating planes: a girt's web seats on the elevation plane. Head, sill and jamb web seating planes use the structural target origin, including layer and wall offsets, not the raw wall-frame origin. Mirrored links: the flange must seat on the negative side of the depth axis for a mirrored link and on the positive side otherwise. Square HSS: every non-end-cap face is a candidate web and flange face, and either seating side is accepted. Rectangular HSS: calibration records deep and shallow face IDs (HssDeepFaceIds, HssShallowFaceIds). Horizontal roles seat a deep face on the exterior plane; jamb roles seat a deep face on the opening-edge plane. Without that metadata, the larger of the web and flange face sets counts as deep. Angles: for girts, the short leg is the web face and the long leg is the flange face (AngleShortLegFaceId, AngleLongLegFaceId). Faces are resolved again after each regeneration, because Revit geometry objects are not stable across regenerations. Non-finite distances or dot products reject a candidate pair. Temporary probe transactions report Revit blocking failures as type warnings or failures in the analysis result (TemporaryTransactionRunner). Plan admission and synchronization PlanStore.Initialize prepares and validates a candidate before it replaces the live plan or advances its revision. A rejected initialization keeps the accepted plan and sends no event; a successful one publishes one initialized event after the lock is released. Plan admission rejects duplicate member keys. Undo of a segment deletion relies on unique keys to match surviving group rows. Every Plan and PlanBaselineSnapshot has a required WallTarget. Host wall, linked wall and link-instance IDs are 64-bit through persistence, Revit lookup, hashing, opening identity, placement and preview. Opening element IDs and compound-wall material IDs are also 64-bit; manual-opening surrogate IDs and layer indexes are int. Plan.Clone() detaches each mutable collection that UI projection uses: editable girt and opening rows, runtime member and opening definitions, baseline lists, type options, layer snapshots, orientation and profile maps, grid collections and the execution context. Shared leaf values are immutable. PlanStore owns a detached accepted plan. Initialization copies its input before it prepares or stamps it. Reads and notifications return detached snapshots. Update is the write boundary. Rejected changes and mutator exceptions keep content and version; a no-op update publishes no event. An accepted update advances the version once and detaches the candidate before storage, so a retained reference cannot change accepted state. Notifications run outside the write lock. Shared wall-layer collections are read-only. Member segment replacement materializes and filters candidates before it replaces the segments. Empty or all-short input, and enumeration failure, keep the previous segments. Replacement from the member's own segment view is valid. Plan-change admission uses one lock and one latest-pending slot: Enqueue clones the accepted plan and assigns a monotonic request revision. An arrival while a dispatcher callback is scheduled replaces the pending snapshot; the scheduled callback applies the latest revision. The apply turn clears the pending slot and marks itself applying before it projects. An arrival during apply fills the pending slot without recursion; completion schedules exactly one later Dispatcher.BeginInvoke turn. The coordinator does not pump frames and does not drop an arrival. The request revision identifies the refresh; Plan.Version is plan data and diagnostic context. If applying one snapshot fails while a newer one is pending, the pending dispatch is still attempted. If both fail, the first failure is reported first, and the failed dispatch resets admission so a later change schedules normally. PlanSynchronizationCoordinator.TryApplyPartialEdit owns every UI-originated partial plan write: the opening parent-row commit, the girt and opening segment flyouts, the PreviewEditingWorkflow entry points (snap, typed gap, segment delete, merge) and jamb segment add and delete. Each such write, and SyncPlanFromUI (the UI-edit preview pass, Place and Update, Change Review), refreshes every pane from the written plan before it returns. It applies the refresh its own write queued (ApplyPendingPlanRefreshOnUI, in the same ApplyPlanRefresh batch as every other plan refresh), so no queued pass or later write projects stale rows over the edit, and a field typed after the write keeps its text. Before it projects, the coordinator applies a refresh still queued by a plan written outside it (Undo or Redo of a preview-only edit, PlanStore.Initialize). It then projects the whole UI (TryProjectPlanFromUI) and writes the edit on top of that projection as one plan version, so unsaved valid drafts are written with it. Examples: a wall offset pushed on LostFocus whose Background sync has not run when a Send-priority opening commit arrives, or an edit made while a 3D scene builds. While any field is invalid it writes nothing, records no Undo entry and shows the blocked-sync status (Fix invalid fields, Fix invalid rows or Preview blocked). Only a write outside the coordinator still refreshes at Background priority; a field typed between that write and its refresh takes the refreshed value. Each writer builds its change from a detached copy of the projection. A PreviewEditOutcome is a pair of plan changes that PreviewEditingWorkflow writes once through the coordinator and then records, so Undo and Redo replay only that change and the drafts written with it stay. A rejected opening segment edit aborts the write. Deleting girt rows is a grid draft without a plan write and is never refused. Undo and Redo bypass admission: they replace the plan and so every pane's fields. A refused type change (girt segment flyout, or an unavailable type in the girt grid) reports through GirtPaneViewModel.ShowRefusedTypeChange and sets no blocker. Girt segment boundaries Domain/Girt/SegmentBoundary/GirtSegmentBoundarySet decides where a girt can start, end and split. For a girt at elevation z, an opening blocks it when the opening spans z (inclusive, 1e-6 ft tolerance), is framed, is not bypassed by the row, is not the row's interior opening, and has a nonzero width after its span is clamped to the wall. Start-capable boundaries: the wall start and the higher edge of each blocking opening. End-capable boundaries: the lower edge of each blocking opening and the wall end. The row's interior opening adds its lower edge as start-capable and its higher edge as end-capable. GirtSegmentBoundarySet.Split is the only girt segment computation. It omits every span shorter than MemberRules.MinimumLength (0.5 ft). Its callers: plan-row segmentation (GirtSegmentationReconciler), preview (PreviewGirtSegmentBuilder), placement (MemberSegmentResolver.ResolveGirtSegments), the usable-span check (MemberResolutionExtentsProjection.HasUsableGirtSpan) and the snap offer (GirtExtentSnapPlanEditor.ResolveBoundaryEdges). MemberSegmentResolver is an internal, girt-only resolver; WallHydrator resolves every member through it and rejects a non-girt member with MemberSegment/RoleUnsupported. GirtSegmentBoundarySource supplies the wall length, openings, grid positions and the framing predicate. FromOpenings has the only production predicate, which frames every opening. FromPlan builds the source from plan rows (segmentation, the resolver, the snap editor); MemberResolutionExtentsProjection.GirtBoundaries builds it from runtime opening definitions (preview, placement, usable-span check). TryResolveT clamps an opening edge to the wall like the boundary set. GirtSegmentationReconciler splits each segment group from its first sibling's start to its last sibling's end (clamped to the wall) and reuses row identities by overlap. The first and last child keep the group's outer anchors and endpoint gaps, also when Split omits an outer pier shorter than the minimum length; only ends between two children become opening-edge anchors. A group with one span becomes one row. A group with no span keeps its rows as authored, and placement reports them. An interior row leaves its segment group, and SegmentGroupRenumberer.RenumberSegmentGroup normalizes the remaining rows (a group of one row dissolves). Girt endpoint anchors Domain/Girt/EndpointAnchor/GirtEndpointAnchor is the stored anchor of one girt endpoint and the only reader of stored girt anchors. Its kinds: Kind Stored as Meaning Wall ExtentKind.FullLength Wall end Grid ExtentKind.Grid Grid line OpeningEdge ExtentKind.OpeningEdge, opening key + Left or Right Lower-T (Left) or higher-T (Right) edge of an opening Girt endpoints never use ExtentKind.MemberEdge; that kind is only for opening-member (jamb, header, sill) segments. Gaps: An opening-edge endpoint stores a user gap only in OpeningEdgeGapOverridesFeet["<key>:<Left|Right>"]. Otherwise the gap is derived from the jamb at that edge and elevation (GirtGapResolver.GetDefaultOpeningEdgeGapFeet), and is 0 when there is no jamb. GirtGapResolver.GetOpeningEdgeGapFeet is that rule; preview, the gap editor and placement all call it. StartGapOverrideFeet and EndGapOverrideFeet apply only to Wall and Grid anchors. Their rule is GirtGapResolver.GetEndpointGapFeet, called by preview (MemberGapResolver.GetEffectiveEndpointGapFeet), the gap editor and placement (GirtEndpointGapEvaluator.ComputeEndpointCutbackFeet): the override when set; otherwise, when the end lies within 1e-4 T of an edge that can bound it (a start on a higher edge, an end on a lower edge of a boundary opening in the girt's own boundary set), the gap derived from that edge's jamb; otherwise 0. When the plan cannot resolve a gap handle (for example the edge of an opening deleted before the preview redraws), PreviewEditingWorkflow.TryGetMemberGapFeet shows a Gap edit failed banner and no gap editor opens. Anchor writes: GirtPlanRow.SetAnchor clears the endpoint gap when it writes an opening edge. GirtPlanRow.ReplaceAnchor (snap edits, merges) also clears the gap entries of the old and new edges. GirtPlanRow.Reanchor (the resolver) clears the endpoint gap and the lost edge's entry and keeps the entry of the edge it moves to. GirtPlanRow.AbsorbPayload takes in a merged row's payload: bypass lists are united and gap entries are added; on a key conflict the receiving row's entry wins. The resolver merge (the survivor receives), the preview segment merge (the kept row receives) and the segmentation group proxy (the first sibling receives) use it. Interior intent is derived, not stored: a row whose start is the lower edge and whose end is the higher edge of one opening that it does not bypass spans that opening (GirtEndpointAnchor.FindInteriorOpeningKey, exposed as GirtPlanRow.InteriorOpeningKey). Re-anchoring GirtEndpointAnchorResolver.Resolve is the only re-anchoring rule. MemberSegmentationReconciler.Recompute runs it after opening-role normalization and before opening and girt segmentation. Recompute runs on each UI-edit or plan-mutation preview refresh, after committed opening edits, and in PreparePlacementPlan before Place or Update preflight; a render-only preview draws the plan as stored. An endpoint is lost when its grid is gone (GridRemoved), its opening is gone (OpeningRemoved), or its opening edge is not capable for that end in the row's boundary set (OpeningNotBoundary; for example the opening no longer spans the girt, lies outside a shortened wall or is bypassed by the row). A lost end uses the row's other end as reference: a start moves to the nearest start-capable boundary at or before reference − minimum length, an end to the nearest end-capable boundary at or after reference + minimum length. The wall ends are the fallback. When both ends are lost, the start moves to the wall start and the end to the first end-capable boundary at or after the minimum length. The re-anchored end loses its endpoint gap and the gap entry of its lost edge; the edge it moves to keeps its entry. Bypass keys and gap entries of openings no longer in the plan are removed. Siblings of one segment group that now overlap merge into the earlier sibling. The survivor keeps its member key; each side keeps the outermost anchor that was not re-anchored (with its gap); bypass lists and gap entries are united with GirtPlanRow.AbsorbPayload; opening-member targets that named an absorbed row are rewritten to the survivor; and the group is normalized with SegmentGroupRenumberer. Segmentation then splits the plan again and reuses identities by overlap. Workflows Window session Lifecycle App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionLifecycle.cs owns the lifecycle states, close intent, startup outcome and finalization result. The modal driver is synchronous and always returns a completed task, because both Revit command callers block immediately. A relink hides the window, runs the synchronous picker, then calls ShowDialog again in the same command frame. One owned ContextIdle callback resumes target analysis after the window is visible. The driver rejects a modal return before the pick or shown handshake completes, and never posts the modal re-entry. WindowSessionOperationObserver observes the current initial-analysis or target-analysis task on the owning dispatcher. A completed task delivers inline; a pending task delivers through one owned dispatcher operation while the modal frame is active. Closing during analysis cancels the analysis and keeps the window and transaction group alive until the outcome arrives. Retirement revokes the callbacks and aborts the operation. Forced retirement clears commit intent, releases payload resources and publishes cancellation. If the synchronous picker is still on the stack, cancellation and transaction rollback wait until it returns; no target analysis or banner runs afterward. An ordinary Closed cleanup is a separate state and keeps an accepted commit. Native window and dispatcher references are captured before registration retirement. Transaction operations complete through the inline Revit call gate, before the command returns. App/Sessions/WindowSession/Revit/SgtWindowSession.cs supplies Revit picking and startup, window resource effects and error-boundary integration. RunModalFlowAsync is the production entry point. Launch uses a closed WindowSessionLaunchRequest: New requires a concrete WallTarget; Edit requires a non-default SystemId. WindowSessionBuilder requires an inline Revit call gate and rolls back construction failures with ordered cleanup. The command consumes only completed lifecycle tasks. Close and the transaction group The session owns one transaction group, Super Girt Tool. SGT refuses a document that is already modifiable at launch. Native X and Alt+F4 reuse the WPF close already in progress. An active analysis delays close until its outcome settles. An accepted Closed releases the mandatory preview and window resources, then finalizes the group inline. A successful close intent with a healthy, successful session assimilates the group; Cancel, errors and forced retirement roll it back. A programmatic close that throws, or returns without Closed, rolls back once and leaves a close-only retry for X, Alt+F4 and Cancel. The retry does not finalize again. No transaction is committed outside the session group. Model commit requires an explicit successful startup and model outcome and a healthy group. Failures of mandatory preview or window cleanup select rollback before assimilation. Synchronous transaction, cleanup and finalization failures propagate. App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionUIStatePersistence.cs saves only cosmetic state: expanded panels, column widths and bulk-edit defaults. It is best-effort and never gates or delays the model commit. Neither OK nor Cancel waits for the disk write. A successful commit with a pending save logs that preferences are saved in the background, without a banner. An already-failed save shows a warning through the Revit default-owner notifier after the close. A finally block always attaches the disk-task observer, also when finalization throws. The observer logs a later disk failure and does not touch the retired window. Cancel releases the transaction and window first, then observes the save without changing the Cancelled outcome. A failed cosmetic save does not change a completed model commit. Error boundary WindowInitializer attaches the Core error boundary of the window. WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry owns the dispatcher subscription and routes DB Tools failures to the most recently attached active window, or the most recently attached window when none is active. A DB Tools failure is thrown from, or passes through, an assembly named DBTools or starting with DBTools.; this includes DBTools.HandyControl and the Helix code merged into DBTools.Presentation, but not another add-in's HandyControl or Helix copy. WindowErrorBoundary classifies, presents and records the handled state. SgtWindowSession subscribes to its own boundary; a missing host fails session construction. When Core handles a failure on the SGT window, the session records the original exception and any presentation failure, requests a rollback close while it keeps the modal frame, completes its cleanup, unsubscribes, and propagates the original failure, ahead of cleanup or modal-assertion failures, through the command's safe-execution boundary. SGT does not attach its own dispatcher exception handler; Core neither handles nor signals other add-ins' exceptions. A ShowDialog failure before ContentRendered cannot have started analysis, so rollback, resource release and finalization run synchronously on the Revit UI thread, and only the cosmetic save can remain. Broken modal-continuation invariants are collected as finalization failures and do not skip rollback or cleanup. When the modal frame is already gone, the session records that invariant, does not await incomplete dispatcher work, downgrades finalization to rollback and continues every safe cleanup step. The safe-execution boundary owns user-facing reporting. View model The view model owns queued plan, preview and render dispatcher operations. Disposal stops both refresh coordinators, drops the pending plan snapshot and aborts queued callbacks before it cancels analysis. Late preview results cannot publish to a retired view. Girt and opening projection publishes validation flags, but those notifications do not queue another UI edit; segment group display refresh is suppressed the same way. Invalid rows and refreshed group labels therefore cannot start a preview loop. Each analysis run owns its cancellation source until its finally completes. A newer run or disposal cancels the active run without disposing its source early. An idle source is canceled and disposed immediately when replaced. Canceled or superseded results cannot publish a plan or change preview mode after an await. A disposed view model creates no new idle source. Recoverable plan rejections are SpecFailure results at the opening-segment, preview girt-snap, member-segment hydration and placement-projection boundaries; the UI shows the typed rejection and publishes no plan or preview change. Argument defects, cancellation and unexpected faults are exceptions and propagate through the safe-execution boundary. Revit transaction and model-write code can throw SpecFailureException when unwinding must roll back; unrelated faults propagate as exceptions. TemporaryTransactionRunner retains operation, accessor, and rollback failures before diagnostics. Snapshot and rollback logging failures follow in attempt order; a single operation failure preserves its original exception. Plan admission rejects an invalid update with SpecFailureException carrying PlanValidationFailed and the validation details. Opening persistence and segment mutation translate only that code into their failure results. A rejection keeps the committed plan and version; parent edits stay suppressed until a successful retry or cancellation. A rejected segment add, delete or property change shows the failure in the banner and the preview status without a refresh request. UI-to-plan synchronization reads the committed layer directly when there is no UI selection. It builds the girt projection where it uses it and lets opening persistence own the opening projection. Segment lookup and deletion use canonical opening rows through the row resolver. PlacementElementTagStore admits elements for contextual selection, update, removal and deconstruction. An owned element has the Structural Framing category, a valid SGT schema entity, the exact SGT marker and a non-blank system ID. An update collects admitted instances once per transaction and indexes them by role and identity; each target consumes its entry, and unmatched admitted instances are deleted after all walls are processed. An element with another marker is never owned, even when its stored system ID matches. PlacementWorkflow keeps the command's SafeExecutionResult and returns one placement or removal outcome. A successful command requests a successful close; a failed or canceled model write requests a rollback close. Declining the removal confirmation leaves the window open, because no write began. Revit/CommittedWrite/CommittedWrite maps Revit refusals and non-committed transaction status to Transaction/NotCommitted and keeps the original cause. Each command uses ordinary transactions inside the session group. GirtView raises typed row requests with the selected GirtRowViewModel, visual anchor, and input event. App routes these requests to the bulk-edit and segment flyouts. Girt column widths are not persisted. The dialog ports IDangerConfirmationDialog and IUpdateSummaryDialog are in Features/Placement/Workflow; App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionDialogs.cs implements them. Change Review Features/ChangeReview owns the detached review candidate, row decisions, target precedence, the decision ledger, relink pairing and the dialog. The dialog is an embedded raw XAML view with no x:Class or code-behind. Accept, Keep and Ignore are the only decision terms in the UI and the code. Opening labels use the source name and the along-wall range; the opening key is internal. ChangeReviewWorkflow synchronizes the accepted plan before it captures its revision, reads one live snapshot and analyzes a confirmed candidate before it publishes it. Confirm writes only the detached plan and ledger state. A later Place or Update command writes the model and sets Placed from the write result, so several model commands can follow one review while the session group stays open. The lifecycle owns the review child and any relink picker. It retires the child in finally, closes the child before it hides the parent for a pick and resumes the same modal driver after the picker returns. Cancel, native close, command failure and forced retirement roll back the session group; only a successful close assimilates it, as one Undo entry named Super Girt Tool. ChangeReviewPlanBuilder decides: it resolves each item's decision once and derives both the candidate plan and the ledger that Confirm saves; rows show the resolved decision. AllowedDecisions is the matrix of allowed decisions and ProposeDecision the default rule. The dialog offers the matrix's decisions (SetInvalidated removes Ignore for a released user-created opening unless Ignore is already selected) and preselects an allowed proposal. The builder applies a proposal to an undecided item that needs no attention only when the matrix allows it. An explicit Ignore returns a Placed opening to its Placed framing configuration, held, also when the draft has a local edit. An opening that was never placed stays unframed; a later Keep frames a never-placed manual opening again. Without a live observation a row offers only Keep and Ignore. The live snapshot carries the grid crossings along the Placed wall and the observed wall; girt grid anchors resolve against the grids of the wall the review adopts. Rows show the opening source name (or Manual opening for an unnamed manual row), source, status and decision; effects appear in the details pane of the selected row. Placement validation messages include the along-wall range where it matters. The canonical key is never shown. Preview Features/Preview/Domain owns the preview scene, palette, wall, girt, opening, grid and segment-assignment state. Features/Preview/Rendering/Scene3D builds plain SGT mesh values. Features/Preview/Views/Rendering/Scene3D/StructuralPreviewSceneAdapter maps them to the snapshot DTOs of IStructuralPreview3D. WPF renderers and canvas layout are under Features/Preview/Views. The Presentation viewport owns Helix, camera navigation, fit and reset, hit testing, hover and selection materials. SGT code has no Helix reference. PreviewPresenterBehavior (App) draws the 2D elevation and section and owns handles, snapping, context menus and row selection; it forwards 3D scene and emphasis updates through the stable API. SgtWindow composes PreviewView.xaml into the host and retires the presenter before transaction finalization. Placement view models store no Preview domain objects. Preview edits change the domain plan and request a FromPlan projection. PreviewServiceCollectionExtensions.cs registers the feature; the window-session builder binds it into the modal runtime. Edit workflows are under Features/Preview/Editing/MemberResolution/Segmentation; reusable plan-edit calculations are under Domain/PlanEditing. StructuralPreviewSceneAdapter is the only conversion from scene metadata to Presentation DTOs. Mesh IDs keep the source row, role and segment identity, so click selection, hover tooltips, sibling dimming, segment emphasis and wall-context materials are deterministic. SGT turns off the viewport's own tooltip popup; the PreviewView overlay is the only tooltip. Viewport pointer events still drive it, including wall-only click tooltips and clearing on wall hover. Wall meshes are pickable context hits but never select rows; a member hit wins when both are present. The adapter adds a transparent floor plane and sets a minimum overlay thickness. Scene bounds and the exterior normal set the home camera orientation; the presenter owns orbit, pan, zoom, fit and camera persistence while the view is hosted. Refresh: Features/Preview/Refresh/PreviewProjectionService projects a given Plan without changing the plan or its store. App reconciles segmentation for PreviewRefreshMode.UIEdit and PlanMutation. A changed plan refreshes the UI and queues RenderOnly before any preview publication. RenderOnly reads the committed plan without reconciliation. PreviewRenderingService owns scene construction and its cache, not plan state. PlanSynchronizationWallSetupProjection projects the Layer selector items from the accepted plan. PreviewRefreshCoordinator keeps monotonic request, completion and success sequences.
