The work returns a PreviewUpdateOutcome: only Applied advances success; Blocked completes without success; Deferred completes without success and queues one RenderOnly successor, which readiness waits for. A disabled preview, a rejected UI synchronization, a missing plan and a canceled or failed build cannot satisfy readiness. A rejected UI dispatch fails that sequence and keeps any newer request for dispatch. Publication: The presenter acknowledges a scene only after the viewport applied the scene, the emphasis or reset, and the selection highlight. A missing subscriber, an unavailable presenter or a contained rendering failure returns Blocked; a failure clears the scene cache so a later refresh can retry. When the presenter attaches after the view entered 3D mode, it invalidates the last publication key and requests one render-only refresh. A reused view model therefore delivers its cached scene again to the new presenter. App records a scene cache key only after publication succeeds. A matching cache hit can satisfy readiness without another publication; a cached but unpublished scene forces a new build. Clearing the cache and a failed publication invalidate the key. Analysis switches to elevation only after preview readiness succeeds. Features/Preview owns preview state, projection, rendering, editing workflows and refresh scheduling and coalescing (PreviewRefreshCoordinator). App runs the refresh: SgtWindowViewModel.UpdatePreviewAsync synchronizes every pane through PlanSynchronizationCoordinator inside the window's analysis lifetime. App also owns PreviewPresenterBehavior, because it routes into the girt and opening grids through WindowSessionSurfaceCoordinator. The Func<PreviewRefreshMode, int, Task<PreviewUpdateOutcome>> that App passes to PreviewRefreshCoordinator injects work into the scheduler. Viewport and input: The stable SGT preview input behavior owns the raw 2D canvas and the zoom and reset buttons; the payload keeps elevation, section, snapping, handle editing and context-menu decisions. Unwiring releases the stable behaviors before the presenter and scene adapter retire. The 3D viewport installs at ContextIdle after Loaded, so the shell paints first. Entering 3D restores the home camera; scene updates keep a user-adjusted camera. The raw preview has the role palette legend, a DirectX failure panel and a Sandbox fallback panel. Unavailable status shows only in 3D mode. Each raw fragment resolves static theme resources through one dispatcher-owned SgtThemeResourceExtension. Grids and flyouts Opening parent-row edits are a DataGrid transaction. SgtDataGridRowEditGateBehavior defers row completion at Send priority while the payload validates and commits or cancels the Opening edit. Add Opening uses the parent-edit helper after the view loads; the same helper saves and restores named Opening column widths around UI-state persistence. The gate aborts pending dispatcher completions before release; the window owns deferred parent-edit and width-restore callbacks through the session, and stale rows are ignored after a replacement or retirement. Completion requires a canonical GUID opening key and valid geometry, also when every framing role is off. Invalid input keeps the row in edit mode and does not raise ParentRowCommitted. SgtWindowInteractionBehavior (Presentation) caches the two DataGrids and flyout roots after the view loads. Its logical and visual traversal skips duplicate nodes and walks ContentElement parents, including PopupRoot to Popup for dropdown scrollbars. Bulk and segment flyout positioning keeps its Render and ContextIdle operations in the releasable behavior, clamps open cards after a window resize and resets the segment card to its 680-pixel default before population. Drag, resize and zero-distance behavior are kept. ComboBox, text, button, toggle and DataGrid input never dismisses by click-away; outside dismissal requires an active bulk edit. The modal scrim is the element named FlyoutModalScrim. The root PreviewMouseDown tunnel dismisses an active bulk edit when the source is outside the bulk card and the excluded controls. The scrim's MouseLeftButtonDown then closes the segment flyout if it is open, otherwise the bulk flyout, and marks the event handled only when it closed one. A right click can take the tunnel path but does not run the scrim handler. The scrim covers the whole client area, including the 16-DIP band outside the main content grid; the floating cards keep their inset. On native non-client mouse-down messages (title bar, resize frame, system areas) the shell dismisses only an open segment flyout. Bulk edit and its flyout stay, so dragging the window keeps the bulk selection. The behavior attaches a session-owned HwndSourceHook, leaves the message unhandled and detaches with the window, so move, resize, system menu and close stay native. The behavior handles the Girt Flip-cell gesture at the root before DataGrid selection runs. Left-click checkbox toggling and row selection are kept, including Shift bypass, Ctrl toggle and deselecting a selected row. Segment expander double-clicks do not activate bulk rows. The opening segment TreeView uses SgtTreeViewSelectedItemBehavior. It forwards only the TreeView's own SelectedItemChanged value, so input in an embedded ComboBox or editor cannot change the selection. It is retired with the shell. The Sandbox sample implements the same interaction surface, so sample rows and flyout drag and resize use the shared behavior. Openings, Orientation, WallAnalysis and BulkEdit Opening keys are canonical GUID-N strings and stay the same when the source changes. OpeningLiveReference and WallTargetReference carry owning-document UniqueIds and, where needed, the UniqueId of the host link instance. OpeningRuntimeIdIndex assigns ordinal IDs 1..n per projection; it never derives them from key bits or element IDs. Opening rows store along-wall start and end distances in feet. OpeningGeometryResolver derives the normalized frame from those distances and the current wall length, so a manual opening does not stretch with the wall. A local geometry edit converts a Live opening to Manual and keeps its live reference and source name. Held and Unframed rows are read-only and show (awaiting review) or (not framed). Only Unframed removes an opening from girt boundaries and opening members; an opening with all roles off still splits girts. OpeningRoleRules.ApplySeedDefaultsForEnabledRoles is the shared seeding rule: a geometry change removes roles that no longer apply, seeds roles that now apply and keeps applicable overrides and user-disabled roles. GeometryFingerprint.Compare owns the wall and opening change tolerances (0.01 ft and 1 inch), including type, layer material and function, frame, reflection and framing-mode changes. Live geometry takes material names from the owning document; WallGeometryContext stores no wall identity. Openings owns Revit opening queries, editable-row mutation, synchronization and projection, and the opening pane view models. Opening identities, ranges, contracts and feet geometry are in Domain/Openings, beside EditableOpeningRow. Opening bounds accept only complete, finite source candidates. Complete cut-face bounds replace every fallback. Otherwise solid bounds seed the result, the width replaces the solid's horizontal bounds before the profile union, and the vertical order of precedence is profile, parameters, solid. Missing geometry, solids, cut generators or profile loops fall through to the next source; traversal, symbol-geometry, triangulation, transform and non-finite-vertex faults keep their original exception and stack. If any supported insert exhausts every source, the query returns one typed OpeningQuery/Incomplete failure and no partial list. Wall-context failures stay typed, and opening-row recovery matches the code UI/PlanMissing, not message text. Orientation: Orientation/Revit/Analysis owns the family-orientation analyzer and solver inputs; Orientation/Analysis has the portable rotation math and solver results; shared orientation values are in Domain/Orientation. WallAnalysis owns the plan-builder contract and Revit geometry extraction, calibration, profile warming, seeding and plan construction under WallAnalysis/{Domain,Revit/{Geometry,Planning}}. WallContextResolver accepts only a closed WallTarget and produces a ResolvedWallContext, the only host or link input to WallGeometryBuilder. Calibration checks cancellation before argument validation and cache access. Argument defects throw; typed SpecFailureException failures become calibration results; only successes are cached. Family calibration runs per family: it logs a failed family and continues, and each type of that family then carries the typed failure, with family and type names, as a per-role orientation failure. The orientation analyzer throws SpecFailureException for expected family incompatibilities, and WallAnalysisFramingTypeAnalyzer converts them per role. Host and linked frame construction share one typed frame-failure boundary in WallGeometryBuilder. Cancellation, rollback failures and invariant defects propagate. When every profile fails, ProfileLoopsAllFailed keeps up to five type IDs and their causes in numeric order and reports how many it omitted. Per-type logs and partial-success warnings stay available. New and edit analysis both pass PlanAdmissionValidator before they return success. Edit analysis keeps the stored configuration and analyzes the current geometry of the selected wall. PlanSeedingStep is the only initial seeding owner. App reports the projected girt and opening counts without adding rows or writing UI values into the plan. A non-foundation plan keeps the no-openings notice. BulkEdit owns the bulk-edit flyout, centered on BulkEditFlyoutViewModel. A failed apply tries to restore every captured girt and opening-role snapshot in request order, then propagates the apply failure followed by every restoration failure. Placement owns GirtTypeItem, GirtTypeCatalog and GirtPaneViewModel.GirtTypeDisplay for the girt grid. Opening, bulk and preview selectors use immutable FramingTypeOption values. The shared combo-box item style, also used by the girt grid, binds IsSelectable and shows ProfileWarningText; selection setters refuse unavailable types. Placement preflight checks opening member profiles before placement. SmartDefaultsResolver, SmartDefaultsInput, TypeDrivenDefaultsInput and FamilyResolutionInput are pure contracts. Girt and opening rows apply resolved values through their own methods; Domain never references feature view models. Features/BulkEdit owns the bulk-edit flyout, centered on BulkEditFlyoutViewModel. Bulk apply changes girt and opening rows with both reactive-sync suppressions active. After a successful commit, the girt owner refreshes the Flip capability and option lists of the selected rows while still suppressed, and clears an earlier type-change blocker only when its own row now has a valid orientation. Opening-only edits and failed applies keep that blocker. One UI-edit preview refresh then writes the committed rows to the plan. A failed apply restores its row snapshots and reports one bulk error without projecting the transient edits. Testing Projects DBTools.SGT.csproj has a desktop and a portable target. The shared portable rules select inward code by layer, turn off content identity and merging, and exclude desktop resources. Project References Content Tests/DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests.csproj portable SGT Domain and features, plan store, persistence, review workflow, preview status Tests/DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests.csproj desktop SGT WPF and session behavior Tests/DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests.csproj owning projects; stages the desktop product Revit fixtures Review cancellation and relink stay in IChangeReviewOperation; desktop lifecycle composition binds App/Views/IChangeReviewDialogHost to the dialog constructor. The presenter maps Presentation status to portable readiness values. Raw XAML and the Windows test project require WPF. Test helpers are under Tests/Support. Fixture boundaries Fixtures mirror production owners under Tests/: Each Pure fixture folder and namespace mirrors the directory of the code it tests. Test-only helpers are under Tests/Support. Fixture names name the current subject, for example OrientationConverterTests, PlanProjectionMapperTests, OpeningProjectorTests and MemberSegmentationReconcilerTests. Preview scene-key tests mirror the domain cache-key owner. DBTools.SGT.csproj has a desktop and a portable target. build/MSBuild/Portable.targets removes App, Revit, Views, DesignTime and XAML inputs from the portable target. DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests references portable SGT and covers domain and features, the plan store, persistence, the review workflow and preview status. DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests references desktop SGT for WPF and session cases, including OpeningSynchronizationControllerTests, PreviewRefreshCoordinatorTests, BulkEditFlyoutViewModelTests and OpeningMemberExtentSnapTargetResolverTests, which need no Revit host. Windows Pure WindowSessionLifecycleTests uses the real modal host and watchdog; it covers re-entry after a pick without another ContentRendered and pending picks after HideForPick (the runner re-enters after each pick, before target analysis finishes). Raw embedded XAML is a desktop resource, because the window host composes it. The presenter maps Presentation status to portable readiness values; the desktop review callback binds IChangeReviewDialogHost to the dialog constructor with its cancellation and relink port. DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests holds the [RevitLocal] fixtures and modeless Revit integration tests; real modal execution is tested in Windows Pure. Revit-hosted window tests use modeless Window.Show() with a bounded DispatcherDrain. StartupAnalysisWorkflowTests covers startup target resolution. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Views/SgtWindowHostedTests.cs builds the raw SgtWindow through ToolWindowFactory and checks the shell dimensions, root composition and the named Girt, Openings and Preview hosts before it releases the session. SgtWindowSessionTests drives the real run scope through RunWindowFlowAsync and checks transaction rollback, plan target, preview, DataContext, overlay cleanup, failure order and startup tasks without opening a modal dialog. The SGT test model, linked document and wall IDs, opening and geometry baselines, plan-build outcomes and preview projections are fixed repository data. Missing or unexpected state fails with the requested baseline, the observed result, the model path and the Revit year. Per-case rollback and cleanup of the fixture document, UIDocument and logging are part of each assertion. The launch smoke test treats startup-analysis completion, the UI-state save, preview and viewport cleanup, group rollback, window close, handler and view-model release and run-scope disposal as ordered cleanup that can fail. The active Revit document belongs to the daemon. The WPF construction smoke test releases the view model it attaches; production window and session disposal has one owner. PreviewPlacementParityTests.Persisted_system_edit_plan_preserves_configuration_and_reanalyzes_desired_geometry round-trips nested girt, left-jamb, opening-key and offset selections through the registered repository, moves the linked wall after it saves the baseline, then calls the registered edit-plan builder. It requires the live wall elevation to differ from storage and checks that the edit plan uses the current geometry and keeps the stored configuration. The transaction group rolls back the storage write and the link move afterward. Run the tests: ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope local -y <year> Revit-hosted submissions normally omit --machine; the daemon selects an eligible worker. --machine forces a worker for diagnosis. See Test Pipeline. Placement and review fixtures Revit-hosted fixtures use the local scope: Contract Test Place creates members, tags and storage WallSystemWriterTests.PlaceAsync_RealProjection_PersistsTagsCountsAndProgressInOneTransaction Delete System removes owned members and storage and keeps a copied foreign tag PreviewPlacementParityTests.DeleteSystem_DeletesStorageAndPlacedElements Deconstruct removes SGT associations and keeps the framing PreviewPlacementParityTests.DeconstructSystem_DeletesStorageAndTags_PreservesPlacedElements Update keeps held opening members and does not adopt a copied identity WallSystemWriter.Updates_HeldOpeningLeavesFramingUntouchedAndNeverAdoptsCopiedIdentity Update keeps matches and deletes unmatched tagged instances WallSystemWriter.Updates_UpdateAsync_PreservesMatchesAndDeletesUnmatchedTaggedInstance A persisted configuration is reloaded and the current wall geometry is analyzed again PreviewPlacementParityTests.Persisted_system_edit_plan_preserves_configuration_and_reanalyzes_desired_geometry Purge keeps the current system and member tags inside the session group WallSystemWriterTests.PurgeUnsupportedAsync_preserves_persisted_v2_system_and_member_tags_inside_the_session_group Removing an opening re-anchors girt ends, and placement matches the preview PreviewPlacementParityTests.Removing_an_opening_reanchors_girt_ends_and_placement_matches_preview The review ledger and an inner Update commit or roll back with session OK or Cancel SgtWindowSessionTests.Real_change_review_confirm_and_inner_update_follow_session_close The Confirm test replaces only the child dialog; the workflow, repository, analysis, placement executor, elements, tags and session group are real. It writes the ledger from Confirm and runs a physical Update before it requests Cancel or OK. See Limitations for the manual Undo check. Input fixtures Pure and Revit-hosted flyout fixtures supply a complete ISgtWindowDragInput (coordinates, capture owner, capture and release), because raising routed mouse events does not take native mouse capture and Revit-hosted jobs run on a hidden desktop that receives no input. SgtWindowDragInput delegates to WPF in production. The Revit-hosted preview gesture test uses the same interface through PreviewPresenterBehavior.SetDragInputSource; the presenter keeps that source across disable and enable. The tests assert capture through the supplied input and keep the production handler, cursor, selection, rendering and zoom assertions. Revit-hosted input tests use layout hit testing and directly raised routed events: the Flip-cell test raises the preview tunnel on the realized grid, the scrim test raises the preview and left-button routes from the same hit, and the Ctrl test sets and restores the thread's keyboard state without injecting input. Limitations Domain storage accepts only format version 3 and does not migrate other formats. Girt endpoint anchors accept only wall, grid, and opening-edge anchors; MemberEdge is reserved for opening-member segments. Zee and Angle types are unavailable for opening roles. The Revit API does not expose the Undo stack. Check the single Super Girt Tool Undo entry in Revit after a successful close.

developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.title: Super Girt Tool (SGT) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.summary: Super Girt Tool (SGT) Overview Super Girt Tool (SGT) analyzes one wall, edits girts and opening members in a modal window with 2D and 3D previews, and places tagged structural framing. It supports new systems and contextual editing of stored systems. The SGT specification defines the data and execution contract. This page is the developer overview. The user guide describes window controls and user procedures. Architecture Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.SGT. manifest.yml registers SgtToolModule and SgtCommand under DBTools.SGT.App.Composition. Owner Responsibility App Composition, startup, modal sessions, UI-to-plan synchronization, window hosting, and cosmetic UI persistence Domain Plan, plan store, baseline snapshots, geometry, member rules, and plan editing Features/BulkEdit Bulk row editing Features/ChangeReview Live comparison, decisions, relink pairing, and review dialog Features/Openings Opening queries, mutation, synchronization, and row UI Features/Orientation Family orientation analysis and portable solver math Features/Placement Readiness, projection, model writes, update, and removal Features/Preview Projection, rendering, editing, hit testing, snapping, and refresh scheduling Features/WallAnalysis Wall geometry, calibration, profile warming, and plan construction Persistence Storage mapper, schema, repository contract, and Revit implementation Revit Cross-feature Revit adapters Domain is independent of App, Features, Persistence, and WPF. Features do not depend on App; App composes their ports. Presentation owns stable WPF controls and the 3D viewport. The payload embeds raw XAML; ToolWindowFactory supplies its modal shell. Sandbox uses the same raw fragments and composition callback. See the specification's owner tree, composition, and application boundary for source locations and lifetime owners. Data and contracts PlanStore owns detached accepted plans. UI edits pass through PlanSynchronizationCoordinator; preview and placement consume the same resolved member contracts. PreviewRefreshMode.UIEdit synchronizes UI values before reconciliation, PlanMutation reconciles the plan, and RenderOnly renders accepted state. Stored systems contain Placed geometry and element identities, baseline settings, and a decision ledger. ISystemRepository provides per-system Save, Load, Exists, Delete, ledger-save, and purge operations. SettingsData.PlacementMode stores the framing mode. The specification defines resolved geometry, storage, and plan admission and synchronization. Workflows Launch a new system with a concrete wall target, or edit a stored system with its SystemId. Analyze the wall, calibrate eligible framing families, warm profiles, and build an admitted plan. Edit girt and opening rows or preview handles. Invalid fields block synchronization and placement. Use Change Review to compare the accepted configuration with live geometry. Confirm publishes the analyzed candidate and saves its decision ledger; Place or Update writes framing. Finish the session. A successful close assimilates its Super Girt Tool transaction group; Cancel, errors, failed close, and forced retirement roll it back. Target re-pick hides and reopens the same modal session within one synchronous Revit command frame. Cosmetic UI-state writes run separately from model finalization. See window session and feature workflows. Testing Tests mirror production owners under Tests/; shared fixture support lives in Tests/Support. Project Execution boundary DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests Portable domain, plan store, persistence, review, and preview logic DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests Windows Pure WPF and modal-session behavior DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests Revit-hosted tests (the local scope), model writes, and Revit integration The specification owns the fixture inventory and commands, including physical placement and review fixtures and hidden-desktop input adapters. Limitations SGT requires a document that is not modifiable at launch and an inline Revit call gate for its modal session. Stored formats other than version 3 are purged within the session group. See the specification limitations for member-role restrictions and the manual Undo check.

developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | DB Tools
developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting This page lists common build, runtime and tool errors, and how to read the DB Tools logs. For a reported failure, read the logs in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ first. Build Choosing a build command Build one project or test project with plain MSBuild: dotnet build path/to/project.csproj -c Release This computes content versions, restores only the selected year and stages the project's runtime inputs. It does not validate or publish a distribution. ./build.sh BuildAll builds, validates and publishes the complete distribution for every supported year, including the Dev Mode preflight and manifest checks. BuildAll compiles no tests; use ./build.sh BuildTests or a selected-test target. See Build Pipeline. Python 3.10 or later is required Python 3.10 or later is required. Install it with: sudo apt-get install python3 On Linux and WSL, build/DotNet/sdk.sh uses Python to verify and install the pinned SDK when the private SDK root is incomplete; test.sh also uses it for test discovery. Install Python and rerun the command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3 bash build/DotNet/sdk.sh On Windows, build.ps1 installs and verifies the SDK without Python. DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package missing or mismatched BuildAll requires the DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package version pinned in build/Distribution/protocol-package-lock.json, with the SHA-256 recorded there. The Validation Runner loads the package after the build tasks verify it. If the package is missing or its bytes differ from the lock, obtain the pinned package and update the lock. sourceKind is github-release for a published release, or local-candidate for an approved local candidate with its candidate-<version> tag, daemon commit, and copies of the bundle README and SHA256SUMS. Do not point the build at a daemon checkout or bypass the check. BuildAll does not need the daemon CLI or an installed Revit. The DIST suite and Revit-hosted tests use the daemon CLI. Dev Mode preflight fails ValidateDistributionCandidate runs the Dev Mode policy on each year and prints: Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<x> Both years must pass. A CollectibleThreadStatic warning counts as a failure. A failed policy, boundary, graph, identity or candidate-byte check needs a source fix and a new build. HandyControl output missing A missing vendor import, resource or DBTools.HandyControl output means the vendor/HandyControl submodule is not initialized. build.sh and build.ps1 initialize it automatically, which requires a Git checkout and network access: git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/HandyControl ./build.sh BuildAll The output is .artifacts/vendor/<Configuration>/handycontrol/net10.0-windows/DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Unsupported Revit year The supported desktop years are Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; the distribution and reference metadata use the year keys 2026 and 2027. A build or candidate for any other year is rejected; there is no fallback framework. Revit backup files in test models Revit writes backup copies (*.0001.rvt, *.00001.rvt) when it saves a model. Under testing/RevitTestModels/ these files are ignored by Git. The build does not delete them; remove them by hand when you no longer need them. Runtime Tool assembly fails to load InvalidOperationException: Failed to load tool assembly 'DBTools.GM' from the declared Tools path '<path>' in ALC rooted at 'DBTools'. Related errors from ToolAssemblyResolver: Tool assembly '<name>' was not found at the declared Tools path '<path>'. Tool assembly path '<path>' declares simple name '<x>', expected '<name>'. Tool assembly '<name>' is already loaded from '<path>', but the declared Tools path is '<path>'. App loads each tool from Tools/<name>.dll beside DBTools.dll. Check that the year directory has the complete product tree (see Assembly Loading Contract) and that the manifest's assembly name matches the file. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll. "Assembly already loaded" during Dev Mode reload Revit shows a popup about an assembly that is already loaded during or after BuildAll, while the dbtools-daemon Dev Mode driver watches the distribution. Causes: The driver watches the multi-year root .artifacts/dist/Release instead of one year directory. A reload starts while promotion replaces the files. DB Tools code loaded or resolved a DBTools.* assembly or type outside the driver's collectible AssemblyLoadContext (for example through an AppDomain-wide scan or Assembly.Load), so the context cannot unload. Point the driver directly at one year directory, .artifacts/dist/Release/2026 or .artifacts/dist/Release/2027, never at a copy, and publish with ./build.sh BuildAll. Promotion keeps each unchanged file as the same file (a hard link), so Windows Defender does not scan it again. A copied directory is a set of new files that Defender scans again, which can add tens of seconds to each Dev Mode inspection. Theme validation Startup validates the theme with ThemeValidator.ValidateOrThrow; a failure stops startup. In a Revit-hosted test run, read the daemon job's startup failure output instead of waiting for a dialog. Theme dictionary merge failed InvalidOperationException: Theme dictionary merge failed at '/DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Brushes.xaml'. A resource dictionary did not load: a missing assembly reference, a broken StaticResource chain or invalid XAML. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll and check that the year directory contains DBTools.Presentation.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll from the same build. Theme resource freeze failed InvalidOperationException: Theme resource freeze failed for key '<key>' in '<source>'. A Freezable resource (brush, geometry) cannot be frozen, usually because it has a binding or a dynamic reference. Make its values static. Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch: expected 9 dictionaries but found 8 in '<root>'. InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch at index <i>: expected '<uri>' but found '<uri>'. Resources/Theme.xaml must merge these dictionaries in this order: HandyControl Themes/SkinDark.xaml, HandyControl Themes/Theme.xaml, then Tokens.xaml, Brushes.xaml, Converters.xaml, Controls.xaml, DataGrid.xaml, Menus.xaml and Components.xaml. See Theme System. Revit API context errors ContextUnavailableException: No UIApplication in current gate scope. InvalidOperationException: ActiveUIDocument is null. Code used the Revit API outside a valid API context, for example from a modeless window without the call gate, after the document closed, or during shutdown. Run Revit API work through IRevitCallGate.RunAsync, check that a document is open, and handle cancellation when a document closes. WPF Dispatcher errors InvalidOperationException: No WPF Dispatcher is available (Application.Current is null and no Revit window dispatcher could be resolved). InvalidOperationException: WPF Dispatcher is shutting down. UI work ran during early startup or late shutdown, when no dispatcher is available. Check for a dispatcher and for Dispatcher.HasShutdownStarted before UI work, and use BeginInvoke where the caller need not wait. Unhandled UI exception from a window command A WPF command that calls ISafeExecutor.RunAsync and lets the exception propagate into an AsyncRelayCommand raises a Dispatcher unhandled exception, which the Dev Mode driver host can also show. In window commands, use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync: it logs and notifies but does not rethrow. Use RunAsync where the caller must receive the exception. XamlParseException on a read-only binding System.Windows.Markup.XamlParseException: A TwoWay or OneWayToSource binding cannot work on the read-only property '<name>' ... Run.Text binds TwoWay by default. Binding it to a get-only property fails when the window loads. Set Mode=OneWay (or OneTime for an immutable value), or bind a TextBlock.Text instead. Contextual ribbon layout changes A contextual ribbon injector that modifies Revit's contextual tabs eagerly (for example the Multi-Select tab) or inserts at index 0 shifts the native buttons. Inject only when the selection contains matching elements, append panels and buttons with Add, and remove them when the selection no longer matches. Core's ContextualRibbonInjector follows these rules. Other startup and manifest errors Message Cause AppRuntime not initialized. Code ran before App startup completed or after shutdown Manifest '<id>' is missing required 'panel' field. (and other missing required messages) Invalid manifest.yml Tool module type '<type>' not found in assembly '<assembly>'. The manifest module type or assembly name is wrong Tools Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) TransferException carries a TransferErrorCode: Code Meaning Action DestinationTypeMissing The destination has no matching drafting view type Create the view type in the destination SourceTypeNameUnavailable The source view type name cannot be read Check that the source is a valid drafting view CreateViewFailed The destination view could not be created Check write access and view limits CopyElementsFailed The view elements could not be copied Check the elements and the target view OverridesFailed The view overrides could not be copied Some overrides cannot be transferred View Template Comparer (VTC): raw XAML resource not found System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Embedded tool XAML resource 'DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml' was not found. The VTC alert body templates are an EmbeddedResource with the logical name DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml, read with ToolWindowXaml.ReadEmbeddedResource. Check the item and its LogicalName in DBTools.VTC.csproj. The shared VTC dictionaries are in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC. Logs Log files Logs are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. File names use Eastern time: dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>.log dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>-manual-<ManualTimestamp>.log The second form is written after Start New Log File in the logger window. Example: dbtools-2026-ABC123-20260124-143022345-a1b2c3d4.log. Startup cleans up old files: at most 50 files across all instances, at most 14 days old, and at most 100 MB in total while more than one file remains (the newest file is kept even if it alone is larger). Failures that occur before logging starts are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log. Debug mode Debug mode lowers the minimum log level from Information to Debug, shows the logger window and flushes the log buffer every 120 ms instead of 600 ms. It is off at every startup and is not saved. It turns on when: you enable it in the Settings window or open the logger window; an Error-level entry is logged and the logger window can be shown. An error logged before the Revit main window exists opens the window once deferred startup can show it. Closing the logger window turns debug mode off. Logger window The title is DB Tools Log - Revit <Year> [<InstanceId>]. The window is a modeless utility window. The logger host applies pin mode changes centrally: a change that keeps the owner mode only updates Topmost, and a change of owner mode closes and recreates the window. Code must not change the owner of the live window directly. The window provides: level filters for INFO, WARN, ERROR and DEBUG, and a text search; Copy All and Export, which save every retained entry in arrival order regardless of the filters. Export writes DBToolsLog_<yyyyMMdd_hhmmss><AM|PM>.txt; auto-scroll, which follows new entries. Scrolling up pauses it until you scroll back to the bottom or until a new entry arrives after 15 s idle; turning it off keeps it off; Start New Log File (in the danger menu), which starts a new file, clears the window and logs a confirmation with the same instance ID. If closing the previous file fails, the new file stays active and a warning is logged. Correlation IDs and execution phases ISafeExecutor gives every operation a GUID correlation ID and logs its phases: [Start] GM Apply starting (CorrelationId=...) [Complete] GM Apply completed in 1234ms (CorrelationId=...) Phase Level Meaning [Start] Information The operation started [Complete] Information The operation finished [Cancel] Warning The operation was canceled [Error] Error The operation failed Search for the correlation ID to find every entry of one operation and its duration. Reporting a problem Include: the log file from %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, or a logger window export; the Revit version (year and build number); the DB Tools version; the correlation ID of the failed operation; the steps to reproduce; a screenshot of any error dialog.

index.html.title: DB Tools documentation | DB Tools
index.html.summary: DB Tools documentation DB Tools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027, mainly for structural engineering workflows. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and installs for the current user. Sections Section Audience Contents User guide Revit users Installation, getting started and one page per tool. Developer guide Contributors Architecture, creating a new tool and troubleshooting. API reference Contributors Reference generated from the XML documentation comments. Tools Tool Purpose Global Mapper Bulk replacement of families, types, styles and materials; duplicate detection; shared parameters. Super Girt Tool Girt, header, sill and jamb placement on walls. Combined Foundation Tags Data and positions for combined pier and footing tags. Transfer Drafting Views Copy of drafting views between a project and a library. View Template Comparer Comparison and merge of view templates. The user guide lists all tools. Requirements Item Requirement Revit Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) or Revit 2027, desktop Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user. The installer needs no administrator rights. Architecture DBTools.dll is the Revit entry point. It loads DBTools.Core (shared infrastructure and the tool registry), DBTools.Presentation (WPF resources and controls) and one assembly per tool from the Tools folder. The architecture overview describes the layers. Source: https://github.com/kirsch33/dbtools. Report problems on the issue tracker.

user-guide/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | DB Tools
user-guide/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started This page describes the DB Tools ribbon, the settings window and the conventions shared by all tools. For installation, see Installation. The ribbon DB Tools adds the DB Tools tab to the Revit ribbon. The tab has these panels: Panel Contents DB Tools Settings Settings DB Tools Common Global Mapper, Transfer Drafting Views (Export To Library and Import From Library), Align Elevation Tags DB Tools Structural Super Girt Tool, Combined Foundation Tags (Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags) and Organize Foundation Types in one split button, Analytical Snap To Level, Allow Join and Disallow Join in one split button, Update Joist Girder Weights DB Tools Testing View Template Comparer, Record Set, Extreme Roof Framing The pages of this guide refer to a panel by its last word, for example DB Tools > Common. The Testing panel holds tools that are still under development. A panel is hidden when its group is turned off in the settings. A tool whose prerequisites are not met is disabled, and a settings warning explains why (see Warnings). Settings Click Settings to open the settings window. It opens without a model. The General section has these options: Option Default Effect Enable Common Tools On Shows or hides the Common panel. Enable Structural Tools On Shows or hides the Structural panel. Enable Testing Tools On Shows or hides the Testing panel. Enable Services On Shows or hides background services in the ribbon. Enable Debug Mode Off Writes verbose logs and opens the logger window. Below General, each tool that has options contributes a settings pack: Elevation Tags, Combined Foundation Tags, Joist Girder Weights, Library Files (Transfer Drafting Views) and others. Each pack has a Reset button. Button Effect Validate Checks the settings and refreshes the warnings. Save Settings Saves all changes and closes the window. Reset All > Reset All Settings Resets every setting. Settings are stored per user and per Revit year in %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json. Several tools have an Auto-Update Enabled option. It makes the tool run when a view is activated. It does not update DB Tools itself. Warnings A tool can raise a settings warning when a prerequisite is missing, for example Combined Foundation Tags Disabled or Library Paths Invalid. The warning disables the commands that depend on the prerequisite. The settings pack of the tool shows a card with a fix action, or states what to correct. Logs and debug mode DB Tools writes a log file for each Revit session to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, named dbtools-<year>-...log. With Enable Debug Mode on, the logger window opens after a tool runs. The window can search and filter entries, copy them, and export them. Conventions A failure while a tool changes the model rolls back the run and leaves the model unchanged, except where a tool page says otherwise. Tools report their result in a banner at the screen corner or in a dialog. A banner closes by itself after a few seconds, except where a tool page says otherwise. A completed run is normally one undo entry. Press Ctrl+Z to undo it. Each tool page states exceptions. Tools that match elements by name take .NET regular expressions in their settings. Next Open the page of the tool you need. See the User guide for the list.

user-guide/index.html.title: User guide | DB Tools
user-guide/index.html.summary: User guide DB Tools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. This guide describes how to install the add-in and how to use each tool. Installation: requirements, installing, uninstalling, files and troubleshooting. Getting started: the ribbon, the settings window, logs and shared conventions. Tools Common Tool Purpose Global Mapper Replaces families, types, styles and materials in bulk, finds duplicates, and adds shared parameters. Transfer Drafting Views Copies drafting views between the open project and a library project. Elevation Tags Aligns the labels of spot elevation tags in plan views. Structural Tool Purpose Super Girt Tool Places and manages wall girts, headers, sills and jambs. Combined Foundation Tags Updates the data of combined pier and footing tags and moves the tags to footing corners. Organize Foundation Types Renames foundation types by their dimensions, assigns type marks and merges duplicates. Analytical Snap To Level Moves analytical beam and column end points to a level. Allow Join and Disallow Join Allow or disallow joins at the ends of structural framing. Joist Girder Weights Estimates joist girder weight and writes it to the Wt parameter. Testing Tool Purpose View Template Comparer Compares two view templates and merges selected settings. Record Set Packages Revit host models together with their linked files. Extreme Roof Framing Tool Adjusts structural columns and beams to sloped roofs and floors. The Testing tools are under development. Help Each tool page lists the tool's limitations and the messages it shows. For a failure, read the newest log in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. See Getting started. To build or extend DB Tools, see the Developer guide.

user-guide/installation.html.title: Installation | DB Tools
user-guide/installation.html.summary: Installation DB Tools is a Revit add-in for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027 on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. The installer runs under a standard user account and needs no administrator rights. Requirements Item Requirement Revit 2026.5 or later, or 2027 (desktop) Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user Installing Download DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe from the GitHub releases page, or from the location your administrator provides. Close all running Revit sessions. Run the installer. On the Revit page, select the Revit years to install for. The installer checks %ProgramW6432%\Autodesk\Revit <year>\RevitAPI.dll. It enables only the years it detects, and it selects them by default. At least one year has to be selected. If DBTools.bundle is already installed, the installer asks An existing DBTools.bundle was found. Overwrite?. Answer Yes to replace it. Answer No to cancel the installation. Wait for the installer to finish. The installation log is shown on the progress page and on the finish page. The button Open install folder opens %APPDATA%\DBTools. Start Revit. The DB Tools tab appears on the ribbon. What the installer does The installer copies the release into a staging folder next to the active bundle, checks that the required files exist for each selected year, and rewrites PackageContents.xml so that the bundle registers only the selected years. It then renames the current bundle to a backup, moves the staging folder into place, and deletes the backup. If any of these steps fails, the installer restores the previous bundle and reports the error. Installing replaces the entire bundle. A new install removes the previous version folder and any other file in the old bundle. There is no in-app updater. To update, run the installer of the new release. Files and folders Path Contents %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\ The add-in, loaded by Revit as an Autodesk application plugin bundle. Contents\DBTools\<version>\<year>\ holds DBTools.addin, DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll, DBTools.Presentation.dll, DBTools.HandyControl.dll and the Tools\ folder with one DBTools.<Tool>.dll per tool. %APPDATA%\DBTools\ The installer's data folder: the uninstaller, the icon and Families\ (Revit families that the tools use). %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json User settings, one file per Revit year. %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ Log files, named dbtools-<year>-...log. %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\ Tool caches, for example VTC\ (saved templates) and TDV\ (temporary library copies). Each tool stores its own data under %APPDATA%\DBTools\ as its page describes. Uninstalling Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, select DB Tools, and select Uninstall. The uninstaller deletes DBTools.bundle together with its .staging and .backup folders, and the Families folder. The uninstaller keeps your settings, logs and caches in %APPDATA%\DBTools\. To remove all DB Tools data, delete that folder. Silent installation The installer is an Inno Setup program and accepts the standard Inno Setup switches, for example: DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART A silent installation installs for every detected Revit year. With /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES, the overwrite question takes its default answer, Yes. The installer has no switch for choosing Revit years or the install folder. Troubleshooting The DB Tools tab does not appear Close Revit and make sure %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\PackageContents.xml exists and lists your Revit year. Start Revit. Open the newest file in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ and search for ERROR or FATAL. If startup fails before logging starts, %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log holds the failure. Reinstall DB Tools. DB Tools theme failed to load Revit shows this message when startup cannot load the DB Tools theme. The message is followed by the failure details. Check that the year folder in the bundle holds DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll, DBTools.Presentation.dll, DBTools.HandyControl.dll and the Tools\ folder. If any file is missing, close Revit and reinstall DB Tools. The installer reports an error The installer reports Could not activate the staged DBTools bundle or a similar message when it cannot rename the bundle folder. Close Revit, close any program that holds a file in the bundle folder, and run the installer again. Antivirus software that locks files in %APPDATA% can cause this error. Revit years A Revit year that is not installed cannot be selected. To add a year later, install Revit for that year and run the installer again.

user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.summary: Analytical Snap To Level Analytical Snap To Level moves the end points of the selected analytical beams and columns to the elevation of a level you choose. It edits the analytical model only. The physical elements do not change. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Analytical Snap To Level. The button is enabled when at least one element is selected. Elements that are not supported analytical members are skipped and reported (see Result). Usage Select analytical members. Select the analytical members themselves, not the physical elements they represent. Click Analytical Snap To Level. In the Select Target Level dialog, select one level and confirm. Closing the dialog without a selection cancels the command with the message No target level selected. Read the Snap to Level Complete dialog. The level list is sorted by elevation, lowest first. Each entry reads <name> (Elev: <value>), where the value is the level elevation in feet with two decimals. The project has to contain at least one level. Snapping rules A member is snapped only when all of these hold: it is an analytical member (the Analytical Member category); its structural role is Beam or Column; its curve is a straight line. Role Rule Beam Both end points move to the level elevation. The member becomes horizontal. Its plan position is unchanged. Column Only the end point closer to the level elevation moves to it. The start point moves when both ends are equally close. The other end stays fixed. X and Y coordinates of every end point are unchanged. Result The whole run is one undo entry named DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level. If an unexpected error occurs, the run is rolled back and no member changes. The completion dialog shows the number of elements processed and skipped. Below that, it lists one line per skip reason with the count. Skip reason Meaning not an analytical member The element is not an analytical member (a physical element, an analytical wall or floor). Only the count is shown. role not supported The structural role is not Beam or Column (for example girder or brace). not straight The curve is not a line. The member is not changed. would collapse The snap would make the member shorter than Revit's short-curve tolerance. For each reason other than not an analytical member, the dialog lists up to 10 element IDs and and N more for the rest. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a completed run in one step. Limitations The tool snaps to levels. It does not accept a reference plane or an arbitrary elevation. To use another elevation, create a level at it. All selected members snap to the one level you choose. To snap different floors to different levels, run the tool once per floor. Braces, walls, floors and curved members are not supported.

user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.summary: Elevation Tags Elevation Tags places the label of each matching spot elevation at a uniform position beside its leader end. The elevation text is re-measured and positioned from the tag type's font, text width and the view scale. The tool runs on demand from the ribbon and, optionally, each time you open a plan view. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Align Elevation Tags. The button is enabled when a view is active. It processes the active view only. Supported views: floor plans, structural plans (engineering plans) and ceiling plans. In any other view type the command shows the warning banner Elevation Tags supports Floor Plans, Structural Plans, and Ceiling Plans only. Active view type: <type>. and changes nothing. Usage Open a floor, structural or ceiling plan. Click Align Elevation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on, the same alignment runs each time a supported plan view becomes active. Automatic runs show no banner. Failures go to the log. What is aligned A spot elevation is processed when all of these hold: one of its names matches a tag name pattern (see Settings); it has a leader; the elevation base of its type is not Relative. For each processed spot the tool computes the label position from the leader end, then applies the per-type offsets. It moves the label only when the new X or Y position differs from the current one after rounding both to two decimals (feet). Spots that already sit at the target position are not counted as updated. For a type whose elevation base is Project Base Point, the displayed elevation is measured from the project base point when the project base point and survey point are at different positions. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Elevation Tags pack. Setting Default Description Auto-Update Enabled On Align tags when a supported plan view is activated. Tag Name Patterns (Regex) ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete\|Steel\|Wall) Label$ Up to 3 regular expressions. A spot is processed when any pattern matches any of its names. Matching is case-insensitive. Along Leader 0 Moves the label away from the leader end (positive) or toward it (negative), along the horizontal direction of the label. Perpendicular 0 Moves the label away from the leader line (positive) or toward it (negative), vertically. A spot is tested against these names: the spot name, the spot dimension type name and its family name, and the name and family name of the type's marker symbol. Because spot elevations are a system family, the patterns match the type and marker symbol names, not only loaded family names. When the pattern list is empty, the default pattern is used. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is skipped and logged. The two offsets are stored per spot elevation type. The settings pack has a type selector (previous and next buttons) and a live preview that shows the label, the tag origin and the leader end for the selected type with the current offsets. The offsets are in paper inches. The tool multiplies them by the view scale divided by 12 to get model units. Settings are stored per user and Revit year in %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json. They apply to every project. Result The command is one undo entry. The banner shows one of these messages: Message Kind Aligned N elevation tag(s). Success Aligned N elevation tag(s); M could not be updated. See the DB Tools log. Warning M elevation tag(s) could not be updated. See the DB Tools log. Warning No spot elevation tags were found in the active view. Info No spot elevation tags matched Tag Name Patterns. Check Elevation Tags settings. Info No matching elevation tags needed changes. Spot elevations without a leader are skipped. Info A failure on one tag does not stop the others. A spot whose names cannot be read counts as failed. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a manual run. Limitations Only the active view is processed. There is no multi-view command; auto-update covers each view as you open it. Linked models are not processed. Spots without a leader and spots on a Relative elevation base are skipped. The last info message does not say which of the two causes applies. The text width is measured with the Windows font engine and the tag type's font. Arial is used when the type defines no font.

user-guide/tools/erft.html.title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/erft.html.summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool The Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) adjusts structural columns and beams so their tops follow the underside of a sloped floor or roof. It changes the top offset of each column and the start and end offsets of each beam; it does not change level associations. You pick a target floor or roof and the members to adjust, check the calculated changes in a table and a 3D preview, then apply them as one undo entry. ERFT stores the result with the members, so you can edit the system later. ERFT is a Testing tool and is under development. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > Extreme Roof Framing. To edit an existing system: select its members, then Modify tab > Edit ERFT. The command needs an open document. Usage Click Extreme Roof Framing. Select the target. The banner says Select a LINKED floor or roof target (press ESC to switch to HOST target selection). Click a floor or roof in a linked model, or press Esc to pick one in the host document. At the host prompt, Esc cancels. Select the source columns and beams to adjust, then click Finish. Check the target, the tolerance, the Columns and Beams tables and the preview. Click Apply. Source members ERFT accepts members of the host document only: structural columns placed at a point; structural framing with a straight location line that is not a brace. Members whose structural material name contains the word concrete (any case) are excluded, and a banner reports how many. The selection must contain a column, or a beam that connects to a column. Otherwise the launch stops with a message (see Messages). Window Target Target: shows the selected floor or roof. Pick hides the window, lets you select another target and recalculates the plan. Tolerance The tolerance is the rounding step for offset changes. Control Values Tolerance: 1/16", 1/8", 1/4" (default), 1/2", 1", or Custom Custom field Inches, at least 0.01; an invalid value shows a message and disables Apply Nearest, Up, Down Rounding direction. Up and Down are numeric: Down makes a negative change larger. The change is rounded to a multiple of the tolerance. Nearest rounds to the closest multiple, so a change smaller than half the tolerance becomes no change. Up rounds to the next multiple above the change, and Down to the next multiple below it. With a 1/4" tolerance, a +0.01" change becomes +1/4" with Up and 0 with Down; a -0.01" change becomes 0 with Up and -1/4" with Down. A row shows No Change when its rounded change is smaller than half the tolerance. Columns and Beams Table Columns Columns ID, Type, Top Offset, Delta, Status Beams ID, Type, Start Offset, End Offset, Status The status is Pending (will change), No Change or Error. Selecting a row selects the member in the preview, and clicking a member in the preview selects its row. Esc, or a click on an empty area of a table, clears the selection; Esc does not close the window. 3D Preview The preview shows the target as a transparent surface and the members at their adjusted positions, colored by status: green for Pending, gray for No Change, red for Error. Hover a member for a tooltip. Zoom to Fit fits the scene and keeps the view angle; Home returns to the default view angle. The target cannot be selected. If the graphics device fails, the preview is turned off for that window and asks you to update the graphics driver or enable GPU acceleration, then reopen the tool. Tolerance, Apply, Cancel and Pick still work. A member type whose section profile cannot be read is left out of the preview. Commands Button Action Cancel Close without changes. Apply Write the changes. Enabled when the tolerance is valid, at least one row is Pending and no row has an error. During Apply, Cancel, closing the window and a second Apply or Pick are blocked. How the changes are calculated ERFT processes columns first, then beams in dependency order. Column: the new top is the nearest point of the target's bottom surface to the column top. The change is rounded to the tolerance and added to the top offset. Beam end at a column (within 1/2"): the end follows the column's adjusted top. Beam end on another beam (within 1/2"): the end follows the adjusted supporting beam, interpolated along its plan position. Free beam end: the end goes to the nearest point of the target's bottom surface. The bottom surface is the set of faces of the target that face downward. "Nearest point" is the closest point in 3D, not a vertical projection, so a member outside the target's outline goes to its nearest edge. If the target has no downward faces, every row shows Error. Result Apply makes one undo entry, ERFT Apply Adjustments. Press Ctrl+Z to undo it. Apply: sets the column top offsets and the beam start and end offsets of the Pending rows; tags each changed member as an ERFT member of the system; saves the system (target, tolerance, rounding and offsets) in the model. If any offset, tag or stored-data write fails, Apply changes nothing. A success alert reports the number of modified columns and beams and the unchanged count, and the window closes. A reported failure shows an Apply failed: error alert and keeps the window open. Apply with no calculated plan shows the information alert No plan to apply. and keeps the window open. An unexpected error closes the window; ERFT logs it and the command ends with an error. Editing a system Select one or more ERFT members. On the Modify tab for Structural Columns, Structural Framing or a multi-category selection, click Edit ERFT. When the selection belongs to several systems, choose one. ERFT restores the stored target, tolerance and rounding, reads the current member geometry and offsets and calculates again. Applying again starts from the current offsets; it does not add the stored changes a second time. If some stored members no longer exist, a warning reports how many, and the others are edited. If no stored member exists, or the stored data is missing or invalid, the edit stops with a message (see Messages). Messages Alerts and banners are titled with the tool name. Some messages end with a diagnostic code in the form [SpecFail/<code>] <detail>; include it when you report a problem. Message Meaning Select a LINKED floor or roof target (press ESC to switch to HOST target selection). Target selection, first step. Select a HOST floor or roof target (press ESC to cancel ERFT launch). Target selection in the host document. Select source structural columns and beams to adjust, then click Finish. Source selection. Filtered out <n> concrete element(s) based on Structural Material name match: /\bconcrete\b/. Concrete members were removed from the selection. Could not extract geometry from the selected floor/roof. The target has no usable geometry. Select another floor or roof. Could not extract geometry from the stored target floor/roof. Edit mode: the stored target was deleted or changed. One or more selected source elements could not be analyzed. ERFT only supports point-based structural columns and straight structural framing members. A selected member is not supported. Adjust the selection. Select at least one column or beams that frame to columns. The selection has only beams, and none connects to a column. Custom tolerance must be a number of inches, at least 0.01. The custom tolerance is invalid. Apply is disabled. Applied adjustments: with the counts of modified columns, modified beams and unchanged elements Apply finished. Apply failed: followed by the reason Apply changed nothing. The window stays open. No plan to apply. Apply was clicked with no calculated plan. <n> element(s) from the original adjustment were not found and will be skipped. Edit mode: some stored members no longer exist. None of the previously adjusted elements could be found in the document. Edit mode: no stored member exists. Stored tolerance value '<value>' is invalid., Could not restore the stored rounding mode '<value>'. Edit mode: the stored data is invalid. Create a new adjustment. Cannot edit the selected ERFT system because stored plan data is missing or invalid. Edit mode: the stored data cannot be read. Limitations Only host-document members can be adjusted. The target can be in the host or in a loaded linked model. Concrete members are excluded. Brace framing and curved beams are not supported. ERFT changes offsets only, never the levels of members. See the developer page and the technical specification for the geometry, rounding and storage details.

user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.title: Combined Foundation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Combined Foundation Tags prepares and positions the combined pier and footing tags (family DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag). It has two commands: Update Combined Foundation Tags computes the data that the combined tag displays and writes it to shared parameters on piers and footings. Move Combined Tags moves combined tags to a corner of the footing they tag. The tool does not place tags. Place the tags with Revit's tag commands. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button. The split button also contains Organize Foundation Types. Command Effect Update Combined Foundation Tags Writes Foundation Pier Top on piers, and Associated Pier and Associated Pier Elevation on footings, in the active view. Move Combined Tags Moves each matching tag in the active view to the corner of its footing that the tag's name specifies. Both commands are enabled when a view is active and process the active view only. Both are disabled while the shared-parameter prerequisites are not met (see Prerequisites). Prerequisites The update command needs three project parameters, bound as instance parameters and identified by GUID: Parameter Type Category Group Associated Pier Text Structural Foundations Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation Length Structural Foundations Identity Data Foundation Pier Top Length Structural Columns Constraints DB Tools checks the parameters when the active model changes and before each command. If a parameter is missing, has another GUID, has the wrong data type, is bound as a type parameter, or is bound to the wrong category, DB Tools raises the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. The warning disables Update Combined Foundation Tags, Move Combined Tags and Organize Foundation Types. To repair the parameters: Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Click Refresh to list the status of each required parameter. Click Install/Repair (or Fix on the warning card). Install/Repair needs an active Revit document. It loads the definitions from the embedded shared parameter file, binds them to the required categories as instance parameters, and clears the warning. It also resolves conflicts: it deletes parameters that have the same name with another GUID, or duplicate definitions with the same name, and reinstalls the DB Tools definitions. It keeps any other categories bound to these parameters and their values. If one of those bindings is a type parameter, Install/Repair changes it to an instance parameter and Revit drops its type values. Status values include MISSING, GUID_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_NAME, WRONG_DATA_TYPE, UNBOUND, WRONG_BINDING_TYPE and WRONG_CATEGORY. Update Combined Foundation Tags Usage Open a plan view that shows the piers and footings. Run Update Combined Foundation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the update also runs each time you activate a floor plan or ceiling plan. Automatic runs show no result banner. What it does The command considers the family instances visible in the active view. A family instance is a pier when its family name matches a pier pattern. It is a footing when its family name matches a footing pattern (see Settings). For each pier, it computes Foundation Pier Top = the Top Offset parameter (0 if absent) plus the elevation of the level in the Top Level parameter, and writes it to the pier. For each footing, it finds the pier nearest in plan (X and Y of the location points) and within 2 ft. It writes the pier's Type Mark to Associated Pier and the pier's Foundation Pier Top to Associated Pier Elevation. A footing with no pier within 2 ft gets an empty Associated Pier. A value is written only when it differs. Lengths are compared after rounding to two decimals. Revit cannot clear a length value. A footing with no pier in range keeps its previous Associated Pier Elevation and counts as skipped on every run until a pier is within 2 ft. Result The update, with its selection sets, is one undo entry. If a Revit write fails unexpectedly, the whole update is rolled back and the error is shown. A failure while creating the selection sets keeps the parameter writes and is reported. The banner reads Updated N element(s); M failed/skipped. or No elements modified. An element is counted as skipped when a pier lacks a valid Top Level, a footing or pier has no location point, a parameter is missing or read-only, or a length cannot be cleared. Outcome Banner At least one element modified Stays open. Has Select Modified, and Select Skipped when some elements were skipped. Nothing modified, some skipped Warning that closes after 10 seconds. No buttons. Nothing modified or skipped Info that closes after 6 seconds. The buttons select the elements of the run that just finished. They work only while the model that ran the update is active. Each run also creates selection sets named DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (<timestamp>) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (<timestamp>) when the respective list is not empty. The timestamp is in Eastern time. A second run in the same second adds a suffix such as (2). The model keeps the 5 most recently created sets with the prefix DB Tools - FoundationTags - . If an automatic update fails, DB Tools shows the error and stops automatic updates for that model until you close and reopen it. After Save As, or the first save of a new model, it tries once more. The commands remain available. Move Combined Tags Usage Open a plan view with combined tags. Run Move Combined Tags. What it does The command examines the independent tags in the active view. It moves a tag when: the tag tags a Structural Foundations element (in the model or in a linked model); the tag's family or type name matches a tag family pattern; and the tag's name is a corner name. The corner name is the name of the tag, or the name of its type when the tag has no name: Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right or Bottom Left (case-insensitive). The command computes the footing's bounding rectangle from its geometry in the footing's own X and Y axes. It selects the corner by the view's orientation, so Top Right is the corner at the top right of the view even in a rotated view. It sets the tag head position to that corner. The Z value of the tag head is unchanged. Linked footings are transformed into the host model's coordinates. The tag's leader is not changed. Result The banner reads Moved N; skipped M of K candidate tags. A candidate is skipped when the corner name is not valid, the tagged element is not a family instance with a location point, or it has no geometry. When no candidate exists, the banner says why: Message Cause No tags were found in the active view. No independent tags in the view. No tags in the active view are currently tagging structural foundation elements. The view's tags tag other categories. No tags matched the configured Tag Family Patterns. Check Combined Foundation Tags settings. Sample rejected tag families/types: <list> Tags tag foundations, but no tag family pattern matches. The move is one undo entry. If an unexpected Revit geometry or write error occurs, the whole move is canceled and no tag stays moved. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Setting Default Used by Auto-Update Enabled On Update (runs on floor plan and ceiling plan activation) Tag Family Patterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ Move Pier Family Patterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ Update Footing Family Patterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Update Each pattern list holds up to 3 regular expressions. Matching is case-insensitive. An empty list uses the default. An invalid expression is skipped and logged. When no valid pier or footing pattern exists, the update does nothing. When no valid tag pattern exists, the move does nothing. Limitations Both commands work on the active view only. Only family instances that are visible in the active view are updated. The nearest-pier search is 2D and has a fixed 2 ft radius. Piers and footings are recognized by family name only. Families with other names need a matching pattern. The corner a tag moves to is taken from its name. A tag with another name is skipped.

user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.title: Allow Join and Disallow Join | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.summary: Allow Join and Disallow Join The Allow Join and Disallow Join commands (the Framing Joins tool) allow or disallow joins at both ends of the selected structural framing elements. Revit joins a beam or brace to the column or framing it meets and cuts the geometry accordingly. The tool sets that behavior for many members in one operation. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the Allow Join / Disallow Join split button. Command Effect Allow Join Allows joins at both ends of each selected framing member. Disallow Join Disallows joins at both ends of each selected framing member. The top part of the split button runs the current command. The arrow lists both commands. Availability Both commands are enabled when the selection contains at least one element of the Structural Framing category. The commands are disabled when nothing is selected or when no selected element is structural framing. Usage Select the framing members. Use a selection box, Ctrl+click, or a Revit selection filter. Run Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the confirmation banner. Selected elements that are not structural framing are ignored. Only family instances of the Structural Framing category (beams, braces and joists) are changed. Columns and other categories are not. Result The command is one undo entry named DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. It sets both ends (end 0 and end 1) of each member. A banner shows Allowed joins on N element(s). or Disallowed joins on N element(s). for 6 seconds. N counts the members processed, including members that already had the requested state. If Revit rejects the change on any member, the command stops, reports Failed to apply allow join operation for element <id>. (or disallow) and changes nothing. No member keeps a partial change. The banner No elements were modified. appears when no member was processed. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a run in a single step. Limitations The command sets both ends together. To set the ends differently, use the end-join controls in Revit. Structural columns are a separate category and are not changed.

user-guide/tools/gm.html.title: Global Mapper | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper Global Mapper (GM) replaces project content in bulk. You map a source (a family, a type, a line style, an object style, a material or a parameter) to a target, review the plan, and apply every mapping in one operation. GM also finds likely duplicates, ranks replacement candidates by name and property similarity, and adds shared parameters to families and categories. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Global Mapper. GM opens as a modeless window and needs an open, active project. It works on the active document only. Linked files are not changed. Tab Purpose Duplicates Finds likely duplicate elements and lets you choose which one to keep. Families Maps families and their types, parameters, object styles and materials to other families. Line Styles Replaces line styles. Object Styles Replaces Detail Items object styles. Materials Replaces materials. Shared Parameters Adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to them. The Shared Parameters tab needs a Revit shared parameter file with at least one group. Without one, GM disables the tab and explains why. Startup waits for all category and parameter-group reads to finish. If a read fails while another is canceled, GM reports the failure. Startup clears the loading state after the reads finish. Usage Open a tab. Choose the source rows to change and the target for each. A target can be chosen by hand or by the similarity ranking. Check Apply on each mapping to include in this run. Click Review Plan. GM opens Commit Review as a modal window and shows the plan. The model is not changed until you click Apply there. Click Apply. Then choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back (see Commit Review). Save the project before a bulk change. Header controls These controls apply to the current tab. Control Effect Search: Filters rows by name. Threshold: Slider from 0 to 100%. Sets the minimum similarity for automatic target selection. Sort mode (Similarity / A-Z) Orders target lists by similarity, with colored scores, or alphabetically with no scores. One setting covers the top-level and nested target lists. Hide Unused Hides elements with no instances in the project. Hide Unscanned Hides unscanned rows. Shown on the Families and Shared Parameters tabs only. Applied Only Shows rows with Apply on, including rows linked from other tabs. Not shown on Duplicates, which has its own status filter. Inspector Pane, Preview Panel, Views Panel, SP Authoring Pane Show or hide those panes. Clear... menu Clear Saved Mappings, Clear Saved UI State, Clear Deep Scan Cache (see Saved state). Mapping Conflicts Opens the conflict list. Shown when conflicts exist. Auto-Resolve All resolves them in the order: Duplicates, Tab Defaults, Family Overrides, Manual. The status line at the bottom left shows the loading state, the number of visible rows and the number of applied and conflicting rows of the current tab. A grid shows Loading... while data loads and a No ... message when a loaded result is empty. Similarity and threshold GM scores each target against its source. Scores are colored green (high), orange (medium) or red (low). At a threshold, an unchanged row selects the highest-scoring target at or above it. If no target qualifies, the row stays empty. A manual choice is never changed by the threshold. Opening a list and closing it without picking another entry is not a manual choice. <Do Not Map> is an explicit choice. On the Duplicates tab, the threshold controls which keep-target candidates appear for each source row. Duplicates tab The tab scans automatically when you open it. It groups elements that look like duplicates by name and property similarity. Styles and materials are matched on their previews. GM does not report two styles or materials as duplicates when it cannot read their previews. Line-style detection covers the whole line-style catalog, including styles with no family usage. Detect refreshes the catalog and the Usage rows and keeps your keep targets. Usage indexing decides which keep targets every restylable curve of a source can accept. While indexing runs, rows show line-style targets pending Usage indexing. A saved keep target stays visible, and Review Plan validates the targets after indexing. Steps Scope the rows. Category limits family rows and follows the category selected elsewhere in GM. Kind filters sources: All, Families, Materials, Line Styles, Object Styles or Shared Params. The status bar filters groups by All, Open, Resolved, Excluded or Conflicts. Group nodes show resolved counts, for example Families (133) · 45 resolved. For each source row, choose the Keep Target. A target must be in the same domain and category as the source. Check Apply for the rows that are ready to commit. Click Accept Applied to stage the rows that are ready. Click Review Plan. Columns Column Description Apply Commit flag for this session. It is off when the tab opens and is never restored from saved state. Source The element to replace, with its Kind, Suggestions and Highest Score. Keep Target The one element that remains. Save Off makes the choice apply to this run only. On saves the keep target for later sessions. Status Ready, Accepted, Mapped, or blank. A row is Ready when Apply is on, the keep target is not the source itself, the row is not excluded, and it has no validation or conflict flag. Choosing the source itself as the keep target marks the row as the keeper and turns Apply off. Accept Applied stages the rows that are Ready, not every row with Apply on.
