The inspector pane shows candidate details and a Metadata section with the Source ID and instance count. Its Accept split button saves the selection. The drop-down Accept Once keeps it for this session only. For a family row, Edit Type Mapping... in the context menu sets which source types map to which keep types. Shared-parameter duplicate rows can drive the selections on the Shared Parameters tab (Map From and Apply). Keep targets, the one-time-save choice, ignored candidates and exclusions are restored with the saved state. Exclusion badges (Saved, Session, Saved (Overridden)) show the exclusion time in a tooltip when it is known. Conflicts A blocking conflict prevents Review Plan. An advisory conflict (a restored saved choice that is not applied) shows in the conflict list only. The conflict button appears when any conflict exists. If one source is accepted to more than one target, GM raises a duplicate multi-target conflict and offers one-click cleanup. Choosing Keep Manual for a duplicate-versus-manual conflict clears the duplicate row's keep and apply state, so the same conflict does not return. Families tab The tab maps families in the selected category to replacement families. A family can be replaced only by a family of the same category. Columns Column Description Expand (+) Shows the row details. Quantity Instances of the family in the project. Apply Includes the mapping. Source The family. Target The replacement family. Choose the category first, then the target. Select the target with the dropdown; entries show their similarity score. Row details Expand a row to map its parts. The detail tabs are Types, Object Styles, Materials and Parameters. Object Styles and Materials are disabled when empty. The nested target lists use the same sort mode and threshold as the parent list. When you change the parent target, nested lists refill and keep the rows you changed by hand. Types: map each source type to a target type, or select <Do Not Map>. To create a type in the target family, check Create on the type row and enter New Type Name. Created types appear after the refresh that follows a commit. Parameters: map parameter names, with example values. Instance and type parameters are separate mappings, labeled (Instance) and (Type). A parameter maps only to a target of the same scope. GM copies parameter values only through these mappings, and they run with the type replacements. A red ! badge marks a conflict, such as a duplicate target parameter or a missing type-write policy. Resolve it before Review Plan. The Parameters tab shows Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. when scanning is unavailable, and No mappable parameters detected for this family. when it finds none. Expanded rows restored from saved state refresh their Object Styles and Materials usage automatically once usage data is loaded. While a target list is open, the mouse wheel scrolls that list, not the grid behind it. Type-scope writes: if a type-scope mapping writes into a target type that already has instances, GM blocks the commit until you choose Keep target type values (skip type-scope copies) or Overwrite target type values (copy them). GM takes the decision from the model state before the replacement batch starts. Moving the target's instances away earlier in the batch does not cancel Keep target type values. When overwriting is allowed, each mapping copies the original source values, even if an earlier mapping changed that source type. Object Styles and Materials: usage found by walking one placed instance. Rows from a deep scan carry a DS badge. An instance cycler, with previous and next buttons and a zoom button, moves to the sampled instance, even when it is in another view. Badges Badge Meaning OS, MAT, OS+MAT The family Apply state is linked from the Object Styles or Materials tab. LK (OS/MAT) Marks the nested rows that currently drive that link. DS Row data came from a deep scan. A tooltip shows partial-scan warnings. A linked Apply marks the family row, but family-owned operations (type swaps, parameter maps, type creation) run only when you checked that family row yourself. A saved target that is no longer among the options is flagged as incompatible. Choose the target again. Line Styles tab The tab replaces one line style with another. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The current line style. Target The replacement. Qty The curves in this document that a commit can restyle from this style. Preview A swatch of the style. GM captures each source's curves before it applies any line-style mapping, so a swap A to B and B to A exchanges the two populations, and a chain A to B to C leaves A's curves on B and B's curves on C. The mappings commit one after another inside the single undo step of the apply. A failed mapping rolls back the whole apply. GM restyles a grouped curve only when its group, and every enclosing group, has exactly one placed instance of its group type. Curves in groups with more than one instance are not counted and not replaced, because Revit requires Edit Group mode for them. GM does not enter that mode and does not ungroup elements. Ordinary curves with the same style are counted normally. A target has to be usable by every restylable curve of the source. A saved target that is not usable stays in the saved intent, shows a warning and is left out of the plan until you choose a valid target or Do Not Map. On the Line Styles, Object Styles and Materials tabs, an unavailable saved or chosen target stays visible as a disabled entry with a reason. A refresh keeps it; choose another target to replace it. Object Styles tab The tab replaces object styles of Detail Items subcategories (styles that are not line styles). Selecting a style lists the families that use it. A preview pane shows the style. Checking Apply links the affected families on the Families tab. Unchecking it removes the link. A family keeps its Apply if you checked it or another source links it. A lock badge only tells where a mapping came from. To override a mapping that a duplicate seeded, edit its target. At commit, GM opens each affected family document and ensures the target style exists in it, creating the style when it is missing. It copies the core style appearance from the project target, rewrites the references to the source style, and reloads the family into the project. Before commit, GM leaves out a top-level mapping whose source style has no family usage and no deep-scanned family reference. A mapping found only by a deep scan is kept and appears in Commit Review. A nested mapping whose owner family no longer shows the source in the usage or deep-scan data is left out with a warning. Materials tab The tab replaces materials. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The material to replace. Target The replacement. Color Preview A swatch of the material color. Families Count Families that use the material. Families affected by a mapping are linked on the Families tab with the badge MAT or OS+MAT. In Families Using This Material, the Apply indicator shows the active link, so a linked family stays marked when a filter hides it from the Families list. At commit, GM updates material parameters in the project and in the affected family documents. When the target material is missing in a family document, GM creates it, copies its core properties and rewrites the references. It then reloads the family. A mapping whose source or target cannot be resolved in the project is ignored before commit and shown as a warning. Revit does not support formulas for parameters of the Material data type. GM migrates writable material defaults for each family type. It leaves formula-determined parameters outside the replacement. A replacement material takes over the appearance and the physical and thermal properties of the new material everywhere the old one was used. Shared Parameters tab The tab adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to shared parameters. The left panel shows a tree of curated categories (Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls, Windows), then families, then types. Category labels show counts such as Mechanical Equipment (12), and empty categories show (0) and are dimmed. The right panel shows an authoring card for each shared parameter of the selected type. Select a group in SP Group. Expand a category and a family, and select a type. The panel shows the existing parameters with sampled values, and the shared parameters of the group. For each parameter to add, check Apply and choose the binding mode. Optionally choose Map From (or enter a formula) to fill the new parameter from an existing one. Click Review Plan. Binding mode Effect Host-level Adds the parameter to the category as a project parameter. If the parameter already has a binding, GM adds the category to it, keeps its group and refuses a change between instance and type. Embed-in-family Adds the parameter inside the family document, so it travels with the family. Plan validation checks that each selected type still belongs to its family and category. It rejects a mismatched or stale selection with an error before apply. Map From writes the value that the Examples column shows: Between two parameters of the same type (Length to Length, Text to Text, Yes/No to Yes/No), the stored value is copied exactly. Into a Text parameter, GM writes the source as shown, with the document's units (300 mm, Yes, or the name of a phase or level). Into a Length, Area or other measured parameter, GM reads the source as Revit reads typed input, in the document's units. In a millimeter project, 12 is 12 mm. Text read into a Number or Integer parameter uses the decimal separator of your Windows number format and no thousands separators. With a decimal point, 1.5 is 1.5, and 1,5 or 1,500 is not written. With a decimal comma, 1,5 is 1.5, and 1.5 or 1.500 is not written. An Integer parameter takes only whole numbers, so 2.5 is not written. A value that cannot be read this way is not written. Examples are a Yes/No into a Number, 300 mm into an Integer, or a level or phase name into another element parameter. Commit Review lists the operation as Failed, with the value, the parameter and the reason, and writes none of its values. The Formula preview reads values by the same rules, including a measured value in the unit it shows. When a value cannot be read as a number, the preview shows that it is unavailable. The first visit to the tab loads the shared parameter groups and the curated categories, with a loading overlay once. Later expanding and collapsing, searching, and conflict updates do not show the overlay. The instance navigator, between SP Group and the authoring pane, steps through sampled instances. Zoom to Instance goes to an instance even when it is not in the active view. Deep scan Some family details, such as embedded parameters and nested families, need a deep scan. A deep scan opens the family document. It is always started by you; GM does not scan when you expand a row. A deep scan is needed to: unlock the expanded details of a family with no instances (Scan required); read embedded definitions, such as nested family graphs, that a placed instance does not expose. For a family with instances, the Object Styles and Materials details come from walking one placed instance, so a deep scan is usually not needed. That walk records whether a source appears directly in the root family or only inside nested family content, and planning reuses that. Action Effect Scan Family (in the expanded details) Always runs a fresh deep scan. A complete result replaces the cache entry. An incomplete result removes the previous reusable entry. Deep Scan Unscanned (top-bar icon, Families tab) Scans all unscanned families with no instances in the current category, after a confirmation, with a progress overlay. Clear Deep Scan Cache Deletes the cached results and refreshes the display before it reports success. Results are cached across sessions. At startup GM restores cached results for eligible families with no instances. The restore is strict: if the cache entry does not resolve in the current document (for example a missing or ambiguous style or material), GM logs a warning and leaves the family unscanned. No banner appears. If you clear the cache while the restore runs, the cleared families stay unscanned until you scan them again. If Revit reports an error while GM reads a family parameter, GM keeps the names it read as diagnostics and marks parameter discovery incomplete. Those names are not offered as mapping choices and are not used for duplicate scoring. GM also removes the older reusable cache entry for that family. A separate successful read of the host can still fill the mapping choices. Otherwise, scan again after you fix the reported problem. If GM cannot fully resolve nested-family or material usage during a scan, it keeps the extracted details and warnings visible as a partial result, and does not cache or restore the family as complete. Scan again after you fix the reported references. A malformed or incomplete cache entry is deleted and needs a new scan. The cache is disposable and is not migrated between formats. Saved state GM saves your mappings and window state for each project, by its file path. Each unsaved document has its own state, so unsaved documents with the same title do not share state. On reopen, saved targets are restored as suggestions. Apply is left off, so nothing is enabled for commit. Menu item (Clear...) Effect Clear Saved Mappings Removes the mapping and duplicate selections for this document. The mappings do not return from an older saved file or from an open GM window. Clear Saved UI State Removes the tab, search, filter and scroll state. The next GM window for the document starts with default state. An open window does not write its older state back when it closes. Clear Deep Scan Cache Removes deep-scan data and the DS badges. Each Clear... item asks for confirmation, and Cancel clears nothing. A completed clear shows a success banner, for example Cleared saved mappings for this document. A failed clear shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Clear Saved Mappings, and no success banner. If GM cannot write the saved mappings, it logs the failure and shows an error banner, and your mappings may not persist. If the saved-mappings file has a format that this GM version cannot read, GM shows a banner and continues without restoring it. A saved target, or a saved Shared Parameters Map From source, that no longer exists is flagged as incompatible and must be created again. A style target must belong to the scope of its source (Line Styles or Object Styles). Each of the Materials, Line Styles and Object Styles tabs lists only its own kind of element. Result Commit Review Review Plan opens Commit Review. Revit is blocked while it is open. The window shows: the planned operations, by section (Plan Overview, Planned Operations, Host Replacements, Family Changes, Nested Families, Shared Parameters, Validation Issues); sections that do not apply are hidden; after apply, Commit Results, Domain Summary (succeeded, failed and skipped counts per stage, with affected references, family and timing context) and Family Breakdown; an Operation Results table with a status for each operation (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped), its operation id, stage and timing. Failed operations are summarized per mapping rule, with the source and target display names rather than element ids. The status bar shows the apply phase before the commit and the Applied, Skipped and Failed counts after it. Right-click a report table for Copy Selected or Copy All. Copy Report copies the whole report. Failed in the rules summary counts failed mapping rules. One rule can run across many families. Use the Families line (Planned / Attempted / Failed) and the Failed Operations row, which adds up the per-family failures. Apply and keep Apply runs the plan as one operation. The changes stay provisional while Commit Review shows the results. The commit continues after a failed operation: failures are recorded and the remaining operations run. The overlay Cancel button requests cancellation at once. After the run, GM verifies that no references to a source remain. Outcome What you can do Every operation succeeded and verification found no remaining source Choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back. An operation failed, verification found a remaining source, or the apply was canceled GM rolls the attempt back. Nothing is kept. Inspect the errors and choose Retry Apply to run the reviewed plan against the current model. Succeeded with nonfatal warnings Labeled Completed with Warnings. The Operation Warnings section lists each distinct instance, parameter and reason. Review it before you keep the changes. Keep remains available when verification succeeds. Keep + Continue records the mappings and returns to GM. GM refreshes the mapped data in place and restores the expanded row context. Types created with Create appear in the refreshed rows. Deep Scan results stay for families the commit did not change. Scan a changed family again to restore its details. Keep + Close GM records the mappings and closes GM. Roll back restores the model and creates no undo entry. A kept apply is one undo entry named Global Mapper: Apply. Press Ctrl+Z to revert it. Do not leave Commit Review open after Apply. Choose Keep or Roll back first. Closing the window with the X: during apply, requests cancellation and cleanup, then closes. If the cleanup fails, the window stays open and shows the error; after apply, asks whether to keep or roll back, with Roll back as the default. After any apply, GM re-reads the affected rows and counts from the model, whether the apply was kept or rolled back. A banner reports the outcome: A successful apply shows a green banner with the Applied, Failed and Skipped counts. If the apply has operation warnings, the banner is a warning banner that ends with Operation warnings: <n>. A failed apply shows a red banner that starts with the reason, for example Apply was rolled back: 1 operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. or Apply failed; no changes were kept. Commit Review stays open. A canceled apply shows Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. If an apply seems to stall near 90%, Revit is still processing one operation. Click Cancel once and wait. GM cancels and cleans up when that operation ends. If it does not recover, report it with the newest DB Tools log. How replacement batches behave Line styles, host materials, family materials, family object styles, types, host symbols and nested-family replacements use each mapping's original source population. A swap A to B and B to A exchanges the populations. A chain A to B and B to C leaves the original A population on B and the original B population on C. References moved by an earlier mapping do not become a later mapping's source. A shared nested family can appear under several selected roots. GM combines its applicable mappings and changes each original reference once. Later family reloads keep the result. Equivalent duplicate mappings get a merged notice. Conflicting targets for the same family source need your attention. A source that is absent from a traversed family is zero work, not a failed mapping. When a family reload cannot complete, every family operation that ran in that traversal is shown as failed, including equivalent shared-family aliases. The report keeps the affected count for writes completed before the failure and shows the reason. GM rolls the whole apply back, and you can choose Retry Apply. A failed operation can report writes that succeeded before it failed. Those counts are diagnostics, and the rollback discards the writes. If one half of a swap fails, the successful half could leave both populations on one target. For that reason GM rolls back the whole apply. Unchanged shared children stay on the project version during another family's reload. Shared children that the current traversal changed are reloaded from the edited family document. The family-document counts in Commit Review include the examined root and nested family documents, including documents where a source has no references. A parent-only material mapping leaves a shared child's material defaults unchanged. Map the child itself, or include it in the traversal, to change those defaults. Messages GM reports results and problems in banners with the title Global Mapper. Message Meaning Apply completed. Applied: <n>, Failed: <n>, Skipped: <n>. Family documents attempted: <n>, family document failures: <n>. The apply finished. The banner adds Operation warnings: <n>. when operations reported warnings, and Verification warning: <text> when the reference check found a problem. Apply was rolled back: <n> operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. One or more operations failed. Inspect the errors in Commit Review and choose Retry Apply. Apply was rolled back: <reason> No changes were kept. The check after the apply found a remaining source reference. Apply failed; no changes were kept. The apply stopped with an error. Commit Review stays open. Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. You canceled the apply. Keep is unavailable: the last apply kept no changes. Retry Apply or close Commit Review. Keep was chosen after an apply that was rolled back. No conflicts to resolve. Auto-Resolve All found no conflicts. No auto-resolvable conflicts were found. The remaining conflicts need a manual choice. Queued creation of new type: '<name>'. You can rename before commit in Commit Review. A Create row was added on the Types detail tab. No unscanned (0-instance) families are eligible for deep scan. Deep Scan Unscanned has no family to scan in the current category. Deep scan cache cleared. Clear Deep Scan Cache finished. Cleared saved mappings for this document. Clear Saved Mappings finished. Cleared saved UI state. Next open will use defaults. Clear Saved UI State finished. No placed instances found to navigate to. The instance cycler has no instance to show. Saved mapping source parameter '<name>' is not available. Re-create the mapping. A saved Shared Parameters Map From source no longer exists. Configure a Revit shared parameter file that has at least one group to use this tab. The Shared Parameters tab is disabled. Set a shared parameter file in Revit. Inline texts: Deep scan to unlock details for families without instances (row tooltip): the family has no instances and no deep scan. Run Scan Family. Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. and No mappable parameters detected for this family. (Parameters detail tab). line-style targets pending Usage indexing (Duplicates row): wait until indexing ends. When an action fails unexpectedly, GM shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Duplicate Type Mapping, GM Deep Scan or GM Clear Saved Mappings, followed by the error text. The action changes nothing. Retry it, and read the DB Tools log if it fails again. If Review Plan is disabled, no mapping is applied, or a blocking conflict exists. If the target list is empty, the category has no other family. If some instances were not replaced, open the family and check that every type is mapped. Limitations GM changes the active document only. A family can only be replaced by a family of the same category. Line style and object style scopes are limited as described above: curves in multi-instance groups are not restyled, and the Object Styles tab covers Detail Items subcategories only. Commit time grows with the number of elements and families. A few dozen changes finish at once; thousands can take minutes. The progress overlay shows the state. The Shared Parameters tab lists the curated categories only: Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls and Windows.

user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.title: Joist Girder Weights | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.summary: Joist Girder Weights Joist Girder Weights estimates the weight per foot of joist girders from their span, depth, panel count and panel point load, and writes the result to the Wt parameter of each girder. The estimate is for preliminary design and takeoffs. It does not replace the manufacturer's tables. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Update Joist Girder Weights. The command processes the whole model. It does not depend on the selection or the active view. Usage Make sure each girder family provides the inputs listed under Family requirements. Click Update Joist Girder Weights. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the same update runs each time you activate a view, with no banner. Disable it in the settings if view changes are slow in a large model. Which elements are processed The tool collects the elements of the Structural Framing category whose family name matches the Family/Type Name Pattern. It matches the type name only when the family name is unavailable. Default pattern: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$. It matches G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder and Vulcraft Joist Girder. Family requirements Each parameter is read from the instance first and then from the type. Names match case-insensitively where the parameter is looked up by alias. Input Parameter names Notes Number of joists (N) Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Must be greater than 1. Length Cut Length, then Length Must be greater than 0. Depth Depth Must be greater than 0. Panel point load Parameters matched by the load patterns See Load resolution. Output Wt A writable decimal-number parameter, such as a Number parameter, on the instance or the type. Numeric inputs may be decimal-number, integer or text parameters. A text value has to parse as a number. Load resolution Load parameters are found by matching their names against the three load patterns. Matching parameters are collected from the instance and the type. Pattern Default Matches, for example Dead Load (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) Dead Load, DL Live Load (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) Live Load, LL Total Load (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) Point Load, Panel Point Load, Total Load The load is resolved as follows: A negative value in any load parameter skips the girder as invalid. More than one parameter with a value in any one group (Total, Dead or Live) skips the girder as ambiguous. This check comes first: one Total Load value plus two Dead Load values skips the girder. If exactly one Total Load parameter has a value, it is the panel point load. Otherwise, if exactly one Dead Load and exactly one Live Load parameter have values, their sum is the panel point load. Otherwise the girder is skipped. A single Total Load value takes precedence over single Dead and Live values. Load values are converted to kips. A Force parameter is converted from its stored unit. A number with no unit is taken as kips. Text values accept a number followed by an optional unit: kip, kips, k, lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds or kN (for example 10 kips, 10000 lb, 45 kN). To use other parameter names, such as localized names, change the patterns in the settings. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Joist Girder Weights pack. Setting Default Auto-Update Enabled On Family/Type Name Pattern ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)\|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ Dead Load Pattern (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) Live Load Pattern (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) Total Load Pattern (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) An empty pattern field uses the default. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is reported as a configuration error. In that case the manual command shows the error as a warning banner for 10 seconds and changes nothing. Auto-update shows the same banner and raises the tool warning Joist Girder Weights Disabled, which disables the command until you clear the warning in the settings. Calculation The estimate uses N joists (N - 1 panels), panel point load P (kips), length L and depth D, in inches: panel spacing = L / N; maximum moment from the end reaction P(N - 1)/2, less the moments of the panel loads between the support and midspan; chord force = moment / (0.95 D); required chord area = chord force / (50 ksi x 0.6); top chord weight = area x L x 0.28356 lb/in^3 x 1.06; bottom chord weight = 1.13 x top chord weight; web weight = 0.7 x top chord weight; Wt = (top + bottom + web) / (L in feet), in lb/ft. The value is written to Wt as a number, without a unit conversion. Result The manual command writes all valid girders as one undo entry named Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. A girder that fails validation is skipped, and the rest are updated. The banner shows: Candidates: <n> Updated: <n> Skipped: <n> Sample skipped element(s): - Element <id>: <reason> The sample list holds up to 5 skipped girders. The banner is a success banner when nothing was skipped, a warning when some girders were skipped, and informational when none were updated. No joist girders were found. appears when no element matches the family pattern. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a manual run. Limitations The tool writes only Wt. It changes no other parameter. The calculation uses a fixed allowable stress and fixed efficiency factors. Check the results against manufacturer data for final design. Auto-update runs on every view activation and reads every matching girder. It adds delay in models with many girders.

user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.summary: Organize Foundation Types Organize Foundation Types renames pier, footing and pile cap types by their dimensions, assigns sequential type marks, and merges types that have identical dimensions. It changes types. It does not move placed instances. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button (with Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags). The command processes the whole model. It is disabled while the Combined Foundation Tags Disabled warning is active (see Combined Foundation Tags). Usage Save the model. Run Organize Foundation Types. Answer Do you want to overwrite existing type marks? Read the Organize Foundation Types result dialog. Answer Effect Yes Regenerates the type mark of every processed type. No Keeps existing type marks. Types with an empty type mark receive a new one. Processed types The tool processes types of these families (exact names, case-sensitive): Family Category Dimension parameters Mark prefix Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Types of other families are not processed. Naming and marks Each type is renamed as <dimensions> (<mark>). Dimensions are formatted in feet and fractional inches. Family Name format Example Foundation Pier <b>x<h> (<mark>) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Foundation Pier - Round <d> DIA. (<mark>) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) Pile Cap-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 4'-0"x4'-0"x2'-0" (CAP-4.0) Types are processed in ascending order of size, and marks are assigned in that order: piers: section area b x h; round piers: diameter; footings and pile caps: width, then length, then thickness. Pier and round pier marks are P-1, P-2, ... and RP-1, RP-2, .... Footing and pile cap marks are <prefix>-<w>.<n>, where <w> is the width in whole feet (rounded down) and <n> counts from 0 within that width: F-3.0, F-3.1, CAP-4.0. Merging Types of one family with equal dimension values are duplicates. The tool keeps the first in the sort order, changes every instance of the other types to the kept type, and deletes the other types. Equality is exact on the stored values, so types that differ by a small amount are not merged. Instances stay where they are. Result The run is one undo entry. The result dialog shows the number of types renamed, duplicates merged and types skipped: Successfully organized pier and footing types. - N types renamed - N duplicates merged - N types skipped When types are skipped, the first line reads Organized pier and footing types with skipped types. and the dialog adds up to 5 lines <type id>: <reason>. A type is skipped when Revit rejects its change, for example when the new name already exists. The remaining types are still processed. If a merged type cannot be deleted, the command fails and changes nothing. Press Ctrl+Z to undo the whole run. Limitations With No, the tool does not compare new marks with preserved marks that come later in the sort order, so two types can end with the same mark. Use Yes for a consistent set. The tool changes only the type name and the Type Mark parameter, and the type of merged instances. The type mark is written only when the Type Mark parameter is a writable text parameter. Linked models are not processed. Types that Revit rejects are skipped, not retried.

user-guide/tools/recordset.html.title: Record Set | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/recordset.html.summary: Record Set Record Set packages Revit host models together with the files they reference. It copies the selected RVT host files and their file-based links (RVT, DWG and other external references) into a target folder with a fixed folder structure, optionally processes DWG Xrefs with AutoCAD Core Console, and rewrites the references in the copied RVT files so they point to the copies. Before it writes anything, Record Set shows the planned output tree and any problems. Record Set is a Testing tool and is under development. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > Record Set. The command opens the modal Record Set window. It needs an open document. Usage Click Target Folder... and choose the output folder. The folder must be inside an allowed target root (see Safety checks). Change picks another folder. Click Add Revit File... (or Add host) and pick one or more host RVT files. In the Host Models grid, set Discipline and Building for each host. Read the Preview tree and the Preview Messages. For DWG files, set the CAD handling from the DWG's context menu in the preview tree. Click Execute when the preview is current and has no blocking message. Canceling a file or folder picker changes nothing. Window Target folder Shows the selected output folder. The footer reports: Field Values Root Pending, Allowed or Blocked: whether the target is inside an allowed root Free Free space on the target drive ACAD The AutoCAD Core Console path, or Unavailable Sentinel Pending, Present or Missing: the .recordset_sentinel file in the target Host Models Column Purpose Host File File name of the host RVT (read-only) Discipline Discipline folder of the host and its links. Empty adds no folder. Building Building folder. The default - adds no folder. The Discipline and Building lists have a < Add new… > choice that asks for a new value; canceling the prompt keeps the previous value. Right-click a row and choose Remove Host to remove it. When you add hosts, Record Set reads each host's external references. A host that is already in the list, or picked twice, is skipped with a message. A host whose references cannot be read is rejected and does not appear in the grid. Record Set does not read links of linked RVT models. Preview The tree shows the proposed output folder structure. It is rebuilt automatically 350 ms after the last change to the target, hosts, metadata or CAD settings. Options menu: Item Effect Manage Disciplines... Add, rename and delete discipline names. Renames and deletes apply to the hosts and links that use them. Manage Buildings... The same for building names. Auto-discover CAD Xrefs Find the Xrefs of each DWG, and of each Xref DWG, with AutoCAD Core Console and copy them beside the DWG. See DWG files. Allow CAD repath Change each Xref path in the copied DWG files to the copy of that Xref. Needs Auto-discover CAD Xrefs. These items are disabled until a host exists. The two CAD options follow Core Console availability until you set them; your choice lasts until the window closes and is not saved. Right-click a DWG in the tree for its CAD actions: Item Effect CAD: Keep Xrefs Copy the DWG and its Xrefs (the default). Xrefs are found by discovery or by the folder heuristic; see DWG files. Discovered Xrefs in the tree have no CAD actions. CAD: Bind All Bind all Xrefs into the copied DWG with AutoCAD Core Console. Clears manually added Xrefs. Bind Type > Bind / Insert AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 or 1. Bind keeps Xref-prefixed names; Insert merges names and can produce name conflicts. Add Xref... Add a DWG Xref by hand, copied beside the DWG. Preview Messages Messages have the severity Info, Warning or Block. Any Block message disables Execute. Examples: a file excluded by the safety policy (Warning); a planned source file that does not exist (Block); a destination name collision; the second file is renamed name (2).ext, name (3).ext and so on (Warning); Auto-discover CAD Xrefs disabled. or AutoCAD Core Console not found. DWG Xrefs copied by heuristic only. (Info); each discovered Xref, with its copy and its new path, for example Xref Grid in Plan.dwg (refs\Grid.dwg): copy to STR\Linked Files\Grid.dwg, repath to .\Grid.dwg. (Info); an Xref file that was not found: Xref <name> in <dwg> not found: <stored path> (Warning); CAD: Bind All, or discovery together with repath, without Core Console (Block); CAD: Bind All for a DWG whose Xref scan failed, or that reaches an Xref that was not found or that the safety policy excludes, for example Bind All blocked for <dwg path>: Xref <name> in <drawing path> not found: <stored path> (Block); a plan larger than 80 GiB or more than 10,000 items (Block). Manage Items The Manage Disciplines and Manage Buildings dialog has Add, Rename, Delete and Close. Names are trimmed and compared without case; a duplicate is ignored on Add and rejected on Rename. Close is the default button, so Enter closes the dialog. Output structure File Destination Host {target}\{building}\{discipline}\{host}.rvt Link used by one host {target}\{building}\{discipline}\Linked Files\{name} Link used by two or more hosts {target}\Common Linked Files\{name} A - building and an empty discipline add no folder. A link counts as common when the same full path and type appear at least twice, also twice in one host. DWG files Keep Xrefs with discovery and Core Console: Record Set lists the Xrefs of the DWG in one Core Console run, then the Xrefs of each Xref DWG in its own run, so nested Xrefs are found too. Each DWG is scanned once, also when Xrefs form a cycle. A relative Xref path is resolved from the folder of the DWG that stores it; when the stored path does not find the file, Record Set looks for the file name in that folder. Every found Xref file is copied once into the folder of the DWG copy. A name that is already used there gets name (2).dwg, name (3).dwg and so on. Allow CAD repath with discovery: at Execute, each copied DWG that has copied Xrefs is opened in Core Console. Record Set changes each of its Xref paths to the copy, as a path relative to the folder of the DWG copy (for example .\Grid.dwg), and saves the DWG. A nested Xref is changed in the copy of the DWG that references it. The run fails when the DWG does not contain a planned Xref or the stored path afterwards does not equal the planned path; the DWG copy is then not saved. An Xref that was not found, or that the safety policy excludes, is not copied, and the copied DWG keeps its stored path. A not-found Xref adds a Warning. Keep Xrefs without discovery, without Core Console or after a failed scan: Record Set copies sibling folders named xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg or cad next to the DWG. Xref paths are not changed, so references can break. A failed scan adds the Warning CAD Xref discovery failed for <name>: <error>. Using fallback. Bind All: the DWG is copied and all its Xrefs are bound into the copy. Record Set scans the Xrefs of the DWG and of each Xref DWG, also when Auto-discover CAD Xrefs and Allow CAD repath are off. The preview blocks the bind when a scan fails, or when a direct or nested Xref was not found or the safety policy excludes its file. At Execute, Record Set scans the copy and its Xref files again just before the bind, because the drawings can change after the preview; the same conditions then fail the run, and the copy is not bound. A relative Xref path does not resolve from the copy, so Record Set first points each Xref of the copy at the file that discovery found. Nested Xrefs then resolve from the source folder of their parent. No Xref files are copied. The run fails when an Xref stays unbound; the copy is then not saved. An Xref DWG that is also a linked DWG in the same output folder is copied once and keeps the CAD handling of the link. The CAD operations need the Unicode AutoLISP engine in AutoCAD (LISPSYS 1 or 2, the default). Core Console is found through the ACCORECONSOLE environment variable, then accoreconsole.exe on PATH, then AutoCAD 2026, 2025 or 2024, then DWG TrueView 2025 under C:\Program Files\Autodesk. Revit references In each copied host, Record Set rewrites the external references that point to copied files and leaves the loaded or unloaded state unchanged. A host with at least one rewritten reference is saved as transmitted. A transmitted workshared copy opens detached and cannot create new local files. Library references (for example keynote and assembly-code tables in a content library) are not copied or changed. Safety checks The safety policy is built into Record Set and cannot be changed by the user. The target folder must be inside an allowed root. The shipped root is \\fileserver\Projects. Files with the extensions .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk and .exe, and files matching *backup*.rvt, *.old and ~$*, are not copied. The target drive must keep at least 10 GiB (10,737,418,240 bytes) free after the copy. Execute checks the policy again and checks every output path, after resolving file and folder redirects, before it writes. Result Execute runs the plan in order under a progress overlay that cannot be canceled. Editing and closing the window are disabled while it runs. Record Set creates {target}\.recordset.lock (only one run per target at a time) and {target}\.recordset_sentinel. It creates folders, copies files (overwriting existing files and keeping their timestamps), runs the CAD operations and rewrites the Revit references. It writes {target}\_recordset_manifests\{run_id}.json with the run ID, plan fingerprint, target, UTC time, the summary counts and the status (ok, cancelled or failed). It removes the lock. An alert then shows Status: ok and the manifest path. A failure shows no alert and no banner: Record Set logs the error with its details and opens the logger window. With Debug Mode on, the logger window also opens when the Record Set window closes. Limitations A failed run is not rolled back: copied or rewritten files stay in the target. Read the log and the manifest before you clean the output or run again. If a run stops without removing .recordset.lock, the next run at that target fails. Delete the lock only when no run is active. There is no cancel action during Execute. The size and item limits are preview estimates, not limits on the final package size. Opt-in CAD tests require AutoCAD Core Console and cover generated drawings. Open the copied DWGs in AutoCAD and check their Xrefs before you hand over the output. Linked RVT models are not scanned for their own links. The safety policy and its allowed root are fixed in the tool. See the developer page and the technical specification for the plan format, fingerprint and audit files.

user-guide/tools/sgt.html.title: Super Girt Tool | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/sgt.html.summary: Super Girt Tool The Super Girt Tool (SGT) places horizontal girts and opening framing (headers, sills and jambs) on one wall in one operation. You configure every girt row and opening of the wall in one window, check the result in a 2D and 3D preview, and place all members together. SGT stores the configuration with the members, so you can edit, update or remove the system later. Use SGT to: add girts to a host foundation wall or a wall in a linked model; frame doors, windows and penetrations with headers, sills and jambs; keep girt spacing and alignment consistent along a wall; edit or update a girt system placed earlier. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Super Girt Tool. To edit an existing system: select one of its members, then Modify | Structural Framing > Edit SGT Wall. The button appears only when SGT members are selected. SGT supports these structural framing shapes: C and MC channels, Z shapes, angles and HSS. Girts can use any of them. Opening members (headers, sills and jambs) use channels or HSS only. Types that analysis found unusable cannot be selected. Usage Click Super Girt Tool. Select a wall in a linked model, or a host foundation wall. SGT analyzes the wall and fills the window. Check the seeded girts. SGT seeds girt rows at a spacing of at most 5'-0". Change elevations and types as needed. Configure the openings. In linked mode, SGT detects the openings. In foundation mode, click Add Opening for each opening. Turn the framing roles on or off. Check the layout in the Elevation, Section and 3D previews. Click Place. SGT computes rotation, justification and position from the selected framing types and the wall. Wall setup Control Purpose Offset Distance from the selected layer plane along the wall depth. 0 places the girt's exterior flange on the layer face; positive values move girts outward, negative values inward. Layer The wall layer plane that girts align to, for compound walls. The default is the most-exterior structural layer; without one, the thickest non-finish layer, or the thickest layer when all layers are finishes. Ties prefer the exterior layer. The list shows the layers of the analyzed wall and follows the current plan, also when the preview cannot update. Girts Each row is one girt at one elevation. Column Purpose (chevron) Opens the segment flyout of a segmented girt Elevation Height above the plan base Girt Type Structural framing family and type, for example C Shapes : C10X15.3 Rotation Cross-section rotation: 0°, 90°, 180° or 270° Y Justification Lateral justification: Left, Center, Right or Origin. The Revit Y offset stays zero. Z Justification Vertical justification: Top, Middle, Bottom or Origin. The Revit Z offset stays zero. Flip Revit Flip Facing. Available only when the type supports facing flips, as found during analysis. To add a girt, type an elevation in the field next to Add Girt and click Add Girt. The row context menu has Move Up, Move Down, Add Row Below, Duplicate Selected and Delete Selected. Select several rows to edit them together. A girt is split at each opening it crosses, unless it bypasses the opening. A girt split in this way shows a chevron in the first column. Click it to open the segment flyout, where you edit Type, Rotation, Y, Z and Flip of each segment, or delete a segment. The selected segment is highlighted in the preview. The flyout opens to the right of the chevron, centered vertically in the window; resizing widens mainly the Type field. The background is dimmed lightly, so the preview stays visible. When opening edits merge the segments back into one, the chevron goes away. Rotation values: 0: default orientation (web vertical, flanges horizontal). 90: rotated 90°. 180: rotated 180° from the default. 270: rotated 270° (-90°). Channels used as horizontal girts usually use 0 or 180. Y justification sets the Revit Y Justification parameter of the member. It positions the cross section across the placement line, in the member's local Y direction; it does not move the member along the wall. Left: the left side of the cross section on the placement line. Center: the cross section centered on the placement line. Right: the right side of the cross section on the placement line. Origin: the family origin on the placement line. Z justification: Top: top of the member at the elevation. Middle: center of the member at the elevation. Bottom: bottom of the member at the elevation. Origin: the family origin. Elevations and offsets Elevation and offset fields accept: decimal feet: 7.5; feet with an apostrophe: 7'; feet and quoted inches: 7'-6", 7'-6 1/2"; quoted inches: 18", 6.5", 6 1/2". Spaces are allowed around the marks, the hyphen and the fraction slash. One leading + or - applies to the whole value, for example -6 1/2". Unit names (ft, in, metric units), localized decimal commas, exponents, signs on components, unquoted fractions and trailing text are rejected. Openings In linked mode, SGT detects the openings of the linked wall; you can also add manual openings. In host foundation mode, SGT ignores the openings of the Revit wall, and the grid contains only openings you add with Add Opening. Column Purpose Opening Name of the opening Source Live (detected) or Manual Center Along Distance along the wall from the wall start Bottom Elevation Distance from the plan base to the bottom of the opening Width, Height Rough opening size Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header, Sill Turn the framing member on or off Member Typical use Header Above most openings Sill Below windows; often off for doors at grade Left Jamb, Right Jamb Usually both on; turn one off when the opening is at a wall end The chevron of an opening row opens the segment flyout for its members: role-level Type, Rotation, Y, Z and Flip and, when a role is segmented, one child row per segment. It behaves like the girt segment flyout. Opening row edits are drafts. While you edit Center Along, Bottom Elevation, Width, Height or a role checkbox, the preview shows the last committed plan. Leave the row or press Enter to commit the row, which re-segments and refreshes the preview once. Esc cancels the draft (see Limitations). If you turn on a role and change its Type, Rotation, Y, Z or Flip before you leave the row, the commit keeps those settings. An invalid row stays in edit mode, and the last committed plan stays, until you fix the highlighted fields or cancel. When analysis of a linked wall finds no openings, SGT shows an information banner, removes stale detected rows and keeps manual openings. Saving edits together An opening commit, a segment flyout edit and a preview edit (snap, gap, delete, merge) each save your other unsaved field edits in the same step; for example, a wall offset you typed just before you clicked another opening row, or a field you changed while the 3D preview was building. While any wall setup, girt or opening field is invalid, SGT refuses such an edit and writes nothing: the opening row stays in edit with its values; the gap editor stays open with the typed gap, also when the preview redraws, until you press Enter again or Esc; a refused flyout choice shows the saved value again; your other unsaved field edits stay; the preview status shows the reason: Fix invalid fields, Fix invalid rows or Preview blocked. Deleting girt rows in the grid, also an invalid row, is never refused. The next sync renumbers the segment group of the deleted row; a group left with one row becomes a plain girt. Undo and Redo Undo and Redo apply to preview edits: drag and snap edits of girt and opening-member handles, typed gap changes, segment deletes and merges. Undo of a typed gap restores the previous override. An accepted typed gap change clears the redo history. Undo and Redo restore the whole plan, so they also replace unsaved field edits, including an invalid field. Bulk edit Double-click a row in either grid to open the Bulk Edit flyout. It is an overlay inside the SGT window, so it stays with the window when you minimize and restore it. Targets: the member roles the operation applies to (Girt, Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header, Sill). Flip: three states; the indeterminate state leaves Flip unchanged. Apply (N): applies the N selected fields (Type, Rotation, Y, Z, Flip). Ctrl+Enter applies; Esc closes. Preview The preview on the right shows what SGT will place. Mode Content Elevation Front view of girts and openings, seen from the exterior. The wall start is at the right. Section Cross-section of the wall at the section marker (see Section preview) 3D Interactive 3D view The Role Palette shows the role colors: Girt blue, Header green, Sill orange, Left Jamb purple, Right Jamb cyan. In Elevation and Section mode the legend also shows segment types. The mode selector, Zoom to fit and Reset view are at the top right of the preview. Entering 3D, and Reset view, show the exterior home camera: a three-quarter view with a slight downward pitch, also for mirrored or rotated links. Other updates keep your camera. Wheel zoom allows close inspection. Pan and orbit stop on mouse-up and when the window loses focus. Click an element in 3D to select it (gold highlight) and show a tooltip with its role and section name. A click selects on mouse-up; a drag pans. Clicking a wall layer shows layer information and keeps the selection. Clicking empty space clears the selection. When a segment is selected, the other segments of the same member are dimmed slightly and unrelated elements fully. 3D shows wall layers as faint context geometry with the selected layer emphasized, thin outlines of all detected openings and a transparent floor plane. Text, line weights and styling use a fixed visual scale; hit testing (snap thresholds, hit radii) follows the display scaling. Grid markers in Elevation are white bubbles with black labels. Elevation, Section and 3D show the same member positions, orientations and segment order that Place and Update write. Profiles in the preview come from temporary instances placed during analysis, with rotation applied first, then Flip, then justification, like placed members. On a wall that is not at a right angle to the project axes, jambs are analyzed and placed with a small rotation correction; the Rotation column still shows 0, 90, 180 or 270. Section preview The Section mode shows a cross-section of the wall at the position of the section marker. The section marker is the blue dashed vertical line on the Elevation preview. Drag it to change the cut position. The marker snaps to 6" steps along the wall. The filled triangles at its top and bottom point screen-left: the section looks along the wall toward the screen-left side of the Elevation preview (the wall end). Dragging the marker changes the view only. In the section, screen-left is the exterior face of the wall and screen-right is the interior face. Horizontal members (girts, headers, sills) are drawn from their section profiles. When the cut meets a jamb edge, the jamb is drawn as a vertical depth band over its placed height, as Revit places it. For a compound wall, the section draws each layer as a band across the wall thickness, labeled <material> - <thickness>. The layer selected in Layer is highlighted. The section shows only the members whose extent along the wall meets the clip range, like the far clip offset of a Revit section view: the range is 2'-0" long, from the section marker toward the screen-left side of the Elevation preview; the Elevation preview shows the range as a translucent blue band, bounded on the left by a dashed line; girts, headers, sills and jambs that lie fully outside the range are hidden in the section. Editing in the preview Drag handles in the Elevation preview to change girt and opening-member extents. Handles snap only to valid associations: other members, grid lines, opening edges and wall edges. There is no free position along the wall. A drag commits only when it ends within snap distance of an accepted target; until then the border and guide show the invalid state. While you drag, available targets show as dim bands and the active guide as a line: cyan when valid, red when invalid. When several handles overlap, press Tab to cycle them (Shift+Tab reverses), Enter to confirm and Esc to cancel. Openings have no drag handles; edit their geometry in the grid. Segmented opening members have handles per segment; dragging one moves that segment's extent. On a girt split by openings, only the outer endpoints (the start of the first segment and the end of the last) move the girt's extents. The other segment endpoints edit the gap at an opening edge. Each one belongs to its opening and edge, also in a mirrored or rotated link. An opening's lower edge is the edge nearer the wall start; its higher edge is nearer the wall end. A girt's start snaps to the higher edge, and its end to the lower edge, of an opening that crosses the girt. For a girt inside one opening, the start snaps to the lower edge and the end to the higher edge. Edges of an opening the girt bypasses are offered too; snapping to one clears the bypass. An edge that would leave the girt no span of at least 6" (0.5 ft) is not offered. Dragging an interior endpoint of a split girt to the opposite edge of the same opening joins the segments into one girt that bypasses the opening. Jamb, header and sill handles, and girt segment handles other than the girt's own start and end, are offered all eligible opening edges in the preview, not only those of the selected opening row. Snapping a girt endpoint to a new association clears the gap override of that endpoint and edge, so the default gap for the new association applies. Merging adjacent girt segments re-targets opening-member extents that referenced either segment to the merged segment. Right-click a segmented opening member to delete that segment. Row delete commands appear in the row menu. Deleting the last segment of a role removes the role; the opening row stays until all its roles are removed. To limit a girt to grid lines, drag its start or end handle to a grid line that crosses the wall. Drag it to the wall edge to return to the full length. Gaps and segmentation rules A girt whose start is on an opening's lower edge and whose end is on the same opening's higher edge lies inside that opening. Every other girt is split at each opening it crosses, unless it bypasses the opening. An opening splits girts even when all its framing roles are off. Girt pieces shorter than 6" (0.5 ft), for example a narrow pier between two close openings, are left out of the preview and of placement. A girt with no piece of at least 6" cannot be placed. A girt end at an opening edge gets the gap of the jamb at that edge, or 0 when there is no jamb. A girt end on a wall edge or grid line that lies exactly on the edge of an opening the girt stops at also gets that edge's jamb gap. A gap override you set replaces the default. Gap override fields reject NaN and Infinity; negative values are allowed. Invalid overrides fail plan validation before placement. When the opening or grid line a girt end was attached to is removed, or the opening no longer crosses the girt (after an opening edit or a shorter wall), SGT moves that end to the nearest opening edge at least 6" from the girt's other end, or to the wall edge, and clears that end's gap override. A gap override of the edge it moves to is kept. When two segments of one girt then overlap, SGT merges them into the first. When re-segmentation leaves fewer than two segments in a group, SGT turns the group back into one row. If a geometry-based gap cannot be computed (a missing profile or a transform failure), SGT reports an error. Reopen SGT to analyze the wall again. Commands Button Action Cancel Close without placing or updating. Undoes every change made in the window. Place Create all configured members (new system). Update Edit mode: update the existing members. Review Changes Edit mode: open Change Review. Delete System Edit mode: delete all elements tagged with the system ID, including tagged copies, and the stored system. Place and Update are disabled when there is nothing valid to place; the tooltip gives the reason. Keyboard Key Action Tab Grid: next cell. Preview: cycle overlapping handles near the cursor (Shift+Tab reverses). Enter Commit an edit. Delete Delete the selected grid rows. Esc Cancel the current edit, or close a flyout. Ctrl+Enter Apply a bulk edit. Edit an existing system Select a member of the system in Revit. When several SGT systems exist on different walls, select a member of the wall you want to edit. On the Modify | Structural Framing tab, click Edit SGT Wall. Change the configuration in the SGT window. Click Update, or Delete System to remove it. Opening rows show their source, Live or Manual. Editing the position or size of a live opening makes it Manual; its distance from the wall start stays fixed when the wall length changes. Change Review When an edited wall or opening differs from the stored observation, SGT opens Change Review before it writes the update; you can also open it with Review Changes. Each row shows the opening's source name (or Manual opening for an unnamed manual row), its source, its status and its decision. The details pane shows the effects of the selected row. Placement validation messages show the along-wall range of an opening outside the wall bounds. Decisions: Accept adopts the current live observation and applies its framing at the next Update. Keep keeps the placed or manual geometry and framing for this session. Ignore leaves the existing framing unchanged and asks again at a later review. An opening you edited in this session returns to its placed geometry and framing. A manual opening that was never placed stays unframed; choose Keep at a later review in the same session to frame it again. Update does not save an ignored manual opening that was never placed. Saved live openings that are missing from a successful observation need a decision. An incomplete observation shows the opening as Unreadable and never deletes it. Without a live observation, a row offers only Keep and Ignore. The review also lists wall and layer changes, remembered decisions, accepted removals that wait for Update, and girt ends that will be re-anchored. Same as and Pair pair a missing live opening with a current opening. Unpair restores the previous pairing and its draft row. Locate selects the source element when it exists. Relink picks a new wall for a system whose wall reference changed. SGT analyzes the selected wall and rebuilds the review draft before any decision is saved. Delete System removes the stored system and its placed members. Deconstruct removes the stored system and the SGT tags and keeps the members in the model. Confirm saves the review plan and decisions in the current session. It does not change Revit members; click Update afterward. Cancel closes the review without saving its decisions. The main window's Cancel, an error or a forced close undoes these changes, including a confirmed review. Result All changes of one SGT window session become one Super Girt Tool undo entry when the window closes successfully. Cancel, an error or a forced close undoes every change of the session. Place creates the configured members and stores the system with them. Update moves the existing members in place. If a required member cannot be matched or moved, Update stops with an error; it does not delete and recreate members. Place and Update set each girt's Start and End Extension from its end gaps (0 where there is no gap), so placed girts match the preview. They replace a family default extension, and Update replaces an extension typed on a placed SGT girt. If Update must change an extension whose parameter is missing or read-only, it fails and undoes its changes. Delete System deletes the members and the stored system. Deconstruct keeps the members as plain framing. Validation failures are reported before any change. If the stored data of a system uses a format that this SGT version cannot read, SGT removes that stored data and the SGT tags of the system when the window closes successfully. Cancel, an error or a forced close keeps them. The framing members are not deleted. Place the system again. Messages SGT shows its messages in banners titled Super Girt Tool (Change Review for the review window). An error banner starts with the action that failed and a bracketed code, in the form <action>: [<code>] <detail>, for example Member snap failed: [GirtSnap/NoUsableSpan] <detail>. Message Meaning No valid wall was selected. Pick a linked wall or a host wall. The selection is not a supported wall. No eligible structural framing families found (only C/MC channels, Z shapes, ANGLE shapes, and HSS are supported). The project has no supported framing family. Load at least one, for example C Shapes, before you start SGT. No eligible structural framing types (C/MC channel, Z, ANGLE, HSS) available to select a default girt type for <context>. SGT cannot choose a default girt type. Load a supported framing type. Prepared <n> girt rows. Detected <n> openings. Analysis finished. No openings were auto-detected. Add openings manually if needed. Analysis of a linked wall found no openings. Orientation analysis failed for some families (girts: <n> families; openings: <n> role/family groups). Affected types are marked with warning icons and may not have usable defaults. Some types cannot be oriented. Choose another type for the marked rows. Profile warmup failed for <n> family types; placement/update may fail for those types until the family geometry is fixed. The section profile of some types cannot be read. Invalid elevation: '<text>'. Use feet/inches (e.g., 2', 8" or 0.25). The Add Girt elevation cannot be read. See Elevations and offsets. Analyze the wall before adding manual openings. Add Opening was used before the wall analysis finished. Flip Facing is not supported for girt type <type>. The type does not support Flip. Re-anchored <n> girt end(s) to the nearest opening or wall edge. Girt ends moved because their opening or grid line was removed. Merged <n> overlapping girt segment(s) into their neighbors. Segments of one girt overlapped and were merged. Auto-segmentation collapsed <n> girt group(s). Segment groups with fewer than two segments became plain girts. Undo unavailable: the segment group changed after deletion. Edit history was cleared; later changes were kept. A deletion changed the segment group, so the undo history was cleared. Preview blocked: ..., Preview update failed: ... The preview cannot show the current plan. Fix the reported field, or reopen SGT. Member snap failed: ..., Segment snap failed: ..., Gap edit failed: ... A preview edit was refused. The plan is unchanged. Segment deletion failed: ..., Segment merge failed: ..., Opening segment deletion failed: ... A segment edit was refused. The plan is unchanged. Opening sync failed: ... An opening row edit cannot be applied. The plan changed during review. Review Changes again before confirming. The plan changed while Change Review was open. System deleted (<n> elements deleted) Delete System finished. System deconstructed (<n> framing elements retained) Deconstruct finished. Layout preferences were not saved. Model changes were applied. The window layout was not saved. The model changes are kept. No active document. Open a Revit document first. Edit SGT Wall was clicked without an open document. The Place and Update tooltip gives the reason when they are disabled: Run Analyze before placing, Fix enabled opening roles with missing Type, Nothing to place (no valid girts and no enabled opening roles), No eligible girt types available or No eligible opening types available. Place and Update report a failure for each girt segment that cannot be placed, with the same text for both. For example, a girt family without Start and End Extension parameters reports Writer/ExtensionParamMissing when an end gap needs them, and a missing opening framing type reports Plan/EligibleOpeningTypesMissing. A header or sill split position outside the wall makes Place or Update fail with a message that names the opening. Troubleshooting Girts are not where you expect Check Layer: girts align to the selected layer plane. Check Offset. Check Rotation and the justifications, and look at the 3D preview. The preview shows nothing Make sure at least one girt row exists with a valid type. For openings, make sure at least one role is on. Close and reopen SGT to analyze the wall again. Openings are not framed The roles were off, or the opening was not detected. Edit the system, turn on Header, Sill, Left Jamb or Right Jamb, and click Update. Members have the wrong orientation Toggle Flip for the row. Change Rotation (0, 90, 180, 270). Adjust Y Justification and Z Justification. If the preview still looks wrong after you change row settings, close and reopen SGT so the wall and openings are analyzed again before you place. Limitations SGT supports straight walls only. Girts do not follow later wall changes. Edit the system and click Update, or delete it and place it again. If you save the window (by fixing another field or making another edit) while an opening row is still in edit, the row's draft is written too. Esc then shows the old values in the row, but the plan keeps the draft, and a later refresh can show it again. A gap handle of an opening you just deleted can remain on the canvas until the preview redraws. Double-clicking it shows a Gap edit failed banner instead of a gap editor. Zee and angle shapes are for girts only, not for opening framing.

user-guide/tools/tdv.html.title: Transfer Drafting Views | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) copies drafting views between the open project and a library file. A library is a Revit project (.rvt) that holds standard drafting views. TDV imports views from a library into the open project and exports views from the open project into a library. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common. Command Effect Import From Library Copies drafting views from a library into the active project. Export To Library Copies drafting views from the active project into a library. Both commands are disabled while the Library Paths Invalid warning is active (see Library settings). Library settings TDV reads its libraries from DB Tools > Settings > Library Files. Control Effect Add Library File Adds a .rvt file as a library entry. Add Fallback Path Adds an alternate path to the selected entry. TDV uses the fallback only when the main path is not valid. Remove Selected Removes the selected entry or fallback path. Validate Libraries Checks every path. Alias Name shown in the library picker. When empty, the picker shows the file name up to the first _R. A path is valid when the file exists, has the .rvt extension, and was saved in the same Revit version as the running session. A file from another Revit version is rejected with Revit version mismatch (file: <year>, current: <year>). TDV refuses to open a library from another version, so it never upgrades a library file. A file whose saved Revit version cannot be read is invalid on its own: TDV reports Could not read the library file's Revit version metadata. Re-save the library in Revit to fix it. If a saved path is invalid, the warning Library Paths Invalid disables both commands. Correct the paths and save the settings to enable them again. Several libraries can be configured. When you run a command, you choose one library from the picker. The picker lists only valid paths. If some paths are invalid, TDV shows a banner with their number. If no library is configured, the command fails with No library files configured. Configure library paths in Settings. If every path is invalid, it fails with All configured library files are inaccessible (<n> path(s) failed validation). Check library paths in Settings. Usage Run Import From Library or Export To Library. Select a library in the picker. TDV opens it in the background; the project you started from stays active. In the Transfer Drafting Views window, check the views to transfer. Resolve name conflicts (see Conflicts). Click Transfer Selected. Read the result dialog. For an import, the source is the library and the destination is the project. For an export, the source is the project and the destination is the library. Window Control Effect View Type filter Shows only the source views of one drafting view type. All Views shows all. Search box Filters the list by view name. The x button clears it. Transfer checkbox Includes the row in the transfer. View Name Destination name. Click it to edit. The name is trimmed before use. Replace Replaces an existing destination view of the same name. View Type Destination drafting view type. The list holds the types of the destination document. The default, Retain Original, uses the source view's type. Clear Selection Unchecks all rows. Transfer Selected Starts the transfer. It is disabled when no row is checked or a checked row has a conflict. Preview Shows an image of the selected source view. Drag to pan, use the mouse wheel to zoom, and click Zoom Extents to fit it. The preview shows Preview unavailable for the selected view. when the view cannot be exported to an image. Preview updates The preview always shows the current row. When you change the selection quickly, TDV skips the older previews. Errors An expander that lists errors. The status bar shows <views> | Selected: <n> | Replace: <n> | Adds: <n>, and during a transfer the count of finished views. A status icon in front of each name shows the row state: pending, success, failure, or conflict. Success icons appear when the whole transfer is committed, not when a single view finishes. Conflicts A checked row has a conflict, and a warning bar asks you to resolve it before continuing, when: the destination name is empty; the destination already has a drafting view with that name and Replace is off; or two checked rows have the same destination name. Rename the row, or turn on Replace, to resolve it. View types With Retain Original, TDV looks for a destination drafting view type with the source type's name. When it is missing, TDV creates it by duplicating an existing drafting view type of the destination. A row shows a warning mark when the source type name cannot be read; select a type explicitly in that case. With a named type, the type must exist in the destination. TDV does not create it. What is transferred For each checked view the transfer: finds or creates the destination view: a new drafting view, or, with Replace and an existing view of that name, the existing view with its type changed and its content deleted; copies the view scale and the View Description parameter; copies the view's elements with Revit's copy mechanism, one element at a time. Groups are copied as groups. Duplicate type names resolve to the types of the destination; copies the per-element graphic overrides. Not copied: viewports, title blocks, schedules, guide grids, other views, and view templates. The transfer copies the view's type but not a view template assignment. If a family used in the view is missing in the destination, Revit copies the family with the element. A detail array arrives as its groups, without the editable array association. The transfer is processed row by row and is one undo entry named Transfer Drafting Views. A failed view is rolled back alone: nothing from that view is added, and a view you chose to replace keeps its old content. The other views still transfer. If Revit discards the whole transfer, TDV reports All attempted changes were rolled back, and no view is added. You can cancel a running transfer from the progress overlay. The views processed so far are rolled back. Result The dialog title is Transfer Completed or, if any view failed, was not attempted or the run was canceled or rolled back, Transfer Completed with Issues. Its text is: Selected <n>, Processed <n>, Added <n>, Replaced <n>, Failed <n>, Not Attempted <n> followed by (All attempted changes were rolled back) or (Cancelled by user) when that applies. A Per-View Issues table lists each failed view with the error code and reason. Copy Details copies the table to the clipboard. Error code Cause DestinationNameRequired The destination name is empty. DuplicateTargetName Two checked rows have the same destination name. DestinationNameConflict The destination view exists and Replace is off. SourceTypeNameUnavailable, DestinationTypeMissing The destination drafting view type cannot be found or created. CreateViewFailed, ClearDestinationViewFailed The destination view cannot be created, renamed or cleared. MetadataCopyFailed The scale or description cannot be set. CopyElementsFailed Revit cannot copy an element. OverridesFailed A graphic override cannot be copied. TransactionRolledBack Revit discarded the whole transfer. Click Accept and Transfer More to keep the window open, or Close Tool to close it. Import TDV closes the library without saving after the dialog closes. If it cannot close the library, a banner asks you to close it manually. Press Ctrl+Z to undo an import; the transfer is one undo entry unless Revit discarded it. Export After the window closes with at least one view added or replaced: a workshared library is synchronized with central, relinquishing all borrowed elements, with the comment DB TOOLS - ADDED [<n>] DETAILS AND REPLACED [<n>] DETAILS.; a library that is not workshared is saved in place. If the library cannot be saved, synchronized or closed, the export fails and the error report names each failure. TDV then reactivates the project you started from. An export cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z once it is saved or synchronized. If nothing was added or replaced, the library is closed without saving. Library files and worksharing For a workshared library, TDV creates a temporary local copy named <library>_<user>.rvt under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\TDV\LibraryLocals\<id>\, opens it with all worksets, and deletes the copy after it closes. A library that is not workshared is opened directly. If two users export to the same library at the same time, one synchronization can fail. Coordinate export times. To create a library, create a Revit project in the same Revit version, add the drafting view types you need, save it where your team can reach it, and add it in the settings. Limitations The library has to be saved in the Revit version that is running. Only drafting views are listed. A view with an element that Revit cannot copy fails as a whole. The names of the views and types in the destination decide conflicts; there is no rename-on-conflict option. The project and the library must be different documents.

user-guide/tools/vtc.html.title: View Template Comparer | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/vtc.html.summary: View Template Comparer View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two view templates in the open project, side by side. For each differing setting you choose which template's value to keep. VTC then writes the result to one of the templates or to a new merged template. It can also save templates to a library and load them back. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > View Template Comparer. The Testing panel is shown when Enable Testing Tools is on in the settings (the default). If the project has no view templates, the command shows No view templates found in the document. Usage Select the Left and Right templates. The Swap button exchanges them. Click a value cell in the Settings Comparison tree to choose which side wins for that row. The Inspector has Use Left, Use Right and a clear button for the selected row. For a category row, use Edit Left or Edit Right (in the Inspector, from the row, or from the context menu Edit Override...) to stage a local graphic-override edit. A staged edit is marked Edited.
